Akaun is bookkeeping software for small teams and freelancers. You install it on your own server, so your books stay with you. Each user signs in from a web browser. Akaun keeps one list of records. Each record tells where money came from and where it went. AI can read your receipts, bills and bank statements and prepare the records for you. Akaun also makes quotations and invoices, matches your accounts to bank statements, and gives standard reports. Many users can work in one book, and each user gets only the permissions that you give. This guide is for the people who keep the books. It is also for the person who installs Akaun and manages its users and settings. Read Getting started first. Then read How Akaun works before you record a lot of data. Use the other sections when you need them. The Glossary gives the meaning of each term.

Getting started: install Akaun, sign in and prepare your book. How Akaun works: the ideas behind records, accounts, contacts and balances. Everyday tasks: record expenses, income, transfers and payments. Auto Import: let AI read receipts, statements and spreadsheets. Quotations and invoices: prepare quotations and invoices for your customers. Contacts: keep a list of the people and businesses that you work with. Bank reconciliation: check each account against the statement from the bank. Dashboard and reports: see how the business is doing. Administration: manage users, permissions, settings and the safety of your data. Help: answers to common problems, and the meaning of each term.

Use this page to keep a safe copy of your book, to restore it, and to install a new version of Akaun. Make a backup on a regular schedule, and always before an upgrade. info Akaun has no backup, restore or reset button in the screens. The description of the Administrators group mentions backups and reset, but these functions do not exist at this time. You make a backup when you copy files on the server.

Akaun keeps all the data of your book in two places. Copy both of them together. The database is the file at DATABASE_PATH. The default is data/akaun.db in the folder of the code. Two more files can be next to it: akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm. The three files are one database. The storage folder is the folder at STORAGE_PATH. The default is data/storage. It holds the receipts, attachments, statements and the company logo. With Docker, both are in the data folder next to docker-compose.yml. Copy the full data folder. Also keep a copy of your settings file: docker-compose.yml for Docker, or .env for an installation from the source code. See Where your data is.

Stop Akaun before you copy the files. While Akaun runs, it can write to the database at any time. The newest changes are often only in the -wal file. A copy of akaun.db alone can lose these changes. A copy made during a write can also be damaged. If you cannot stop Akaun, copy the three database files together, at a time when nobody uses Akaun. A copy of a running database is not fully safe.

Go to the folder that contains docker-compose.yml. Stop Akaun: docker compose stop Copy the full data folder to a different disk or computer, for example: cp -a data /backup/akaun-2026-10-09 Start Akaun again: docker compose start

Stop the server. Use the service manager of your server, or press Ctrl+C in the terminal of bun server.js. Copy the database file to a different disk or computer. If akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm are next to the database file, copy them too. Copy the storage folder. From the folder of the code, start the server again with bun server.js.

documents.t: The backup has the database file and the storage folder. Keep each backup with its date in the name. Keep one or more backups on a different computer from the server. tip To test a backup, restore it on a different computer and open Akaun there. A backup that you did not test can be incomplete.

caution A restore replaces all the data of the book with the backup. The changes that users made after the backup are lost. Before you restore, copy the current data to a different folder. Stop Akaun. Move the current database files and the storage folder to a different folder. Copy the database file of the backup to the location of DATABASE_PATH. If the backup has -wal and -shm files, copy them too. Make sure that no -wal or -shm file from the current data stays next to the database. Copy the storage folder of the backup to the location of STORAGE_PATH. Start Akaun. Sign in and do the ledger integrity check. See Check the book. The book shows the data at the time of the backup. With Docker, Akaun makes the user PUID the owner of the data folder each time it starts. Restore a backup only into the version of Akaun that made it, or a newer version. An older version cannot always read a database that a newer version changed.
caution Make a backup before each upgrade. A new version can change the database, and you cannot undo this change from inside Akaun. Keep the backup until you check the book with the new version.
Make a backup. See Make a backup. Go to the folder that contains docker-compose.yml. Get the new version: docker compose pull Start the new version: docker compose up -d

Make a backup. See Make a backup. Make sure that the server is stopped. In the folder of the code, get the new code: git pull Install the packages: bun install Build the application: bun run build Start the server: bun server.js

documents.t: A new version updates the database by itself when it starts for the first time. You do not type a command. Usually Akaun changes the database in place and keeps no copy. This is why your own backup is necessary. A book from an older version, from before the standard chart of accounts, needs a larger conversion. Akaun does this conversion on a copy of the database first: If all the checks pass, Akaun puts the converted copy in place. It moves the previous files into a new folder next to the database. The name of the folder is pre-chart- with the date and time, for example data/pre-chart-2026-10-09T08-15-30.123Z. The folder holds akaun.db, and akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm if they existed. If a check fails, Akaun does not start. The server shows This installation's books could not be converted, so the server has not started. Your database has not been changed. and the reason. Akaun does not use the pre-chart- folder again. After you check the book, you can move the folder to your backup storage. If the book is very old, Akaun does not start. The server tells you which version to install first. Install that version, start it one time, and then install the new version. Akaun does not change your database in this case.

documents.t: Do this check after each upgrade and after each restore. info You need the View permission on Reports to see the Ledger tab. A superuser can see it. In the sidebar, click Settings. Click the Ledger tab. Under Ledger integrity check, click Check now. If the tab shows Migration results, read each part of it. Open the Reports screen and compare the main figures with the figures before the upgrade. If all records balance, Akaun shows The ledger is in balance. All records and the trial balance agree. See Settings reference. If Migration results says that nothing old was thrown away, the copy of your data from before the upgrade is in the pre-chart- folder next to the database. If a figure is wrong, do these steps: Stop Akaun. Restore the backup that you made before the upgrade. Install the previous version again. Report the problem. See Troubleshooting.

A backup copy holds all your financial data and the API keys of your AI providers. Keep it in a safe place. Akaun does not make backups on a schedule. Use the tools of your server, for example a cron job, to stop Akaun, copy the files and start Akaun again.

Akaun can give data to an AI assistant that supports MCP (Model Context Protocol). Then you can ask the assistant questions about your books, for example "What did we spend on shipping in September?". If you allow it, the assistant can also do work in your books, for example "Record this receipt as a software expense paid from the bank account". By default the assistant can only read. It can change data only when you give it change access.

The assistant can read these items. It reads only the areas where the user has the View permission, and where the token or the connection gives read access. What the assistant can read Permission that the user needs The list of records, with filters for dates, kinds, accounts, categories, contacts, text, amounts, paid and reconciled View on Records One record, with its lines. It can also read the settlements and the stored text of the documents. View on Records A file attached to a record: a receipt or bill as an image or a PDF, or a spreadsheet as text View on Records The statement of one account View on Records The outstanding amounts: receivables (what customers owe the business) and payables (what the business owes) View on Records The list of accounts, with their balances View on Accounts The list of contacts View on Contacts The balance of one contact View on Contacts and Records A report: Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow Statement or Partners' Equity View on Reports The list of files on Auto Import, and the items of one file View on Auto Import Invoices and quotations, with their lines View on Invoices or Quotations Bank statements, their lines, and the records that can match them View on Reconciliation and Records The history of changes to one item View on the area of the item Akaun also gives the assistant guidance for record descriptions. The assistant can use it to suggest better descriptions in a table. It changes a description only after you approve it.

The assistant can change data only if all of these are true: You gave the assistant the access. With the sign-in, you select change access when you connect. With a token, you choose the level or the ability when you make the token. See Connect with the sign-in and Connect with a personal access token. The user may hand on the permission to tokens and apps. The administrator sets this on each group, in Members may hand on to tokens & apps. See What members may hand on. The user has the permission in Akaun. The assistant can never do more than the user. Akaun checks these on each request. If the administrator removes a permission from the group, or from what the group may hand on, the assistant loses it immediately. A permission that the user has as an extra permission is never handed on to an assistant. What the assistant can do Permission that the user needs Record an expense, income or transfer. Change a record. Set an opening balance. To make a new invoice in its place, also Add on Invoices.
