With the sign-in, this is a separate choice when you connect. With a token, select Full for the area, or select Custom and switch on Delete. Then the assistant can delete records, settlements, accounts, contacts, draft invoices, quotations and import files, where the user has Delete. Setting an opening balance to zero deletes it, so that also needs Delete on Records. Skipping a file on Auto Import deletes the uploaded file, so the assistant asks you first. Some changes are only for you to make in Akaun, never for an assistant: Merge two contacts. Remove an attachment from a record. Correct or delete a line of a bank statement. These cannot be undone, or they change the evidence that the books are checked against.

A journal entry, or a record between any two accounts, needs Adjustments on Records. With the sign-in, the assistant also needs the separate Adjust choice when you connect. Change access to records does not include it. Give it only to an assistant that you trust with your books: an adjustment can change any balance and keep the ledger in balance. A bank line recorded as a transfer to anything other than a bank or cash account is an adjustment too. Akaun applies all its normal rules to the assistant. For example: A record that is paid or matched to a bank line keeps its amount and date. Its description can still change. A sent invoice keeps its amounts. The assistant must void it and make a new one. An account with records cannot be deleted. The assistant can archive it. If someone else changed an item after the assistant read it, Akaun refuses the change. The assistant must read the item again. Each change is saved at once. It shows in the history of the item under the name of the user, and on other open screens at once. The assistant asks you before it deletes or voids something. caution The assistant sends the data that it reads to the AI service of the assistant. This can include amounts, contact names, descriptions, the text of your receipts and bills, and the receipt and bill files themselves. Connect an assistant only if you agree that this service can read this data. Give the assistant only the permissions that it needs. Give change or delete access only to an assistant that you trust to act for you.

With the sign-in (OAuth), the assistant opens Akaun in a browser. You sign in and choose what the assistant can read, change and delete. Use this way when the assistant supports it. The administrator must enable it first. With a personal access token, you put a token in the settings of the assistant. Use this way when the assistant cannot use the sign-in. The token can do only what you select when you make it. See Connect with a personal access token. In both ways, the server address is the address of Akaun with /mcp at the end, for example https://books.example.com/mcp.

For the sign-in way, the administrator must change two settings on the server: Set ORIGIN to the public HTTPS address of Akaun, for example https://books.example.com. Add the setting OAUTH_ENABLED=true. Start Akaun again. See Install Akaun. ORIGIN must start with https://. Only a localhost or 127.0.0.1 address can use http://. Do not put a path after the address. If the address is not correct, Akaun does not start, and the server log tells why. An assistant that runs in the cloud must reach your server from the internet. If you use a reverse proxy, it must send the paths /mcp, /oauth/ and /.well-known/ to Akaun. For the assistant to attach the largest files, BODY_SIZE_LIMIT must be 21M or more. The Docker image already sets it.

caution The app sends its own name. Akaun does not check it. Connect only from an assistant that you started yourself. If you did not start the connection, click Cancel. In the assistant, add a new MCP server. The name of this function is different in each assistant, for example "connector" or "integration". Type the server address, for example https://books.example.com/mcp. Choose OAuth as the type of authentication. If Akaun asks you to sign in, sign in. On the Connect page, read the app name and the Client ID. Select the access that you want to give, and clear the rest. Click Allow selected access. The app shows on your profile, on the Connected apps tab. The page shows the access that the app asks for, in up to three groups: Read — Akaun selects each read permission that you can give. Change — Akaun never selects these for you. Select each area that the assistant may add to and change, for example Record and change records, payments and settlements, and attach files. Delete — Akaun never selects these for you. Select them only if the assistant must delete things. Under each choice, Includes lists the abilities that the choice gives, for example Invoices: Add, Invoices: Change, Invoices: Send, Invoices: Void. The page offers only what you may hand on to tokens and apps. You cannot select the other choices: If you do not have a permission, the page shows Your account does not have this permission. If you have a permission, but your administrator does not let you hand it on, the page shows Your administrator does not allow apps to do this. See What members may hand on. If you clear all the permissions, Akaun shows Select at least one available permission. Click Cancel to refuse the connection. Usually an app asks for read access first. When the assistant needs a tool that changes data, the app asks again, and the Connect page opens again with the new access. You can also connect the app again to give it more access. A connection stays valid for 30 days or less. Then connect the assistant again.

caution A token can do more than read. A program with the token can do all the actions that you select for the token, also changes and deletes. Select only the permissions that the assistant needs. For a read-only assistant, select View for each area that it must read, and None for the other areas. If you are a superuser, do not give the token more than the assistant needs. Open your profile, and click the Access tokens tab. Click New token, and make a token with only the permissions that the assistant needs. See Make a token. Click Copy to copy the token. It starts with akp_. In the assistant, add a new MCP server of the type "Streamable HTTP". Type the server address, for example https://books.example.com/mcp. Add the header Authorization with the value Bearer and the token, for example Bearer akp_1234…. The assistant sees only the tools that the permissions of the token allow. For example, a token with only the View level gives the assistant no tools that change data. A token stops working at the end of the day in Expires (UTC). Then the assistant cannot connect. Make a new token, and put it in the settings of the assistant. For an assistant that does not act for one person, a superuser can add a separate user with only the permissions that the assistant needs. Then the superuser signs in as that user, and makes the token on the profile of that user. A superuser cannot make a token for a different user. See Add a user and The tokens of a user.
documents.s: Connect with a personal access token

documents.t: If you connected with the sign-in, open your profile, click Connected apps, and click Revoke access for the app. See Your profile. If you connected with a token, open your profile, click Access tokens, and click Revoke for the token. See Replace or remove a token. A superuser can also revoke the tokens of each user on Users & Groups. See Revoke the tokens of a user. The assistant stops immediately. A new password also disconnects all the apps and revokes all the tokens of the user. Sign out does not disconnect them.

Akaun checks the permissions of the user on each request. If you remove a permission from the group, or from what the group may hand on, the assistant loses that ability on its next request. A superuser is also limited to the access that the superuser selected for the connection or the token. No token and no app can manage users and groups. The API tokens of older versions do not work any more. See API tokens were replaced by personal access tokens. The assistant reads the data at the time of its question. It does not get live updates. A list gives 50 rows at a time by default, and 200 rows at the most. A statement gives 500 lines or fewer. For a long period, ask about a shorter period. The assistant can read an attached file of 5 MB or less. One user can read 60 files in 10 minutes. After that, the assistant must wait. The assistant can attach a file of 15 MB or less. One user can attach 30 files in 10 minutes. The assistant cannot upload a new file to Auto Import or a new bank statement. Upload these in Akaun. Use HTTPS for a connection over the internet. A token sent over plain HTTP is not safe.
A permission lets a user do one thing in one area of Akaun. Read this page before you make a group, give a user extra permissions or make a token. To change the permissions, see Users and groups.

Each area of Akaun has a list of abilities. In Users & Groups and on the New access token page, each area shows as a row. You choose a level of access for the row, or you switch on single abilities. See Levels of access. View opens the screen of the area and shows its items. Without View, the screen does not open, and its item does not show in the sidebar. Add, Change and Delete make, change and remove the items of the area. Some areas have more abilities, for example Send and Void on Invoices. Each one lets a user do one special task. A superuser has all the abilities in all the areas. The levels and the abilities do not apply to a superuser.

The table tells what each ability lets a user do. Area Ability What the ability lets a user do Records View Open the Records list, the record pages and the account statements. Add Make a new record. Record a payment. Change Change a record. Attach a file to a record. Delete Delete a record or an attachment. Click Reverse allocation on a settlement. Adjustments Save a record that is not an everyday record. See Adjustments. Auto Import View Open Auto Import and see the import profiles. Upload Upload files. Change Correct what Akaun read from a file. Confirm Confirm or skip the items of a file. Profiles Add, change, enable, disable or delete an import profile. Delete Click Discard on a file. Click Clear history. Contacts View Open Contacts and the contact pages. Add Add a contact. Change Change a contact and its roles. Delete Delete a contact. Merge Merge two contacts into one. Quotations View Open Quotations and the quotation pages. Print a quotation. Add Make a quotation. Change Change a quotation and its status. Delete Delete a quotation. Revise Replace a sent quotation with a new revision. Convert Make an invoice from an accepted quotation. Invoices View Open Invoices and the invoice pages. Invoices are sales invoices issued to customers. Print an invoice. Add Make a draft invoice. Change Change an invoice. Delete Delete a draft invoice. Send Mark an invoice as sent. This posts the invoice to the ledger. Void Cancel a sent invoice. This reverses the posting of the invoice. Reconciliation View Open the reconciliation screen of an account. Add Upload a statement. Make a transfer from a statement line. Change Edit a statement line. Match Match statement lines to records, and remove a match. Delete Remove a statement or a statement line. Accounts View Open Accounts and the account pages. Add Add an account or a category. Change Change an account, deactivate it, or enter its opening balance. Choose the default accounts. Delete Delete an account that has no records. Reports View Open Reports. See the Ledger tab in Settings. Dashboard View Open the Dashboard. Settings View Open Settings and see the settings. Manage Change the settings. See Settings. Users & Groups Manage Open Users & Groups. See Users & Groups.

For each area, you select one level: None, View, Edit, Full or Custom. A level is a quick way to choose a set of abilities. Akaun keeps each ability on its own. A sentence under the name of the area tells what the choice allows, for example "Can see, add, change and send invoices. Cannot delete or void." None gives no ability in the area. View gives the View ability only. Edit gives View and each ability that adds or changes items. Full gives all the abilities of the area, except Adjustments. Custom shows a switch for each ability of the area, with its description. Switch on the abilities that you need. Area Edit gives Full also gives Records View, Add, Change Delete Auto Import View, Upload, Change, Confirm, Profiles Delete Contacts View, Add, Change Delete, Merge Quotations View, Add, Change, Revise, Convert Delete Invoices View, Add, Change, Send Delete, Void Reconciliation View, Add, Change, Match Delete Accounts View, Add, Change Delete Settings View, Manage no Full level Reports and Dashboard have one ability. They offer only None and View. Read these notes: A set of abilities that is not the same as a level shows as Custom. For example, the Data Entry group has Add on Records but no View. One ability never gives a different ability. Adjustments on Records is never part of a level. It always has its own switch under Records. Thus you give it only on purpose. An ability with a warning sign gives a lot of power. Examples are Adjustments on Records and Manage on Settings. Give them only on purpose. A level that includes an ability that you cannot choose is not available. Hold the pointer on it to see why.

To mark an invoice as sent, a user needs Send on Invoices and Add on Records. To cancel a sent invoice, a user needs Void on Invoices and Change on Records. To make a new invoice in its place, the user also needs Add on Invoices. To make an invoice from a quotation, a user needs Convert on Quotations and Add on Invoices. To revise a quotation, a user needs Revise and Add on Quotations. To merge two contacts, a user needs Merge, Change and Delete on Contacts. To record a statement line as a transfer, a user needs Add on Reconciliation and Add on Records. To read a file again on Auto Import, a user needs Upload and Change on Auto Import. To record a payment from an invoice page, a user needs View on Invoices and Add on Records. To confirm the items of a file on Auto Import, a user needs only Confirm on Auto Import. The user does not need a permission on Records.
documents.s: Tasks that need more than one ability

documents.t: Records is one permission area for all kinds of record. It covers expenses, income, transfers, payments, opening balances and journal entries. A user cannot have permission for expenses only.
Reports is view only. A report shows figures and never changes them. Thus Reports has only the View ability.

Adjustments is an ability in the Records area. It lets a user save a record between any two accounts. Akaun decides from the accounts if a record needs this ability. These records are everyday records, and they do not need Adjustments: An expense: debit an expense category, credit a cash or bank account. A bill to pay later: debit an expense category, credit Accounts Payable. An income: debit a cash or bank account, credit an income category. A transfer: debit one cash or bank account, credit a different cash or bank account. A payment: debit Accounts Payable and credit a cash or bank account. Or debit a cash or bank account and credit Accounts Receivable. An opening balance. A split: one cash, bank, receivable or payable account, and two or more categories of the same kind. All other records need Adjustments. Examples are a correction between two categories, a record with two cash or bank accounts and a category, and a record with partner capital. On the record form, Adjustments also gives the user a choice of all accounts. caution No group that Akaun makes gives Adjustments. No level includes Adjustments, also not Full on Records. A user with this ability can make the ledger show any figures, and the ledger is still in balance. Give it only to a person that you trust with the books. Give it on purpose, to one user, as an extra permission. See How a record moves money.

Send and Void on Invoices change the ledger: they add or remove an Invoice record. Thus each one also needs a permission on Records. See Tasks that need more than one ability. The groups that Akaun makes have permissions on Quotations and Invoices, as the table in Users and groups shows. A new group that you make has none. Choose a level for them in the group.

Settings has two abilities: View lets a user open Settings and see all the tabs. Akaun never shows the key of an AI provider. Manage lets a user change the settings. Examples are the company details, the templates of printed documents, the number format, the AI providers and Rebuild search index. A user with View and no Manage sees the settings as read only. A note at the top of the page tells the user to ask an administrator for Settings › Manage. Two parts also have a check of a different area: The Ledger tab shows only for a user with View on Reports. To choose a default account, a user needs Change on Accounts. The groups that Akaun makes have View on Settings only. Thus at the start, only a superuser can change the settings. To let a different user change them, give Manage on Settings. See Settings reference.
Users & Groups has one ability, Manage. Only a superuser group has it. You cannot give it to a different group, to one user, to a token or to an app. Thus only a superuser can open Users & Groups.

A user can let a program act for them, with a personal access token or with a connected app. See Your profile and Connect AI assistants. Each group has a second list of areas: Members may hand on to tokens & apps. It is the most that the tokens and the apps of a member can do. A token or an app can do an action only when all of these are true: The token or the app has the permission. One of the groups of the user lets the user hand it on. The user can do the action at that time. A permission that a user has as an extra permission is never handed on. See What members may hand on.
documents.s: What tokens and apps can do

documents.t: Before this version, each area had the same four actions. Akaun changed the permissions of each group at the upgrade. In the areas of the book, no user can do more or less than before. Old permission New abilities Change on Auto Import Change, Confirm and Profiles Delete on Contacts Delete and Merge Change on Quotations Change, Revise and Convert Change on Invoices Change, Send and Void Change on Reconciliation Change and Match The Adjustments area Adjustments on Records Settings is different. Before, all users could change the settings. Now each group got View on Settings, and no Manage. Thus only a superuser can change the settings until you give Manage to a group or a user. Each group can hand on to tokens and apps all the permissions that it gives, except Adjustments and the Settings abilities. All the old API tokens stopped working. See Your profile.

A change to the permissions applies on the next action of the user, and of each token and app of the user. A user who is in no group has no permissions, and extra permissions have no effect. At the next start of the server, Akaun puts that user into Administrators. See Stop the access of a user. An AI assistant that connects as a user can read only the areas that the user can view. See Connect AI assistants.

This page tells what each setting in Settings does, tab by tab. To prepare a new book in the correct order, use Prepare your book. To open the settings, click Settings in the sidebar. The tabs are General, Company, Ledger, Intelligence, Templates and Advanced. info To open Settings, you need the View permission on Settings. To change a setting, you need the Manage permission on Settings. Without Manage, Akaun shows all the tabs as read only, with a note at the top. The groups that Akaun makes give View only. Thus at the start, only a superuser can change the settings. Akaun never shows the key of an AI provider. See Permissions explained.

Each part of a tab has its own Save button. On the Ledger tab, the button is Save defaults. Click the button of the part that you changed before you go to a different part. After a save, Akaun shows Settings saved. If you have unsaved changes and you click a different tab or a different screen, Akaun shows Unsaved changes: Click Keep editing to stay and save your changes. Click Discard changes to remove your changes and continue. A reload of the page, or a closed browser tab, removes unsaved changes without a message. The Unsaved changes message also does not cover the Default accounts lists on the Ledger tab.
The General tab has two parts: Display and Numbering.

Currency: the main currency of the book. All amounts show in this currency. Akaun changes the amounts of foreign records into it. Default payment account: the account that new expenses and income use first. You can still change the account on each record. This row shows only when the book has two or more cash or bank accounts. At this time, a change in this row is not kept. To change this account, use Default transaction account on the Ledger tab. Chart of Accounts: click Open accounts → to open the Accounts screen. Click Save under these rows to save Currency. caution Currency locks when the first record, quotation or invoice exists. An opening balance is also a record. After the lock, Currency shows a lock icon and you cannot change it. See Foreign currency.

Numbering sets one number format for expenses, income, payments, quotations and invoices. Click a token, or drag it, to add it to the format: PREFIX, YYYY, YY, MM, DD and SEQ. Type other characters, for example a dash, directly in the format. The Preview line shows an example number. Click Save under Numbering. Prepare your book tells what each token means. The help text lists the codes EX, IN, CL, QT and IV, but it does not tell what CL is. CL is the code for a payment. caution The number format locks when the first record, quotation or invoice exists. After the lock, the tokens and the Save button do not show, and you cannot change the format.

Akaun shows these details on printed quotations and invoices. Logo: click Upload to add a JPEG or PNG image of 5 MB or smaller. Click Replace to use a different image, or Remove to remove it. At this time, the logo does not print on quotations or invoices. Letterhead: a JPEG or PNG image of 5 MB or smaller, usually a wide banner with your logo, name and address. It prints at the top of quotations and invoices, in place of the company name, when Header on the Templates tab is Letterhead. Upload, Replace and Remove work as for the logo. Company Name: the name of the business. Address: the address of the business. Registration No.: the registration number of the business. Click Save to save the fields.
info The Ledger tab shows only for a user with the View permission on Reports.

Akaun uses these accounts for the automatic line of some records. Each list shows only the accounts that fit the default. Default What Akaun uses it for Accounts receivable An invoice that you send, and a payment from a customer. Accounts payable The amounts that the business must pay to suppliers and other parties, for example a bill that you pay later. Opening balances The other line of each opening balance. Sales revenue An invoice that does not choose a different revenue account. Uncategorised expense An imported expense with no matching expense account. Default transaction account The account that new expenses and income use first. Default payment account on the General tab shows this account. Uncategorised income An imported income with no matching revenue account. Click Save defaults to save. Akaun shows Default accounts updated. To change a default, you need the Change permission on Accounts and the Manage permission on Settings. Without them, the lists and the button are not available. caution Do not change Accounts receivable after you send invoices. A payment from a customer then cannot settle an invoice that you sent before the change. See Prepare your book.

The check adds the lines of each record and makes sure that each record balances. It only reads the book. It changes nothing. On the Ledger tab, find Ledger integrity check. Click Check now. If all records balance, Akaun shows The ledger is in balance. All records and the trial balance agree. If a record does not balance, Akaun shows the number of unbalanced records, for example 2 unbalanced records. Each line shows the record number and the difference, for example Record #41 is out of balance by 10.00. If the totals of all accounts also do not agree, Akaun shows Trial balance difference and the amount. Report this problem. See Troubleshooting.

Migration results shows only after Akaun converted a book from an older version. It shows only when the conversion had to make decisions without you. Each part lists the records that the conversion changed, for example Uncategorised records or Files that could not be found. Check each record in the list. Akaun keeps the previous files in a pre-chart- folder next to the database. See Backups and upgrades.

The Intelligence tab controls Auto Import. It has three parts. Providers holds the AI providers that read your documents. Import profiles holds the saved ways to read one kind of document. Processing controls how Akaun processes the files. Click Save at the bottom of the tab to save the changes on this tab. Import profiles shows only for a user with the View permission on Auto Import. See Connect an AI provider and Import profiles.

The Templates tab controls printed quotations and invoices, and the terms that new ones start with. Under Printed documents: Layout: shows Standard. At this time, Akaun has one layout only, and you cannot change it. Accent color: the color of the printed documents. Choose a preset color, or choose a different color. Header: what prints at the top of the page. Company name prints the name as text. Letterhead prints the letterhead image from the Company tab in its place. The layout decides where the header goes. You can choose Letterhead only after you upload a letterhead. If you later remove the letterhead, the documents print the company name again. Under Default terms: Invoice due in (days): a new invoice is due this number of days after its issue date. Type 0 for due on receipt. Leave it empty for no due date. Quotation valid for (days): a new quotation expires this number of days after its issue date. Leave it empty for no expiry date. Type a whole number from 0 to 365. The default for each setting is 30. A change applies only to new invoices and quotations. The due date of an invoice that you make from a quotation also comes from Invoice due in (days). Click Save to save the color and the terms.

The Advanced tab has Search index. The search index is the text that the search box on each list uses. On the Advanced tab, find Rebuild search index. Click Rebuild. Akaun reads the stored files again. Then it makes the search text again for all records, quotations, invoices and contacts. The row shows the progress. At the end, it shows the number of records. Use this when the search does not find a record that it must find.
Each setting applies to the full book and to all users. Your name, your password and the order of your screens are on your profile, not in Settings. See Your profile.

Use the Users & Groups screen to add the people who work in your book. A group controls what each person can do. Do these tasks after the first sign-in, and each time a person joins or leaves. info Only a superuser can open Users & Groups. The screen needs Manage on Users & Groups, and only a superuser group has it. Akaun does not open the screen for other users. In the sidebar, the screen is under Administration.

A permission lets a user do one thing in one area, for example Add on Records. See Permissions explained. A group is a set of permissions. A user can be in more than one group. A user gets each permission that one or more of their groups gives. A group cannot remove a permission that a different group gives. A group with the Superuser switch on gives all permissions in all areas. Its members are superusers. You can give one user extra permissions. Extra permissions only add. They cannot remove a permission that a group gives. Each group also sets what its members may hand on to their tokens and apps. See What members may hand on.

Akaun makes four groups. At each start of the server, Akaun makes each of these groups again if it is missing. Administrators is a superuser group. Its members can do all actions in all areas, and they can open Users & Groups. The other three groups give these permissions: Area Bookkeeper Data Entry Reviewer Records View, Add, Change Add View Auto Import View, Upload Upload View Contacts View, Add, Change View, Add View Quotations View, Add, Change, Revise, Convert Add View Invoices View, Add, Change, Send, Void Add View Reconciliation View, Add, Change, Match none View Accounts View, Add, Change none View Reports View none View Dashboard none none none Settings View View View Users & Groups none none none Read these notes before you choose a group: No group except Administrators gives Delete, Adjustments on Records, Merge on Contacts or Manage on Settings. Bookkeeper does not have Change, Confirm or Profiles on Auto Import. Thus a Bookkeeper can upload files, but cannot confirm or skip the items. To let a Bookkeeper confirm items, give Confirm on Auto Import. Only a superuser can change the settings. To let a different user change them, give Manage on Settings. Each of the three groups lets its members hand on to tokens and apps all the permissions that the group gives, except View on Settings. A screen opens only for a user with View on its area. Data Entry has View on Contacts only. Thus a Data Entry user cannot open Records, Auto Import, Quotations or Invoices. No group except Administrators has View on Dashboard. The description of Administrators mentions backups and reset. Akaun has no backup or reset in the screens. See Backups and upgrades.

The Users tab shows one row for each user, with these columns: User: the name and the email. Groups: the groups of the user. No groups shows that the user is in no group. Access: Superuser, Standard or No access. Tokens: the number of active personal access tokens of the user, for example 2 active, or None. Created: the date when the user was added.

Email, Username and Temporary password are necessary. Each user must have a different email and a different username. caution Select one or more groups for each user. At each start of the server, Akaun puts each user with no group into Administrators. That user then becomes a superuser. In the sidebar, click Users & Groups. On the Users tab, click Add user. In Full name, type the name of the person. In Email, type the email address. In Username, type the name that the person types to sign in. In Temporary password, type a password for the first sign-in. Under Group membership, select one or more groups. If the person needs more permissions than the groups give, choose them under Extra permissions. See Give a user extra permissions. Click Create user. Akaun shows User created, and the user shows in the list. Give the username and the temporary password to the person. Tell the person to change the password on the Security tab of the profile. See Your profile.

caution Do not change the username of the admin user. At each start, Akaun looks for a user with the username admin. If it finds none, it adds a new admin user with the password akaun-admin. This new user is a superuser, and anyone who knows the default password can sign in. On the Users tab, click the row of the user. If necessary, change Full name, Email or Username. If the user needs a new password, type it in Reset password. Under Group membership, select or clear the groups. Keep one or more groups selected. Click Save changes. Akaun shows User saved. If Reset password is empty, the password does not change. A new password also disconnects all the connected apps of the user, and revokes all the tokens of the user.

Use extra permissions when one person needs one more ability than their groups give. On the Users tab, click the row of the user. Under Extra permissions, find the area. Select a higher level for the area, or select Custom and switch on the ability that the user needs. See Choose the permissions. Click Save changes. Extra permissions already shows what the groups of the user give: An ability that a group gives is on and shows From a group. You cannot switch it off there. To remove it, change the groups of the user. A level that is lower than what the groups give is not available. Hold the pointer on it to see A group already grants more than this. Extra permissions work only when the user is in one or more groups. The Extra permissions section does not show for a superuser, because a superuser has all permissions. Extra permissions are never handed on. The tokens and the connected apps of the user cannot use them.

A personal access token lets a program connect to Akaun as a user. Only the user can make a token, signed in as themselves, on the profile. See Your profile. You cannot make a token for a different user. You can see and revoke the tokens of a user. On the Users tab, click the row of the user. Look under Personal access tokens. Each row shows the name, the last four characters, what the token can do in each area, the expiry date and the date of the last use. If the user has no tokens, the section shows No access tokens yet. The Tokens column of the list shows the number of active tokens of the user. For a program that does not act for one person, for example a shared AI assistant, add a separate user with only the permissions that the program needs. Then sign in as that user, and make the token on the profile of that user. See Add a user and Make a token.

caution A program that uses a revoked token cannot connect any more. You cannot undo this. On the Users tab, click the row of the user. Under Personal access tokens, find the token. Click Revoke. In the message, click Revoke. To revoke all the tokens of the user, click Revoke all N tokens under the list, and then click Revoke all in the message. The link shows when the user has two or more tokens. The token buttons act immediately. You do not need Save changes for them. A new password in Reset password also revokes all the tokens and the connected apps of the user.
documents.s: Revoke the tokens of a user

documents.t: caution Do not leave a user in no group. The panel says that such a user sees an empty app. This is true only until the next start of the server. At each start, Akaun puts each user with no group into Administrators. That user then becomes a superuser. To stop the access of a user safely, put the user in a group with no permissions: On the Groups tab, make a new group with no permissions, for example No access. See Make a group. On the Users tab, click the row of the user. Under Group membership, clear all the groups. Select the No access group. Under Extra permissions, select None for each area. In Reset password, type a new password that the person does not know. Click Save changes. Under Personal access tokens, make sure that no token shows. If a token shows, click Revoke all N tokens or Revoke. See Revoke the tokens of a user. The Access column shows Standard. The user cannot sign in with the old password. The new password revokes all the tokens and disconnects all the connected apps of the user. If the user is still signed in, the user cannot open the screens of the book. The records of the user stay in the book.
documents.s: Stop the access of a user

documents.t: caution You cannot undo the removal of a user. Do not remove the admin user: at the next start, Akaun adds a new admin user with the password akaun-admin. If the user made records or other items, Akaun can refuse the removal and show Failed to delete user. Then use Stop the access of a user instead. On the Users tab, click the row of the user. Click Remove. In the message of the browser, click OK. Akaun shows User removed, and the row goes from the list. You cannot remove yourself. If you try, Akaun shows Cannot delete your own account.
The Groups tab shows the list of groups on the left. Each item shows the number of members and the number of permissions. Click a group to see its details on the right.

On the Groups tab, click New group. Akaun adds a group with the name New group and opens it. At the top of the group, type a name for the group. In the description box, type what the group is for. Under Members can, choose a level for each area that the group gives. See Choose the permissions. Under Members may hand on to tokens & apps, choose what the tokens and the apps of the members can do. See What members may hand on. Click Save changes. Akaun shows Group saved. Save changes and Reset show only when the group has unsaved changes. Reset removes your changes.

Members can, Members may hand on to tokens & apps and Extra permissions use the same editor. It shows one row for each area, for example Records or Invoices. Each row has a level picker with None, View, Edit, Full and Custom. A sentence under the name of the area tells what the choice allows, for example "Can see, add, change and send invoices. Cannot delete or void." View gives the View ability only. Edit gives View and each ability that adds or changes items. For example, on Invoices it gives View, Add, Change and Send. Full gives all the abilities of the area, also Delete, except Adjustments. Custom shows a switch for each ability of the area, with a description. Use it to give one ability. See Levels of access for the abilities in each level. An area with one ability, for example Reports or Dashboard, offers only None and View. A set of abilities that is not the same as a level shows as Custom. For example, Data Entry has Add on Records but no View. Adjustments on Records is never part of a level. It has its own switch under Records, so you give it only on purpose. A warning sign shows an ability that gives a lot of power, for example Adjustments on Records and Manage on Settings. A level that includes an ability that you cannot choose is not available. Hold the pointer on it to see Includes something that cannot be chosen here. The line above Members can shows the number of abilities that the group gives, for example 15 of 41 granted. Users & Groups does not show in the editor. Only a superuser group has it. The levels only help you choose. Akaun keeps each ability on its own, as before. See Permissions explained.

Members may hand on to tokens & apps is a second list of areas under Members can. It is the most that the personal access tokens and the connected AI apps of a member can do. Each member chooses less for each token or app. A member cannot choose a permission that is not in this list. You can choose only what the group gives under Members can. An area that the group does not give shows Not granted to this group. When you remove a permission under Members can, Akaun also removes it here. When you give the group a new permission, Akaun does not add it here. Choose it here if the tokens and the apps of the members need it. A token or an app never does more than what its user may hand on at that time. When you remove a permission in either list, each token and each app of the members loses it on its next request. When a user is in two or more groups, the user may hand on each permission that one or more of these groups allow. A permission that a user has as an extra permission is never handed on. caution Do not let members hand on Adjustments or Manage on Settings unless a program must do these things. A program with a token acts without a person who checks each step. A superuser group does not show this list. The tokens and the apps of a superuser can have all permissions except Manage on Users & Groups.

caution When you set Superuser to on, each member of the group becomes a superuser. A superuser can do all actions in all areas. A superuser can also add users, remove users and make other users superusers. Use it only for people that you trust with all the books. Click the group. Click the Superuser switch. Click Save changes. The group shows Superuser. Under Members can, the group shows Every permission, and the permission lists do not show.

Administrators shows Protected. You cannot change its name, its description, its Superuser switch or its permissions. You cannot delete it. You can change, rename and delete all the other groups, also Bookkeeper, Data Entry and Reviewer.

At least one user must stay in a superuser group. Only a superuser can manage users and groups. Thus Akaun refuses a change that removes the last one, and shows At least one user must stay in a superuser group, or nobody could manage users and groups. These changes can show it: You turn off Superuser on the only other superuser group that has members. You remove the last superuser from their superuser group. You delete the last superuser. caution Keep two or more trusted users in Administrators. If the only superuser forgets the password, no screen in Akaun can give a new password to that user.

You can delete a group only when it has no members and is not protected. Click the group. Click the menu button (three dots) next to the name. Click Delete group. In the message of the browser, click OK. Akaun shows Group deleted. Akaun makes the default groups (Administrators, Bookkeeper, Data Entry and Reviewer) one time only, when you install it. If you delete or rename Bookkeeper, Data Entry or Reviewer, Akaun does not make it again. To get it back, make a new group and choose its permissions.

A change to the permissions applies on the next action of the user, and on the next request of each token and app of the user. The user does not need to sign in again. A user can have 50 personal access tokens or fewer. A sign-in stays valid in the browser for up to 30 days. A new password does not end a sign-in that is already open. To stop the access immediately, use a group with no permissions.
Your profile holds the settings that apply only to you. Examples are your name, your password and the order of your screens. All users can open their own profile. No permission is necessary.

At the bottom of the sidebar, click the user menu button (three dots) next to your name. Click Profile. The My Profile screen opens. It has five tabs: Profile, Security, Access tokens, Connected apps and Navigation.

caution If you are the admin user, do not change the username. At each start, Akaun adds a new superuser with the username admin and the password akaun-admin when no user has the username admin. See Users and groups. Click the Profile tab. Change Display name, Email or Username. Click Save changes. Akaun shows Profile updated. Email and Username are necessary. Each user must have a different email and a different username. If the step fails, Akaun shows one of these messages: Email or username is already taken. Enter a valid email address.

Use this tab to change your password. Click the Security tab. In Current password, type your password. In New password, type a new password. Use 8 characters or more. In Confirm new password, type the new password again. Click Change password. Akaun shows Password changed. Akaun also disconnects all your connected apps and revokes all your access tokens. The other browsers where you are signed in stay signed in. If the step fails, Akaun shows one of these messages: Current password is incorrect. New password must be at least 8 characters. Passwords do not match.

A personal access token lets a program, for example a script or an AI assistant, connect to Akaun as you. Each token has its own name, expiry date and permissions. Only you can make a token for yourself. The program sends the token in the header Authorization: Bearer akp_…. A token works on the API of Akaun and on MCP. See Connect AI assistants. caution A program with your token can do all the actions that the token permits, also changes and deletes if you select them. Give each token only the permissions that the program needs. Give the token only to a program that you trust.

Click the Access tokens tab. The tab shows one row for each token. You can also open the tab with the address /profile?tab=token. Each row shows: the name of the token, akp_… and the last four characters of the token, what the token can do in each area, for example Invoices Edit or Records View + Adjustments. Hold the pointer on an area to see a sentence that tells what the token can do there, Expires: the date when the token stops working, Never, or an Expired badge, Last used: the date of the last use, or Never, the Regenerate and Revoke buttons. If you have no tokens, the tab shows No access tokens yet.

Click the Access tokens tab. Click New token. The New access token page opens. Under Token, in Name, type a name that tells what the token is for, for example Claude — bookkeeping. Each token must have a different name. In Expires, select the last day when the token works. See Choose the expiry date. Under Permissions, select a level for each area that the program needs. See Choose the permissions of a token. Read the This token can panel at the side. It tells, for each area, what the token can do. At the bottom of the page, click Create token. Akaun shows the token one time, with the warning Copy the token now. It won't be shown again. Click Copy. Keep the token in a safe place, for example a password manager. Click Done. Akaun shows the list of your tokens again. The token starts with akp_. After you click Done, Akaun shows only the last four characters of the token. The bar at the bottom of the page shows after your first change. To remove your changes, click Discard. Choose the expiry date​ Expires shows a date 6 months from today. Click the field to select a different date. You can select only a date after today. The token works until the end of that day (UTC). To make a token that never expires, click × in the field. The field then shows Never expires, and a warning says "Anyone who gets this token can use it until you revoke it." To set a date again, click the field and select a date. caution A token that never expires works until you revoke it. Use an expiry date when you can. Choose the permissions of a token​ Permissions shows one row for each area, for example Records or Invoices. For each area, select None, View, Edit, Full or Custom. A sentence under the name of the area tells what your choice lets the token do. See Levels of access. Permissions offers only what you may hand on to tokens and apps. Your administrator sets this on your groups. See What members may hand on. An area that you cannot hand on shows You can't hand this on. A level that includes an ability that you cannot hand on is not available. Hold the pointer on it to see why. Adjustments on Records is not part of a level. To give it, switch it on by its name. If nothing can be handed on, Permissions says that an administrator chooses what each group may hand on, on Users & Groups. Then ask your administrator.

A token never does more than both of these: the permissions that you selected for the token, what you may hand on to tokens and apps at the time of each request. Thus when your administrator removes a permission from your group, or from what your group may hand on, each of your tokens loses it immediately. The permissions that you have as extra permissions are never handed on to a token.

To replace the secret of a token, click Regenerate, and then click Regenerate again in the message. The new token shows above the list one time only. Click Copy, and then click Done. The old token stops working immediately. The name, the permissions and the expiry date of the token stay the same. To remove a token, click Revoke, and then click Revoke again in the message. To remove all your tokens, click Revoke all N tokens under the list, and then click Revoke all in the message. The link shows when you have two or more tokens. An expired token has no Regenerate button. You cannot regenerate it. Make a new token instead. A program that uses a revoked token cannot connect any more. You cannot undo a revoke. You can have 50 tokens or fewer. A new password revokes all your tokens. A superuser can also see and revoke your tokens in Users & Groups, but cannot make a token for you. See Revoke the tokens of a user.

The Connected apps tab shows each app that you let read your data, for example an AI assistant. For each app, it shows: the name of the app, the access that you gave, for example records:read, the date of the connection and the date when it expires, Last used: the last time that the app read your data, or Never. If no app is connected, the tab shows No apps connected. To disconnect an app: Click the Connected apps tab. Find the app. Click Revoke access. Akaun shows App access revoked. The app cannot read your data any more. To use the app again, connect it again. A new password also disconnects all your apps. Sign out does not disconnect them. A connected app also never does more than what you may hand on to tokens and apps at that time.

Use this tab to change the order of the main screens in the sidebar. You can also choose the screens on the bottom bar of a phone. The list shows only the screens that you have the View permission for. Click the Navigation tab. Drag an item by its handle to change the order. Select Show on mobile for each screen that you want on the bottom bar. Click Save changes. Akaun shows Navigation order saved. You can select Show on mobile for five screens or fewer. After the fifth, the other boxes are not available. See Choose your navigation.

The Connected apps tab is empty when the administrator did not enable OAuth. See Connect AI assistants. Your groups and permissions are not on your profile. Only a superuser can change them. See Users and groups.

Auto Import uses an AI provider to read your documents. Add one provider before you upload the first file. This page also tells what the processing options on the same tab do. info To add or change a provider, you need the Manage permission on Settings. Without it, the Intelligence tab is read only. Akaun never shows the key of a provider.

caution The provider is a service outside your server. Akaun sends it the text of each document that you upload to Auto Import. Do not add a provider until you agree that it can read your receipts, bills and statements. Akaun reads the text from each file on your own server first. For a photo or a scanned PDF, the server uses text recognition (OCR). Then Akaun sends this text to the provider: the text of the document, the names of your expense and income categories, your Custom instructions, or the instructions of the import profile, for Auto-detect, the start of the document and the name and description of each enabled import profile. Akaun does not send the file itself. The bank statements that you upload on the reconciliation screen also go to the same provider. A spreadsheet that an import profile reads as Table rows does not go to the provider. See Import profiles.
documents.s: What Akaun sends to the provider

documents.t: Provider type What you need OpenRouter An API key from the OpenRouter website. One key gives access to many models. Google AI Studio An API key from the Google AI Studio website. It gives access to the Gemini models. Groq An API key from the Groq website. ChatGPT plan A paid ChatGPT plan. You sign in with a one-time code. You do not need an API key. The form shows a Get a key ↗ link for each provider that uses an API key. The link opens the page of that provider where you make a key.

Click Settings. Click the Intelligence tab. Under Providers, click Add provider. In Provider type, choose OpenRouter, Google AI Studio or Groq. Click Get a key ↗ and make a key on the website of the provider. Paste the key into API key. If you use OpenRouter and want no usage cost, click the Free models only switch. Wait until Akaun loads the models. Then choose a model in Model. If you want a different name for the provider, change Name. Click Add provider at the bottom of the form. Click Save at the bottom of the Intelligence tab. The provider is not saved until you click Save in step 11.
documents.s: Add a provider with an API key

documents.t: Before you start, enable device code sign-in in the security settings of your ChatGPT account. If your ChatGPT account belongs to a workspace, ask the workspace administrator to do this. Click Settings. Click the Intelligence tab. Under Providers, click Add provider. In Provider type, choose ChatGPT plan. Click Sign in with ChatGPT. Akaun opens the ChatGPT sign-in page in a new tab. Under Your one-time sign-in code, click Copy code. If no new tab opened, click Open ChatGPT ↗. In ChatGPT, paste the code and approve the sign-in. Return to Akaun. Wait until the form shows Signed in. Choose a model in Model. Click Add provider at the bottom of the form. Click Save at the bottom of the Intelligence tab. The code expires after a short time. The form shows the time of expiry. If the code expires, click Cancel and start again from step 5.
The provider shows in the list under Configured providers. Its type, name and model show on the row. Auto Import can now read documents.

You can add more than one provider. Akaun tries the enabled providers in the order of the list. If the first provider fails, Akaun tries the next one. To change the order, drag a provider by its handle on the left. Then click Save. To stop the use of a provider, click its switch. Then click Save. To change a saved provider, click its pencil icon. Make the change and click Save changes. This change is saved immediately. caution You cannot undo the deletion of a provider. To use it again, you must add it again with a new key or a new sign-in. To delete a provider, click its pencil icon, then click Delete. Click Delete again to confirm.

The Processing section is on the same tab. Click Save after you change an option. Option What it does Parallel tasks The number of files that Akaun reads at the same time, from 1 to 10. Rate limit The time that Akaun waits between two calls to the provider, from 0 to 30 seconds. Use it if your provider has a limit on calls per minute. Category hints The switch is saved, but at this time it does not change how Akaun reads documents. Custom instructions Extra guidance for the AI, for example your usual suppliers and their categories. An import profile with its own instructions uses those in place of these.

If no provider is enabled, each file that needs AI fails with the message "No LLM providers configured". A ChatGPT provider that shows Reconnect required must sign in again. Click its pencil icon, then click Sign in with ChatGPT. The quality of the reading depends on the model. If many fields are wrong, try a different model.
Import receipts and documents Import profiles Settings reference

Some documents hold many records, for example a statement from a marketplace or an e-wallet. Akaun reads each line as an item. You review the items of one document on its own page. Akaun reads a document this way when you choose Multiple records under Read as. It also reads a document this way when an import profile reads it. If the reading finds only one item, Akaun shows it as one card. See Review and confirm and Import receipts and documents.

A document with many records shows as one card under Ready to review. The card shows: how Akaun read the document, and the number of items, the number of items that are ready, need attention, are confirmed and are skipped, the control total, if the document has one. See Control total. Click the card to open the page of the document. Skip on the card skips each item that still waits. Akaun asks you first, and you click Skip in the dialog. Items that are already confirmed keep their records. Skip shows only when you have the Confirm permission.

On Auto Import, click the card of the document. Check the items in the list. Click an item to open its card. In the account field, choose the account for all items, for example Bank. Click Confirm all (12). The name of the account field tells what the account does: Field When it shows Payment account All items are expenses. Deposit account All items are income. Payment or deposit account The document has expenses and income. Statement account The document has transfers. The account field shows Choose one for every item until you choose an account. Akaun saves your choice immediately. If an account does not fit an item, the item keeps its own account, and a note tells you why. If you choose no account, each item stays on its account from the reading. Usually this is Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable, so the records are Outstanding. See Review and confirm. The number in Confirm all (12) is the number of items that are ready. The button confirms only these items. A bar shows the progress. If Akaun leaves an item, a report shows the item and the reason.

Each confirmed item becomes one record on the Records screen. The document file is attached to each record. A confirmed item in the list links to its record. At the end, the page shows the note "Every item is confirmed or skipped." The document then moves to This session on Auto Import.

An item needs attention when Akaun cannot confirm it without your check. For example: it is a possible duplicate, it has a foreign currency and no rate, it has no account, the import profile marked it for review, with a note. Confirm all (12) leaves these items. Open each item, correct it, and click Confirm & import. For a possible duplicate, the button is Import anyway.

Use the tabs above the list: All, Ready, Needs attention, Possible duplicates, Confirmed and Skipped. Two more filters show when they are useful: Kind shows when the document has more than one kind of record. Choose Expense, Income or Transfer. Section shows when the import profile has more than one section. Choose one section. The list shows 50 items on each page.
Click the item in the list. Correct the fields on its card. Click Confirm & import, or click Skip. Akaun saves each change on an item immediately. You do not lose it when you leave the page.

Select the check box of each item. Only the items that wait have a check box. In the bar at the bottom, choose an action. Action What it does Confirm Confirms the selected items that are ready. Skip Skips the selected items, after you click Skip in the dialog. Category Gives the selected items one category. Account Gives the selected items one account.
Click the file name to open the original document in a new tab. Akaun attaches this one file to each record that it makes from the document.

The control total is the total that the document prints, for example "Total payout released". Akaun compares it with the total of the items that it read. On the document is the printed total. Items as read is the total of the items. If the two are different, a line shows the difference. You can still confirm the items. A difference usually shows that the reading missed a line, or read one line twice. Compare the items with the document before you confirm. Akaun checks the items as it read them. Your later changes and skips do not change the result.
A line such as Ignored 3 lines shows the number of lines that the reading left out, for example subtotals. Click it to see the lines. For a long list, Akaun shows only the first lines.

This shows for a spreadsheet that an import profile read from its columns, with a balance column. Akaun checks that each row's balance is the previous balance plus the row's amount. If the balance does not follow, the panel names the row. A row can be missing from the export, or changed.

Read again reads the file again in a different way. The new reading replaces each item that waits and each skipped item. When an item is confirmed, you cannot read the document again. You need the Upload and Change permissions on Auto Import.

caution You cannot undo this. The items that wait are removed. The records that Akaun already made stay, and so does the file while a record uses it. In the side panel, under Discard, click Delete. In the dialog, click Delete. To discard a document, you need the Delete permission on Auto Import. The Discard section shows only while items wait.
One file is imported one way only. If a file already made records, Akaun does not read a second copy of it as many records. A document can have 1,000 items or fewer.
Review and confirm Import spreadsheets Import profiles

An import profile is a saved way to read one kind of document, for example the monthly statement of a marketplace. You make it one time. Then Akaun reads each new statement of that kind the same way. info To see the profiles, you need the View permission on Auto Import. To add, change, enable, disable or delete a profile, you need Profiles. To enable or disable a profile, or to import one from a file, you also need the Manage permission on Settings. Without it, the Intelligence tab is read only.

You do not need a profile for a receipt or a bill. Single record reads those well. Make a profile when: you import the same report each week or each month, each row or line of the report must become one record, each type of line must go to its own category, for example commission or shipping fees, the report has withdrawals to your bank, which are transfers, you want Akaun to read a spreadsheet table without AI. See also Import spreadsheets.

Choose the type in What to import. The type decides what Akaun reads and who reads it. Type What it imports Who reads it Table rows Each row of a spreadsheet table becomes a record. Akaun reads the cells. No AI. Spreadsheets only. Summary lines The totals and fees in the summary of a statement. The AI. Transaction lines Each line of a document. The AI. Table rows and summary lines The rows of a table, and lines outside the table, for example a fee. Akaun reads the table. The AI reads the other lines. Spreadsheets only.

Click Settings. Click the Intelligence tab. Under Import profiles, click New profile. In What to import, choose the type. In Reads, select PDF files and photos, Spreadsheets, or both. A type that reads a table always reads Spreadsheets only. Type a Name, for example "Marketplace monthly statement". In Account, choose the account of the document, for example the wallet of the marketplace. Complete the cards below. See the sections that follow. Check the Before you save card on the right. Click Add profile. Account is optional. If you choose one, the items use it in place of Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable. A profile with a transfer section must have an account. Sheet shows when the profile reads spreadsheets. Type the name of the sheet to read in a workbook with many sheets. If you leave it empty, Akaun finds the sheet with the table headings. For an AI profile, Akaun uses the first sheet.

A profile that reads a table needs a sample. The sample is a real report of the same kind. In the Table card, drag a sample .xlsx or .csv file onto the drop area. Make sure that Akaun found the correct heading row. If the heading row is wrong, click Select a different table. Check the role of each column: Date, Description, Amount, Reference, Direction (inflow or outflow), Running balance or Not used. Akaun gives a role to some columns from the sample. Date, Description and Amount are necessary. If one column tells the direction of the money, give it Direction (inflow or outflow). Then set each of its values to Inflow or Outflow. An inflow is money into the account. An outflow is money out of the account. Akaun does not keep the sample. More options has the less common settings, for example Date format, Decimal separator, CSV separator and Labels of the stated totals.

The Rows become cards tell Akaun which rows become which records. Each table section, including Every row, has Import rows only when. Add conditions such as Status is Completed to keep only matching rows. Every condition must match; with no conditions, all rows assigned to the section are kept. Comparisons ignore case and extra spacing. Filters remain in place when you change the column used to split rows. Use Test sample to check the resulting section counts and ignored rows. Assignment counts are shown before filtering. Filtered rows count as ignored and are not read by AI in a mixed profile. A stated total still compares against the imported items, so filtering can cause a difference from a whole-document total. Running-balance checks still inspect the source table. If all rows are of one kind, use one section. Give it a kind and a category. If the rows are of different kinds, click Split rows by a column. Choose the Column that tells the type of each row. Then choose a section for each value, or Ignore. Each section has these fields: Field What it does Name The name of the section, for example "Fees". A profile with one section for all rows shows Every row in place of a name. Kind Income, Expense, By sign or Transfer. With By sign, a positive amount is income and a negative amount is an expense. With Income or Expense, Akaun ignores a row with the opposite sign. Category The category for each record of the section. If you choose none (Reviewer selects), the reviewer chooses it. Other account For a Transfer only. The account that the money goes to or comes from, for example your bank. Line types Optional. Divides the section into types, for example commission and shipping. Each type can have its own category. More in each section has additional row-selection and overlap rules.
documents.s: Tell Akaun where each row goes

documents.t: For Summary lines and Transaction lines, the cards are under Lines to import. For Table rows and summary lines, the AI part is under Lines outside the table. Click Add section. Type a Name. Choose a Kind and, if you know it, a Category. In Description, tell the AI what the lines are and where they are on the document. If you choose no category (AI suggests), the AI suggests one. A profile can have 20 sections or fewer.

The Auto-detect card helps Akaun find this profile when you upload with Auto-detect. Document description: tell who sends the document and what it shows. A profile that the AI reads must have a description. Fixed phrases: text that is always on the document, for example its title. Type a phrase and click Add. You can add 10 phrases. Auto-detect checks fixed phrases across all enabled profiles that can read the file first. If exactly one profile has all its phrases in the document, Akaun selects it without AI. For a spreadsheet with no phrase matches, a unique table-heading match is used next. If the choice is still unclear, AI chooses among the matching profiles, or reports that none fits. A table profile whose required headings are absent cannot read the file and is excluded. The upload page remembers your last Read as selection on this device. Choosing a specific profile uses that profile directly for every upload; choose Auto-detect to match each document automatically.

This card shows for a profile that the AI reads. Instructions: guidance for the AI for this profile only. They replace the Custom instructions in Settings › Intelligence. Stated total: the label of the printed total, for example "Total payout released". Akaun then shows if the items agree with the total. See Documents with many records.

A profile that reads a table has the Test on the sample card. You can test before you save. Load a sample in the Table card. In Test on the sample, click Test. Read the result: the number of rows in each section, the ignored rows and the first items. If the profile has stated totals, compare Items with Stated total. Correct the profile, and then click Test again. The test keeps no data and makes no records.

The Before you save card lists each problem that stops the save. Click a problem to go to its field. When the list is empty, the card shows Ready to save. To save a new profile, click Add profile. To save changes to a saved profile, click Save profile.

Only an enabled profile shows under Read as and in Auto-detect. Click Settings. Click the Intelligence tab. Under Saved profiles, click the switch of the profile. Click Save at the bottom of the tab. If you disable a profile, a document in the queue that waits for it fails.

You can export a profile to a JSON file, and import it into a different Akaun installation. To export a profile: Open the profile from Settings › Intelligence. If you changed the profile, save it first. Click Export. If Settings has unsaved changes, save or discard them before you import a profile. To import a profile: Click Settings. Click the Intelligence tab. Under Saved profiles, click Import. Choose the JSON file. Check the profile in the editor. Choose each account or category that the editor shows as empty. Click Add profile or Save profile. The file names each account by its code and name. Akaun finds the account with the same code first, and then with the same name. If it finds neither, the field stays empty. The Imported from card lists these fields. If a saved profile has the same name as the profile in the file, the editor opens that profile. Your save then replaces it. The History of the profile keeps the changes. Nothing is saved until you click the save button.
documents.s: Move a profile to a different installation

documents.t: caution You cannot undo this. The profile no longer shows under Read as. The records that you imported with it do not change. Open the profile. Click Delete. In the dialog, click Delete.
