Use Auto Import to let AI read receipts, bills, invoices, statements and spreadsheets. Akaun reads each file and prepares a record. You check each record before Akaun saves it. info To upload files, you need the Upload permission on Auto Import. To confirm or skip a record, you need Confirm. To correct a record before you confirm it, you need Change. To read a file again, you need both Upload and Change. See Permissions explained. Before you start, add an AI provider. See Connect an AI provider.

File Notes PDF A PDF with text, or a scanned PDF. Akaun reads a scanned PDF with text recognition (OCR). JPG or PNG A photo of a receipt or a bill. Akaun reads it with OCR. Excel workbook (.xlsx) See Import spreadsheets. CSV See Import spreadsheets. Each file can be 15 MB or smaller. OCR reads English and Simplified Chinese.

Read as is below the drop area. Choose it before you add the file. Choice What Akaun does Auto-detect Akaun uses an enabled import profile that fits the document. If no profile fits, Akaun reads the document as one record. Single record Akaun reads the document as one receipt or one bill. It makes one record. Multiple records Akaun reads each item on the document as a separate record, for example each line of a statement. The name of a profile Akaun reads the document with this import profile. A profile that reads one type of file only shows it after its name, for example "(spreadsheets only)". Akaun remembers your last choice on this computer or phone.
documents.s: Choose how Akaun reads the file

documents.t: Click Auto Import. In Read as, choose how Akaun reads the files. Drag the files onto the area with the text Drop files here, or browse. To choose the files from a folder, click the area, and then choose the files. You can add many files at the same time. If Akaun refuses a file, the reason shows below the area. On a phone, you can also scan a page with the camera. See Scan with your phone.

Each file goes into the Processing queue. The row of each file shows its type and its state: State Meaning Queued The file waits for a free place. Extracting text… Akaun reads the text from the file. Reading with AI… The AI provider reads the text. Reading part 3 of 25… Akaun reads a long document in parts. The numbers show the progress. The heading of the queue shows the number of files that Akaun reads at this moment, for example "2/3 workers active". The number after the slash is always 3. It does not show the Parallel tasks setting.

When Akaun finishes a file, the file moves to one of these sections: Ready to review: Akaun made one record, or a document with many records. See Review and confirm and Documents with many records. Failed: Akaun could not read the file. The row shows the reason.

A failed row has these buttons: Retry: uploads the same file again, with the same Read as choice. This button shows only in the browser tab where you uploaded the file, before a reload. Read again: reads the file again from the copy on the server. You can choose a different Read as choice. Then click Read again in the dialog. This button shows only when you have the Upload and Change permissions. Discard: removes the row from the list. You need the Delete permission on Auto Import. A review card also has Read again. The new reading replaces the card and all your changes on it. If Akaun cannot read the document again, the button is not available. Point to the button to see the reason.

This session lists the documents that are confirmed, imported or skipped. Click the row of an imported record to open the record. Click the row of a document with many records to open its page. A skipped row does not open. A row with "filed as Uncategorised" went to the default category for uncategorised items. Give it a better category on its record page. caution Clear history removes the list for all users. You cannot undo it. The records that Akaun made do not change. To clear the list: Click Clear history. In the dialog, click Clear history. To clear the history, you need the Delete permission on Auto Import.

All users see the same queue. Any user with the Confirm permission can confirm a document that a different user uploaded. If Akaun reads too little text, the file fails. Use a clearer photo, or a PDF with text. If you upload a file that Akaun already imported as one record, the card shows a possible duplicate. See Review and confirm. If Akaun reads a file as many records and that file already made records, the file fails. The row tells you how the file was imported before. If no AI provider is enabled, a file that needs AI fails. The row tells you to add a provider. See Connect an AI provider. If an import profile reads all of a spreadsheet from its columns, Akaun does not use AI for it. See Import spreadsheets.
Review and confirm Import profiles Attach receipts

Akaun shows each record that it read as a card under Ready to review. Check the card, correct it, and then confirm it. Akaun saves no record until you confirm. info To confirm or skip a card, you need the Confirm permission on Auto Import. You do not need a permission on Records. Without Confirm, the buttons still show, but Akaun refuses the action. To correct the fields of a card, you need the Change permission on Auto Import.

The title of the card is the name of the file. Click the title to open the original document in a new tab. Below the title, a line tells if the AI read the document as an expense, an income or a transfer. Field What it holds Description A short text that tells what the record is for. Contact The supplier or the customer, as printed on the document. Amount The amount in the main currency. Currency The currency of the document. Source account Where the money came from. See the next section. Target account Where the money went. See the next section. Date The date of the document. Reference The number of the receipt or the bill. Remark Your own note. Akaun never completes it. When you change a field, the word edited shows beside its name. The bottom of the card can show how many fields you changed. If you change nothing, it can show Importing AI values as-is. A note about the accounts shows there in place of these texts.

The Source account decides if the record is an expense or an income. Record Source account Target account Expense A cash or bank account, a credit card, or Accounts Payable. The list shows them under Payment. An expense category, or a thing that you buy and keep. Income An income category. The list shows them under Income. A cash or bank account, or Accounts Receivable. If you choose an income category as the Source account, the card becomes an income. The Target account list then shows only the accounts that fit.

A document proves that an amount is owed. It does not prove that the money moved. So Akaun starts each card as a record that is not paid yet: An expense starts with Accounts Payable as the Source account. An income starts with Accounts Receivable as the Target account. An expense on Accounts Payable shows a note at the bottom of the card: "Recorded in accounts payable to the contact above until it is paid." Akaun records a bill from the contact that is not paid yet. It is a payable. If you confirm without a change, the record is Outstanding. It is a payable to the contact on the card, or a receivable from that contact. To pay a bill later, see Bills you pay later. If the money already moved, choose the cash or bank account. For example, choose Bank as the Source account of an expense. The record is then Paid when you confirm it. An import profile can name the account of a document, for example a marketplace wallet. A card from that profile starts on that account. See Import profiles.
documents.s: The record is outstanding at first

documents.t: If the AI finds no category that fits, the Target account of an expense is the default for an uncategorised expense. In a new book, this is Other Expenses. An income uses the default for uncategorised income, which is Other Revenue in a new book. You can choose a better category before you confirm.

A card that an import profile read as a transfer has Transfer from and Transfer to in place of the two account fields. Both accounts hold money, for example a wallet and a bank account. A transfer has no contact and no category. A transfer must be in the main currency. If it is in a different currency, you cannot confirm it. Record it by hand, or skip it.

Akaun compares the name on the document with your contacts. A tag beside Contact shows the result: existing: Akaun uses this contact. new: no contact has this name. Akaun adds the contact when you confirm. A new contact gets the role Supplier for an expense, or Customer for an income. To use a different contact, choose it in the list. To use a new name, type the name.

If the document is in a foreign currency, the card shows two more fields. One is the amount in that currency. The other is the rate, for example Rate (1 USD = ? MYR). Akaun tries to find the rate for the date of the document. Amount then shows the amount in the main currency. If Akaun finds no rate, the card shows "Enter the rate manually to convert to MYR." Type the rate. You cannot confirm the card until it has a rate. See Foreign currency.

Akaun compares each card with the records that are already in the book. If they look the same, the card shows a Duplicate tag. The tag shows a score and the reasons, for example "Duplicate · 85% · reference · amount". Akaun looks at these signs: The file is the same file as one that Akaun imported before. The reference is the same. The amount is the same, or almost the same. The date is the same, or near. The contact has the same name, or a similar name. The file name is similar. The text of the document is similar. For a transfer, Akaun looks for a record with the same amount, between the same two accounts, in the same direction, within seven days. The confirm button of a possible duplicate is Import anyway. The card does not link to the existing record. Find the record on the Records screen and compare it first. If the card is a second copy, click Skip.

Check each field on the card. Make sure that the Source account and the Target account are correct. If the document is in a foreign currency, make sure that the rate has a value. Click Confirm & import. If a rule stops the record, the bottom of the card shows the reason. Akaun saves nothing. To make no record from the card, click Skip. The card moves to This session as skipped.

Check each card on the list. Click Confirm all (3) at the top of Ready to review. The button confirms each card that is not a possible duplicate and has both accounts. It leaves a card in a foreign currency that has no rate. Confirm those cards one at a time.

The card moves to This session. It shows Importing…, and then a check mark. Click the row to open the new record. The record shows on the Records screen. Its kind is Expense, Income or Transfer. The original document is attached to the record. See Records.

Your changes on a card stay in this browser tab only. If you reload the page before you confirm, the changes are lost. If a different user reads the document again while you review it, Akaun refuses your confirm. Check the new card and confirm again. A document with many records opens on its own page. See Documents with many records.
Outstanding, partially paid and paid Contacts Accounts and categories

Choose an Asset source that holds transaction funds, such as Shopee clearing, a wallet or a bank account. Select a target under Contra revenue, with the Contra operating revenue or Contra other revenue sub-type. Ordinary Revenue sources cannot target contra revenue. For example, Sales → Shopee clearing records RM1,000 of gross sales. Shopee clearing → Sales discounts then records RM100 of deductions: credit clearing RM100 and debit contra revenue RM100. Net revenue is RM900 and clearing holds RM900. A separate RM50 expense charge uses Shopee clearing → Expense, leaving clearing RM850 and profit RM850. These deductions use the outgoing (Expense) import flow and record shape. Financial reports classify them by their Revenue account, so they reduce revenue rather than increase expenses. Select contra accounts for outgoing sections and fee types in import profiles, or as a target while reviewing an outgoing item. The profile's account remains the clearing, bank or wallet account. Income sections and AI income-category suggestions exclude contra accounts. You can bulk-assign a contra category to outgoing items and a clearing account as their funding account. Payables, credit cards and non-transaction assets cannot fund contra-revenue deductions.
documents.s: Importing deductions from clearing into contra revenue

documents.t: On a phone, Auto Import can scan a paper receipt with the camera. Akaun finds the edges of the page, makes the image flat and clear, and adds it to the queue as a PDF. The Scan button shows only on a narrow screen, such as a phone. On a computer, take a photo and upload it. See Import receipts and documents.

Open Auto Import on your phone. In Read as, choose how Akaun reads the scan. Put the receipt on a flat surface with good light. Tap Scan at the bottom right of the screen. Take a photo of the receipt with the camera, and accept it. Wait until the text "Finding document…" goes away. The title of the screen is Review scan. Check the image. If you must change it, use the tools in the next section. Tap Save.

The bar at the bottom of Review scan has these tools: Tool What it does Retake Opens the camera again for a new photo. Adjust Shows the four corners of the page. Drag each corner to the edge of the page. Tap Apply to keep the change, Reset to start again, or Cancel. Rotate Turns the image by a quarter turn, clockwise. Filter Shows three filters: Colors, Grayscale and B&W. Tap one to use it. B&W is the default and usually gives the clearest text. Save Makes the PDF and adds it to the queue. To stop without a scan, tap Cancel at the top left.

Akaun shows "Preparing document...", and then closes the scanner. The scan shows in the Processing queue as a PDF with a name such as scan-1760000000000.pdf. Review it as usual. See Review and confirm.

One scan makes a PDF with one page. For a document with many pages, use a scanner app that makes one PDF. Then upload the PDF. The scanner loads its tools from the server the first time. If the message "Could not load the scanner" shows, check the connection and try again. The scan is a picture of the page. Akaun reads its text with text recognition (OCR), so a sharp photo gives a better result.
Import receipts and documents Review and confirm
Auto Import reads Excel workbooks (.xlsx) and CSV files. Use it for a report that a marketplace, an e-wallet or a bank lets you download.

Click Auto Import. In Read as, choose how Akaun reads the file. See Which reading to choose. Drag the .xlsx or .csv file onto the drop area. The queue shows the file as Spreadsheet. Akaun reads the cells directly. It does not use text recognition.

Read as Use it for How Akaun reads it Single record A small sheet that is one bill. The AI reads the text of the sheet. The text must have 6,000 characters or fewer. Multiple records A list of items that you import one time. The AI reads all the text and makes one item from each line. An import profile A report that you import each month. The profile tells Akaun how to read the report. Auto-detect Any file. Akaun uses a profile that fits. If no profile fits, Akaun reads the file as a single record. With Multiple records and with an import profile, Akaun shows the items on one page. If the reading finds only one item, Akaun shows one review card in its place. See Documents with many records.

Make an import profile when one or more of these is true: You import the same report each week or each month. The report has many rows, and you want each row to become one record. You want Akaun to read the table without AI, so that the amounts come directly from the cells. Each type of row must go to its own category, for example commission or shipping fees. The report has a running balance, and you want Akaun to check that no row is missing. The report has withdrawals to your bank. These are transfers, not expenses. A profile of the type Table rows reads the table without AI. If you choose it in Read as, Akaun sends nothing to the AI provider. See Import profiles.
documents.s: When you need an import profile

documents.t: A marketplace wallet or an e-wallet report often shows a withdrawal to your bank. The withdrawal moves money between two of your own accounts. It is a transfer, not an expense. To import withdrawals as transfers, use an import profile: Give the profile an Account, for example the wallet account. Add a section with the Kind Transfer. In the section, choose the Other account, for example your bank account. The card of a transfer shows Transfer from and Transfer to. A transfer must be in the main currency. If the same transfer is already in your records, the card shows a possible duplicate. This can happen when you also import the bank statement. See Review and confirm.

Akaun refuses some files when you upload them. The message shows below the drop area. File Message What to do Old Excel file (.xls) "This is an old Excel file (.xls), which cannot be read." Open the file in Excel. Save it as .xlsx or .csv. Upload it again. Binary Excel file (.xlsb) "This is a binary Excel workbook (.xlsb), which cannot be read." Save it as .xlsx or .csv. Upload it again. Workbook with a password "This workbook is protected with a password, so it cannot be read." Remove the password in Excel. Save the file. Upload it again. A .csv file that is a workbook "The file is named .csv but is an Excel workbook." Change the name to .xlsx, or save it from Excel as CSV. An empty .csv file "The CSV file is empty." Download the report again.

A spreadsheet can have 200,000 rows or fewer, in all its sheets. An import profile reads one sheet of a workbook only. The built-in readings read all the sheets. A CSV file always has one sheet. So a profile that you made for a workbook also reads the same report as CSV. A single record from a spreadsheet longer than 6,000 characters fails. Read it again with Multiple records or with an import profile.
Import profiles Documents with many records Move money between accounts

Bank reconciliation is a check of one account against the statement from your bank. You match each statement line to a record in Akaun. When each line has a match, Akaun and the bank agree. Do this check each month, after the bank sends the statement.

You need these things: The Reconciliation permission. View lets you open the screens. Add lets you upload a statement, retry a failed statement and record a line as a transfer. Match lets you save and remove a match. Change lets you correct a line and move a statement to a different account. Delete lets you delete a statement or a statement line. To record a line as a transfer, you also need the Add permission on Records. See Permissions explained. An AI provider. Akaun uses the AI provider to read the lines of a statement. See Connect an AI provider. The statement as a PDF, JPEG or PNG file. The file can be 15 MB or smaller. The records for the period of the statement. Record each expense, income and transfer first. info You reconcile an account from its account page. Reconcile shows only on an active account, and only if you have the View permission on Reconciliation. To open the reconciliation screen of an account: Click Accounts. Click the account, for example Bank. Click Reconcile. If the account has statements that are not complete, the button shows their number, for example Reconcile · 2 open. The Bank reconciliation screen shows the statements of this account. Below the title, Akaun shows the unreconciled amount, for example 1,250.00 unreconciled. When nothing is left, it shows Fully reconciled.

On the Bank reconciliation screen, click Upload Statement. Click Choose file. Select the statement file. Click Upload. Akaun shows "Statement extraction started". The new statement shows in the list with the status Extracting. When Akaun has read the lines, the status changes to Active.

The list has these columns: Statement: the file name and the date of the upload. Date Range: the date of the first line and the last line. Status: Extracting, Failed, Active or Matched. Matched: the number of statement lines with a full match, out of all lines. Remaining: the amount of the statement lines that has no match yet. The Active, Completed and All tabs show a count for each group. Active shows statements that still need work. Completed shows statements with a full match on each line. All shows both groups. The page opens on Active by default. Use Search statements… to find a statement by its file name.

Click a statement in the list to open its matching page. The summary shows the account, statement period, matched transactions and unallocated statement amount. Open Statement details to see the full filename, upload date and View source file link, which opens the original in a new tab. If you uploaded the statement to the wrong account, choose the correct account in Account this statement belongs to, then click Move statement. You can move a statement only before it has a match. This control shows only if you have the Change permission. After the move, the matching page opens under the new account.

If Akaun cannot read the file, the status is Failed. The matching page shows the reason. Open the statement from the list. Read the reason shown below the summary. Click Retry extraction. If the retry fails again, delete the statement. Then upload a clearer file. If no AI provider is enabled, the statement fails. Add a provider, and then retry. The reason can tell you to add the transactions manually. Akaun has no control to add a statement line. Upload a different file of the statement instead.

caution You cannot undo this. Akaun deletes the statement, its lines and all their matches. Each record that only this statement matched is then unreconciled. Open the statement from the list, then expand Statement details. Click Delete statement. Confirm Delete statement. Akaun returns to the statement list.

In the list of statements, click the statement. Click a record in the list on the left. Make sure that the correct statement lines are ticked. Click Save & Next. Akaun saves the match and opens the next record. If no other record needs a match, the button is Save. You need the Match permission to save. The match screen has three parts: The list of records. Each row shows the record, the Account, the Date, the Total, the Match status and the amount that is Remaining. The match panel, beside the list. It shows the record that you clicked. Extracted Transactions, below the list. These are the lines that Akaun read from the statement. The title of the screen shows the file name. Below it, Akaun shows the status of the statement, the number of records to match and the amount of the statement lines without a match. Click Source file to open the uploaded file in a new tab. A statement line can match only a record that used the account of the statement. The list of records can also show records from other accounts that have a statement. These records have no lines to match. Look at the Account column, and do not choose them.

Type in Search records… to filter the list. Akaun searches the description, the contact, the account and the kind of each record. Click Date, and then choose a From date, a To date or both. The list then shows only the records in that period. Click Clear to remove the dates. On a narrow screen, the date filter is under Filters. The bottom of the list shows how many records the filters show, for example "Showing 8 of 20".

Akaun looks for statement lines that have the same direction as the record: Credit (money into the account) or Debit (money out of the account). The lines must have the same date as the record, and their total must equal its amount. If Akaun finds them, the record shows Exact match. If records compete for the same line, they show Needs manual choice and automatic matching skips them. You can still select lines manually when the bank and record dates differ. The Match column shows one of these statuses: Exact match: Akaun found statement lines with exactly the amount of the record. Needs manual choice: records compete for the same statement line; choose the correct record manually. Partial: some of the amount has a match, but not all of it. No match: Akaun found no lines that fit. Matched: statement lines cover the full amount of the record. The list shows Exact match records first, then Partial, then No match, then Matched.

When you click a record, the panel shows three amounts: Total: the amount of the record. Staged: the total of the ticked statement lines. Remaining: the amount of the record that has no line yet. If Akaun found an exact match, it ticks those lines for you. The panel then shows Suggested match. If you change the ticks, the panel shows Exact Match Found. Click Use Suggested Match to tick the suggested lines again. Compatible Statement Lines lists the lines that can match this record. A record of money into the account shows Credit lines. A record of money out of the account shows Debit lines. Each line shows the amount that is still available.

One record can use more than one statement line. One statement line can also go to more than one record. For example, the bank shows one line of 500.00. In Akaun, you have two records: 300.00 and 200.00. Click the record of 300.00. Tick the line of 500.00. Make sure that the amount beside the line is 300.00. Click Save & Next. Click the record of 200.00. Tick the same line. Click Save & Next. The line now has 0.00 available, and both records show Matched. The staged total cannot be more than the amount of the record. If it is more, the panel shows the difference in red, for example "50.00 over record total". You cannot save until you correct it. Click Reset to remove the changes that you did not save.
documents.s: Match a part of a line

documents.t: caution This saves many matches at one time. To remove a match later, you must remove it one record at a time. Click Save n exact matches. For example, Save 12 exact matches. Read the message. Click Save Matches. Akaun saves the suggested lines for each record that shows Exact match. It does not change a record that already has a part of a match. Competing records are skipped until you choose a match manually. A record is also skipped if its suggested lines are no longer available. Akaun then shows the number of records that it matched and skipped. The button counts only the records that the list shows. If you search or filter the list, the button saves only the matches in the filtered list. You need the Match permission to see the button.

Sometimes Akaun reads a line incorrectly. You can correct the line. In Extracted Transactions, click the line. Change Date, Description, Amount, Direction or Note. Akaun saves each change when you leave the field. You need the Change permission. In Direction, Credit is money into the account. Debit is money out of the account. These are the terms of the bank statement.

Some statement lines have no record, because the money moved between two of your own accounts. For example, you moved money from Bank to Cash. Akaun can make the transfer record for you. In Extracted Transactions, click the line. Click Record as a transfer from another account. Choose the other account. Optional: change the Description. Click Save & Match. For money into the account, the field of the other account is From account. For money out of the account, it is To account. Akaun makes a Transfer record in the main currency, with the date and amount of the line. Then it matches the line to the transfer. The button shows only on a line without a match. You need the Add permission on Reconciliation and on Records. The list of other accounts shows only cash and bank accounts. A category, an owner account, a receivable or a payable is not a transfer: record the line as an expense or income, or as a payment, and match it. A user with Adjustments on Records sees every account.
documents.s: Record a line as a transfer

documents.t: caution You cannot undo this. Akaun deletes the line and all its matches. In Extracted Transactions, click the line. Click Delete Transaction. In the dialog, click Delete Transaction. You need the Delete permission.

Click the record that has the match. Remove the tick from each statement line. Click Save & Next or Save. The record then has no match. If nothing else locks it, you can change its amount, date and payment account again.

A statement is complete when each of its lines has a full match. Its status then changes to Matched. It moves from Active to Completed. You do not click a button to complete a statement. If a statement line has no record, do one of these things: Add the missing record on the Records screen. Then match the line. If the money moved between two of your accounts, record the line as a transfer. If the line is wrong or appears two times, delete the line.

When statement lines cover the full amount of a record, the record is reconciled. On the Records screen, a record without a full match shows Unreconciled. When a record has a match, also a part match, the record page shows Reconciled in the Bank section. A record with a match, also a part match, is locked. You cannot change its amount, date or payment account, and you cannot delete it. See Locked records. Reconciled and paid are different. Paid tells that the money has moved. Reconciled tells that the bank statement agrees.
documents.s: What a match does to a record

documents.t: To find the records of all accounts without a full match, use the Unreconciled filter on the Records screen. See Find records. On a narrow screen, the match panel opens as a drawer. If you open a different record or leave the match screen with changes that you did not save, Akaun asks you first. Click Discard Changes to continue without them. An AI provider can make mistakes. Compare the Matched count and the Remaining amount with the statement from the bank.
Locked records Move money between accounts Find records Connect an AI provider
An account is a place where money is kept, owed or counted. Some accounts tell where money is. Other accounts tell what the money was for. This page tells how Akaun keeps the two apart.

Each record moves money from one account into a different account. Usually one side is a place where money is, for example Bank. The other side tells what the money was for, for example Software. A cash or bank account is an Asset account that holds money, for example Cash or Bank. Accounts Receivable is in this group too. It holds the receivables: the money that customers owe. A category tells what the business spent money on, or how it earned money. Examples are Advertising, Shipping and Product Sales. In Akaun, a category is an account of the type Expense or Revenue. There is no separate screen for categories. You find all accounts and all categories on the Accounts screen. On the Records screen, the Category filter shows only the records of the categories that you choose.
documents.s: Where money is, and what it was for

documents.t: Each account has one of five types. The Accounts screen has an All tab and one tab for each type. Type What it is Examples Asset A thing that the business owns. Cash, a bank balance, receivables, stock, equipment. Liability Money that the business owes to a different person or business. Payables (a supplier bill that is not paid yet), a loan. Equity The value that the owners or partners have in the business. Owner's Equity, Retained Earnings. Revenue Money that the business earns. A Revenue account is an income category. Product Sales, Other Revenue. Expense Money that the business spends. An Expense account is an expense category. Advertising, Software, Utilities. The type tells the reports where the account goes. Asset, Liability and Equity accounts go on the Balance Sheet. Revenue and Expense accounts go on Profit & Loss. You cannot change the type of an account after a record or a bank statement uses it.

Equipment is an asset that you buy and keep, for example a laptop. It stays on the Balance Sheet and does not go into the expenses on Profit & Loss. But you record its purchase in the same way as an expense. The record form shows these asset accounts together with the categories. These are the Asset accounts with these sub-types: Fixed asset, Intangible asset, Inventory, Prepayments and deposits, Tax receivable, Other current asset and Other non-current asset. All other Asset accounts are cash or bank accounts.
documents.s: Things that you buy and keep

documents.t: The sub-type puts an account into a line of a report. Each type except Equity has sub-types. Type Sub-types Asset Cash, Bank, Wallet, Prepaid/debit card, Accounts receivable, Inventory, Prepayments and deposits, Clearing, Tax receivable, Other current asset, Fixed asset, Intangible asset, Other non-current asset Liability Accounts payable, Credit card, Accrued liabilities, Short-term loan, Tax payable, Other current liability, Long-term loan, Other non-current liability Revenue Operating revenue, Other revenue, Contra operating revenue, Contra other revenue Expense Cost of goods sold, Operating expense, Other expense The sub-type is important for the reports: Balance Sheet: the sub-type puts each asset and liability into current or non-current. For example, Fixed asset is non-current and Short-term loan is current. Profit & Loss: the sub-type puts each expense into cost of goods sold, operating expenses or other expenses. It puts each income into operating revenue or other revenue. Cash Flow Statement: Asset accounts with the sub-type Cash, Bank, Wallet or Prepaid/debit card count as cash. An Asset or Liability account must have a sub-type. If an account has no sub-type, it shows Unclassified. Give it a sub-type on its account page. A Revenue or Expense account can have no sub-type. The reports then count it as operating.

Sales discounts, returns and allowances can use a Revenue account with the sub-type Contra operating revenue or Contra other revenue. These accounts normally have a debit balance. Profit & Loss shows their debit balances as deductions from revenue. Contra operating revenue reduces operating revenue; Contra other revenue reduces other revenue. Existing accounts keep their sub-types. To identify an existing contra account, edit its sub-type on the account page. Contra accounts cannot be the default Sales revenue or Uncategorised income.

Each account has a number, the account code. The field is Code. Each type has its own range of numbers: Type Codes Asset 1000–1999 Liability 2000–2999 Equity 3000–3999 Revenue 4000–4999 Expense 5000–5999 If you leave Code empty when you add an account, Akaun gives the lowest free number in the range.

A new book starts with these accounts. You can rename them, and you can add more. Code Name Type Sub-type 1000 Cash Asset Cash 1100 Bank Asset Bank 1200 Accounts Receivable Asset Accounts receivable 1300 Inventory Asset Inventory 1400 Marketplace Clearing Asset (none: Unclassified) 2000 Accounts Payable Liability Accounts payable 2100 Loans Liability (none: Unclassified) 3000 Owner's Equity Equity — 3100 Retained Earnings Equity — 4000 Product Sales Revenue Operating revenue 4100 Other Revenue Revenue Other revenue 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Expense Cost of goods sold 5100 Advertising Expense Operating expense 5200 Packaging Expense Operating expense 5300 Shipping Expense Operating expense 5400 Software Expense Operating expense 5500 Utilities Expense Operating expense 5900 Other Expenses Expense Other expense Akaun uses some of these accounts for special jobs: Bank is the account that new expenses and income use first. To change it, use Default transaction account in Settings, on the Ledger tab. On the Accounts screen, this account shows Default account. The General tab also has a Default payment account row, but at this time a change there is not kept. Accounts Receivable holds the receivables: the money that customers owe to the business. Accounts Payable holds the payables: the money that the business owes. By default, Owner's Equity is the other side of each opening balance. Marketplace Clearing and Loans show Unclassified. A loan can be short-term or long-term, so give Loans the correct sub-type.

If you do not use an account now, click Deactivate on its account page. Akaun keeps the account and all its records, but the record form does not show it. Click Reactivate to use it again. You cannot deactivate an account that Settings names as a default account. First choose a different default account. The Accounts screen hides inactive accounts. If there is an inactive account, the screen shows a button with the number of inactive accounts, for example Show inactive (2). Click it to see them. Click Hide inactive (2) to hide them again.

A contact is a person or a business that you work with. Akaun uses contacts to show who owes money, and to whom. This page tells how Akaun calculates the balance of each contact.

Each contact has an entity type: Individual or Business. A contact can also have one or more roles. The roles are Customer, Supplier, Employee and Partner. For example, a business that buys from you and also sells to you is a customer and a supplier. A contact can also have no role. A record can name one contact. A payment to several contacts names a contact on each allocation.

A record that uses Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable must name a contact. These two accounts hold the money that is owed. The contact tells who owes the money, or to whom it is owed. On such a record, the Contact field shows a star (*), and you cannot save the record without a contact. On all other records, the contact is optional.
documents.s: When a record must name a contact

documents.t: Akaun does not keep a separate account for each contact. It calculates the balance of a contact from the records that name the contact: The receivable is the money that the contact owes you. It comes from records on Accounts Receivable that are not paid yet. The payable is the money that you owe the contact. It comes from records on Accounts Payable that are not paid yet. Payments reduce the balance. You cannot type a balance. Thus the balance of a contact always agrees with the records. For example, a customer gets an invoice of 500.00 and pays 200.00. The balance of the customer is a receivable of 300.00. If a contact has a receivable and a payable at the same time, Akaun shows the difference as one balance.

The Contacts screen has a Balance column. Each balance has the tag Receivable (the contact owes you) or Payable (you owe the contact). A dash (—) shows that nothing is outstanding. If something is outstanding, the Contacts screen shows two totals under its title: Payables and Receivables. The page of a contact shows the balance at the top. The text beside it is Receivable, Payable or nothing outstanding either way. On the page of a contact, See everything with this contact opens the Records screen with only the records of this contact. You see balances only if you have the permission to see records.

Your book has one main currency. You can also record an expense, an income, a quotation or an invoice in a different currency. This page tells how Akaun changes a foreign amount into the main currency.

The main currency is the currency of your book. All amounts and all reports show in it. You choose it in Settings, on the General tab, in the Currency field. Choose the main currency before you add data. When the book has one record, quotation or invoice, Akaun locks the Currency field. A lock icon then shows beside it. A change of the main currency would make all the old amounts wrong.

On an expense or an income, click + Foreign currency. A Foreign currency box opens with these fields: Currency: the currency of the bill or the receipt. Amount (USD): the amount in that currency, as the bill shows it. The label shows the currency that you chose. Rate (1 USD = ? MYR): the number of units of the main currency for 1 unit of the foreign currency. The form shows + Foreign currency only when one of the two accounts is an expense category or an income category. A transfer, a payment, an opening balance or a journal entry is always in the main currency.
documents.s: A record in a foreign currency

documents.t: Akaun tries to find the exchange rate for the date of the record. It gets the rate from a free public rate service on the internet, and it keeps a copy of each rate that it finds. If you change the date, Akaun finds the rate again. If Akaun cannot find a rate, the form shows a message. An example is "No rate found for that date — enter it yourself." Then type the rate from your bank or your bill. You can also change a rate that Akaun found. Without a rate, the save bar shows "Enter the exchange rate before saving." and Akaun does not save the record. Akaun keeps the rate with the record. Later changes in the rate do not change the record.

Akaun calculates the amount in the main currency: the foreign amount multiplied by the rate. The Amount field of the record shows this result, and you cannot change it there. For example, the main currency is MYR. You pay a bill of 100.00 USD, and the rate is 4.50. The record amount is 450.00 MYR. The Records screen shows the main-currency amount. Under it, the screen shows the foreign amount and its currency.

A quotation and an invoice have their own Currency field and rate field. The line items and the PDF use the currency of the document. When you mark an invoice in a foreign currency as sent, Akaun records the amount in the main currency. It uses the rate of the invoice. A payment from the customer is always in the main currency. If the rate on the day of the payment is different, a few cents can stay outstanding on the invoice. Akaun has no account for exchange gains and losses, so it cannot clear this difference. See Invoices.
documents.s: A quotation or an invoice in a foreign currency

documents.t: All reports and all balances add the main-currency amounts. They never add foreign amounts. Thus a report total is always in one currency.
Record an expense or income Invoices Quotations Settings reference Prepare your book
Each record moves an amount out of one account and into a different account. This page tells how the record form shows this, and why it keeps each balance correct.

Each record has two lines. On the record form, the Journal entry section shows a Debit line and a Credit line. You choose one account for each line. The amount of the record goes out of the credit account and into the debit account. Debit: value goes into this account. Credit: value goes out of this account. For example, you buy printer paper for 50.00 with cash: Line Account Amount Debit An expense category, for example Office supplies 50.00 Credit Cash 50.00 The balance of Cash goes down by 50.00. The total of the expense category goes up by 50.00. Income works in the same way, but in the other direction. A customer pays you 200.00 into the bank. The debit is Bank. The credit is Product Sales. The income category is the place that the money came from. A transfer also has two lines. You move 100.00 from Bank to Cash. The debit is Cash. The credit is Bank.
documents.s: Two lines: a debit and a credit

documents.t: Sometimes one amount goes to more than one place. For example, one supplier bill of 80.00 is for fuel and for paper. Click + Add a line to add a line for each category. The form shows + Add a line only on an expense or an income, unless you have the Adjustments permission. On an expense or an income, each extra line is a category of the same kind. You type the amount of each category. Without the Adjustments permission, you can add only this type of line. Akaun keeps one record with all the lines. It is still an Expense or an Income. See Split across categories.

The total of the debits must be equal to the total of the credits. With two lines, this is always true, because both lines use the amount of the record. With more lines, the form shows the difference while you type. At the top of the Journal entry section, a label shows Balanced when the debits and the credits are equal. If they are not equal, it shows the difference, for example 5.00 apart. Then the save bar shows the reason, and Akaun does not save the record.

Each record adds the same amount to the debit side as it takes from the credit side. Thus the money in the book is always complete. Money cannot appear from nowhere, and it cannot disappear. Akaun calculates the balance of each account from its records. You cannot type a balance. If you change or delete a record, each balance that the record touches changes with it. Thus two screens cannot show two different balances for one account.
documents.s: Why this keeps each balance correct

documents.t: Most records match an everyday kind: an expense, an income, a transfer, a payment or an opening balance. Some records do not match one of these kinds. Examples: A record between two accounts that do not fit together as an everyday kind. For example, you receive a loan of 1,000.00 into the bank. The debit is Bank. The credit is Loans. A record with extra lines that are not an everyday split. For example, the lines include two cash or bank accounts, or an expense category and an income category. Akaun saves such a record as a Journal entry. To save a journal entry, you must have the Adjustments permission. info A journal entry needs the Adjustments permission. No group that Akaun creates gives this permission. A user with it can save a record between any two accounts. The record form then shows all accounts on each line. See Permissions explained. :::info For accountants Akaun is a double-entry system. The record form labels each line Debit or Credit. The lines of each record add up to zero. Akaun keeps each amount as a signed number: a debit is positive and a credit is negative. In the reports, Akaun shows each balance with its natural sign. Thus Liability, Equity and Revenue balances show as positive numbers. On the Accounts screen and on each account page, Akaun shows the stored sign. There, a credit balance shows with a minus sign. :::
documents.s: Records that need the Adjustments permission

Some changes to a record can make a different record wrong. Akaun locks a record to prevent this. This page tells when a record is locked, what you can still change, and how to unlock it.

A record is locked in these two cases: A payment settles some or all of the record. The payment record is also locked. A bank statement line matches the record. For example, a supplier bill is 300.00 and a payment of 300.00 settles it. If you change the bill to 250.00, the payment is then wrong. Thus Akaun locks the amount of the bill.

On a locked record, you cannot change these fields: The amount. The date. The currency and the exchange rate. The accounts. On an expense or an income, only the cash or bank account is locked. The category is not locked. You also cannot delete a locked record.

On a locked record, you can still change these fields: The description. The contact. The reference. The remark. The attachments. On an expense or an income, the category, and the extra lines of a split. A change to these fields cannot make a payment or a bank match wrong.

On the Records screen, a lock icon shows beside the description. Put the pointer on the icon to see the reason. On the record page, a note above the form gives the reason. The locked fields are read only. On the record page, Delete is not available. Put the pointer on it to see the reason. The reason tells you what to undo. For example: "A payment has settled this record. Undo the settlement before changing its amount, date or the account it moved through."
documents.s: How Akaun shows a locked record

documents.t: Trusted users with both Edit records and the separately granted Correct settled dates permission can use Correct date on a settled expense or income record. This action is available only in the browser, and only when the record has no bank statement matches. Payment records and records created by issuing an invoice cannot use it. Save or discard other edits first. Enter the corrected date and a reason of 10–500 characters, then review and confirm. Moving between calendar months or years requires an extra acknowledgement. Both dates, your reason, and who made the correction are saved in History. The correction preserves payment allocations and payment dates. It changes the accounting date, so reports and historical balances can change. Do not use it for a finalized period without consulting the person responsible for your accounts. Akaun does not enforce a closed-books cutoff for this action. Ordinary date editing remains locked.

Remove each thing that locks the record: If a payment settles the record, click the undo icon (Reverse allocation) beside the payment. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid. If a bank statement line matches the record, remove the match on the reconciliation screen of the account. See Bank reconciliation. When nothing settles or matches the record, it is unlocked. You can then change all of its fields.

When you mark an invoice as sent, Akaun makes an Invoice record. This record belongs to the invoice: All fields on its record page are read only. A note above the form says "This record was created by issuing an invoice. Change it on the invoice instead." Delete on its record page is disabled. Put the pointer on it to see the reason: "Cancel the invoice instead". A delete of many records on the Records list does not delete it. Akaun deletes the other selected records and shows the reason. The Invoice card in the rail opens the invoice. On the invoice page, you can still change the due date, the reference, the notes and the terms. You cannot change the customer, the issue date, the currency or the lines. To remove the Invoice record from the books, cancel the invoice. See Cancel an invoice.

Some records are paid when they happen. Other records stay outstanding until a payment comes later. This page tells how Akaun knows which records are paid.

A record that moves money straight from a cash or bank account is paid when you save it. For example, you pay 50.00 from Bank for software. The record shows Paid immediately. A record that uses Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable is outstanding. The money did not move yet: Accounts Payable holds the payables. A payable is money that the business owes to a contact. For example, a supplier sends a bill of 300.00, and you pay it next month. Accounts Receivable holds the receivables. A receivable is money that a contact owes to the business. For example, you send an invoice of 500.00 to a customer. Such a record must name a contact. Akaun then knows who owes the money, or to whom the business owes it. See Contacts and their balances.
documents.s: Paid now, or outstanding until later

documents.t: Each record has one of these statuses. The page of a transfer shows no status. Status What it shows Outstanding Nobody paid any of the amount yet. Partially paid Payments cover some of the amount, but not all of it. The record page shows the amount that is still outstanding. Paid Payments cover the full amount, or the record did not use Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable. The Records screen has a tab for each status: All, Outstanding, Partially paid and Paid.

You cannot mark a record as paid. Akaun calculates the status from the payments against the record. Thus the status on each screen is always the same. A payment is a record of its own. It moves money out of a cash or bank account and puts it against one or more outstanding records. The part of a payment that goes against one record is an allocation. When you record a payment, the Allocation section shows each outstanding record and its allocation. For example, a supplier bill is 300.00. You pay 100.00. The bill shows Partially paid, with 200.00 outstanding. Later you pay 200.00. The bill then shows Paid. A payment cannot put more against a record than the amount that is outstanding on it.

One payment can settle many records. For example, a supplier sends three bills in one month. You pay all three with one bank transfer. One payment can also settle records of many contacts. In the Payee field (or the Payer field), choose Batch (several contacts). On the Records screen, Pay all payables opens a payment for all contacts that the business owes money to. On the page of a record, the rail shows Payments applied: each payment that settles the record. On the page of a payment, the rail shows Allocated to: each record that the payment settles.

If a payment is on the wrong record, reverse the allocation. On the record page or the payment page, click the undo icon (Reverse allocation) beside the allocation. The record is then Outstanding or Partially paid again. To do this, you must have the permission to delete records. Reverse allocation removes the allocation only. The payment record stays. Its money still moved out of the cash or bank account.
Paid tells that the money moved. Reconciled tells that a bank statement line matches the record. A record can be paid and Unreconciled. See Bank reconciliation.

A record is one event with money. Each record tells where the money came from and where it went. This page tells what a record is and which kinds of record Akaun keeps.

Akaun keeps all records in one list. The Records screen shows each expense, income, transfer, payment, opening balance, invoice and journal entry. Expenses and income are not in separate lists. To see one kind only, use the Kind filter on the Records screen. Each record names at least two accounts. Money goes out of one account and into a different account. For example, you pay 50.00 from Bank for a software subscription. The money came out of Bank and went into Software.
documents.s: One list of everything that happened

documents.t: The kind tells what a record is. The Records screen shows the kind of each record in the Kind column. There are seven kinds: Kind What it is When you see it Expense Money that the business spends. Money goes out of a cash or bank account, or out of Accounts Payable, into an expense category or into a thing that you buy and keep. Income Money that the business earns. Money comes from an income category into a cash or bank account, or into Accounts Receivable. Transfer Money that moves between two of your own accounts. Money goes from one cash or bank account into a different cash or bank account, for example from Bank to Cash. Payment Money that pays an amount that is owed. Money goes out of a cash or bank account to pay a payable. Or money from a customer comes into a cash or bank account to pay a receivable. Opening balance The money in an account on the day that you start to use Akaun. You give an account an opening balance on its account page. Invoice The amount that a customer owes for an invoice. You mark an invoice as sent. Akaun makes this record for you. If you cancel the invoice, Akaun removes it. Journal entry A record that does not fit the other kinds. Usually it is a correction. The accounts on the record do not match an everyday kind, or the record has extra lines that are not an everyday split. A cash or bank account is an account where money is kept, for example Cash or Bank. A category tells what the money was for. See Accounts and categories.

The record form does not ask for the kind. It asks for two accounts: the account on the Debit line, and the account on the Credit line. Akaun finds the kind from the two accounts that you choose. For example, money goes out of Bank and into Software. Software is an expense category, so the record is an Expense. Money goes out of Bank and into Cash. Both are cash or bank accounts, so the record is a Transfer. If you change an account on a record, Akaun finds the kind again. A Journal entry needs the Adjustments permission. See How a record moves money.
documents.s: You do not choose the kind

documents.t: Click a record on the Records screen to open its page. The page shows the amount, the status, the accounts and the details of the record. It also shows the contact, the payments, the attachments and the History of the record. Each record page has its own web address. Copy the address from the browser to share the record with a different user. That user must have permission to see records.
documents.s: Each record has its own page

A contact is a person or a business that you work with, for example a customer or a supplier. Use the Contacts screen to add contacts, change their details, see what they owe and merge duplicate contacts. To learn how Akaun calculates the balance of a contact, read Contacts and their balances. info To add a contact, you need the Add permission on contacts. To change one, you need Change. To delete one, you need Delete. To find duplicates or merge contacts, you need Merge, Change and Delete.

Open Contacts to see all contacts in name order. Each row shows the name, the type, the roles and the email. A contact without a role shows no roles. The tabs above the list filter it by role: All Customer Supplier Employee Partner A contact with two roles shows on both tabs. To find a contact, use these controls: Type: choose All types, Individual or Business. The search box (Search name, email, reg no…): type a part of the name, the email or the registration number. Clear: removes the type filter and the search, and selects the All tab again. Clear shows only when a type filter or a search is active.

If you have the permission to see records, the list also shows the Balance column. Each balance shows Receivable or Payable. Receivable is money that the contact owes to the business. Payable is money that the business owes to the contact. A dash (—) shows that nothing is outstanding. Under the title, the screen shows two totals: Payables: the total that the business owes to all contacts. Receivables: the total that all contacts owe to the business. The totals show only when one of them is more than zero.

On the Contacts screen, click New contact. The Add contact panel opens. In Entity type, click Individual or Business. In Legal name, type the name of the contact. Optional: in Roles, click each role that applies: Customer, Supplier, Employee or Partner. Optional: type the Registration no., the Email and the Phone. Optional: type the Address. Optional: in Remark, type a note for your team. Click Create contact. Create contact is not available until you choose an Entity type. Akaun adds the contact to the list and closes the panel. The Partner role does not make accounts for the partner. The Partners' Equity report uses it to divide the profit. See Partners' Equity. tip You can also add a customer when you write a quotation or an invoice. In Customer, type the new name and click Create "…". The button shows the name that you typed. When you save, Akaun adds the contact as a Business with the Customer role. You need the Add permission on contacts. The Contact field on a record has the same button.

Click a contact on the list to open its page. At the top, the page shows the entity type, the roles and the name. If you have the permission to see records, it also shows the balance. The text beside the balance is Receivable, Payable or nothing outstanding either way. The page has these sections: Contact details: Entity type, Legal name and Roles. Contact information: Email, Phone, Registration no., Address and Remark. Contact ledger (in the rail): See everything with this contact, with the number of records and invoices. Click it to open the Records screen with only the records of this contact. History (in the rail): who made each change, and when.

Open the contact. Change the fields in Contact details or Contact information. A bar shows at the bottom of the page. Click Save changes. To stop without a change, click Discard. A change to the name shows on all records, quotations and invoices of the contact. A PDF that you print after the change shows the new details.

Duplicate contacts split the records and the balance of one customer or supplier into two. Use Find duplicates to find them. On the Contacts screen, click Find duplicates. The Duplicate contacts panel opens. Akaun puts contacts in one group when they have one of these items in common: Same name: Akaun ignores capitals, punctuation and extra spaces. Same email: Akaun ignores capitals. Same phone: Akaun compares only the digits. Same registration no.: Akaun ignores capitals. Akaun does not compare the entity type or the roles. Each group shows the reasons under its name. If no contacts match, the panel shows No duplicates found. If a group is not a set of duplicates, click Not duplicates. Akaun hides the group from the panel. The group shows again the next time that you click Find duplicates.

When you merge contacts, you keep one contact. Akaun moves the records, quotations and invoices of the other contacts to the contact that you keep. The comparison table shows each contact in a column. Akaun marks each row that has different values. The Usage row shows the number of records of each contact. caution You cannot undo a merge. Akaun deletes the other contacts permanently. Akaun merges the contacts immediately when you click Merge into selected. No dialog asks you to confirm. In the group, at the top of the column, select the contact that you keep. Below the table, Akaun tells you which contact it keeps and which contacts it deletes. If records move, it also tells you how many. Read this text. Click Merge into selected. Merge into selected is not available until you select a contact. Akaun merges the contacts. In the Duplicate contacts panel, Akaun removes the group. The Merge selected contacts panel closes. After the merge, the contact that you keep has these values: All roles of all the merged contacts. Its own Registration no., Email, Phone and Address. If one of these is empty, Akaun copies it from a merged contact. Its own Remark. Akaun does not copy the remark of a merged contact.

Use this when Akaun does not put two contacts in one group, for example two different spellings of one name. On the Contacts list, select the check box of each contact to merge. In the bar at the bottom, click Merge selected (2). The number is the number of contacts that you selected. The button is not available until you select two or more contacts. The Merge selected contacts panel opens. Do the steps in Merge contacts.

You can delete a contact only when nothing names it: no record, no quotation and no invoice. If something names the contact, Delete is not available. Point to it to see the reason. To remove a duplicate that has records, merge it into the correct contact. caution You cannot undo a delete. Akaun removes the contact permanently. Open the contact. Click Delete. In the dialog, click Delete.

At this time, the screen cannot archive a contact. The tooltip on Delete says "Archive it instead", but the screen has no control for it. Not duplicates is not saved. When you select Partner in the Add contact panel, a note says that the partner gets two accounts. At this time, Akaun does not make these accounts. You see balances only if you have the permission to see records.

Attach a receipt, a bill or a statement to a record as proof. You can attach files when you make the record, or later on the page of the record. A record can have many attachments.

PDF, JPEG and PNG files only. Akaun checks the content of the file, not only its name. Each file can be 15 MB or smaller. The server also has an upload limit. If that limit is lower than 15 MB, a large file does not upload. Ask your administrator to check it. See Environment variables.

On the New record page, find the Attachments section on the right. Click Add, or click Drop files here or click to add. Choose one or more files. You can also drag the files from your computer into the Attachments section. Complete the record. Click Save record. Akaun keeps the files in a list until you save. It uploads them only after it saves the record. The list shows the name and the size of each file. To remove a file before you save, click the X beside it. If you click Discard on the save bar, Akaun also removes the files from the list.
documents.s: Attach files to a new record

documents.t: Open the record. In the rail on the right, find the Attachments section. Click Add. Choose one or more files. Akaun uploads each file immediately. You do not click a save button. You can also drag files into the Attachments section.
documents.s: Attach files to a record that you saved

documents.t: Open the record. In Attachments, click the name of the file. The file opens in a new tab.
caution Akaun deletes the attachment when you click X. It does not ask you to confirm. To get the file back, you must attach it again. Open the record. In Attachments, click the X beside the file.
The Attachments section shows each file with its date. The History section of the record shows each file that was added or deleted, and who did it. A new change shows there after you reload the page.

You can attach and delete files on a locked record. A receipt does not change the amounts. See Locked records. To attach a file to a saved record, you need the Change permission on Records. The Add button shows also without this permission, but the upload fails with no message. To delete a file, you need the Delete permission on Records. Without it, the X is greyed out. If a file does not upload after you save a new record, Akaun saves the record without it. A message tells you how many files did not upload. Open the record and attach them again. On the page of a saved record, Akaun does not show a message when an upload fails. If the file is not in the list after the upload, check its type and its size. Akaun can read the text of some attached files. The search box on the Records screen then finds the record by that text. See Find records. To make a record from a receipt automatically, use Auto Import. See Import receipts.
Record an expense or income Change, delete or undo a record

A bill that you pay later is a payable: an expense that the business owes. Akaun keeps it on Accounts Payable until a payment settles it. This page tells how such a bill gets into Akaun and how you pay it. Read Outstanding, partially paid and paid first. It tells what Outstanding, Partially paid and Paid mean.

At this time, Auto Import is the way to record a bill that you pay later. When Auto Import reads a receipt or a bill, it prepares an expense. The Source account of the expense is Accounts Payable by default. The item also names the supplier as its contact. When you confirm the item, Akaun saves an expense that is Outstanding. Import the bill. See Import receipts. On the review card, make sure that Source account shows Accounts Payable. Make sure that the contact is the supplier that you owe. Confirm the item. See Review and confirm. If you change Source account to a cash or bank account, for example Bank, the expense is Paid when you save it. info The New record form does not offer Accounts Payable to a user without the Adjustments permission. Thus you cannot record a bill to pay later by hand. Use Auto Import.
documents.s: How a bill to pay later gets into Akaun

documents.t: When the business has payables, the Records screen shows the Outstanding payables panel above the list. It shows the number of contacts and the total. On the Records screen, find the Outstanding payables panel. Click View details. A panel opens with one group for each contact. Each group shows the total and each bill that is outstanding. Click a bill to open its page. You can also click the Outstanding tab or the Partially paid tab on the Records screen.

On the Records screen, in the Outstanding payables panel, click View details. Find the group of the contact. Click Record a payment. The Record a payment page opens. Who shows One contact, and Payee shows the contact. In Description, type a description, for example "Payment to supplier, March". In Date, choose the date of the payment. In Payment account, choose the account that the money came out of. In Allocation, select the check box of each bill that this payment pays. Akaun puts the full outstanding amount of each bill in its amount box. If the payment pays only part of a bill, change the amount in its box. Check Amount. Akaun adds the ticked amounts for you. Optional: in Details, type a Reference and a Remark. Click Save. If Amount is more than the ticked amounts, the Allocation section shows the part that is not put against a bill.
documents.s: Pay the bills of one contact

documents.t: Use this when one bank transfer pays bills of more than one contact. On the Records screen, in the Outstanding payables panel, click Pay all payables. Who shows Batch (several contacts). Allocation shows each outstanding bill of each contact, and all of them are selected. In Allocation, clear the check box of each bill that you do not pay now. If you pay only part of a bill, change the amount in its box. In Description, type a description. In Date, choose the date of the payment. In Payment account, choose the account that the money came out of. Click Save. tip Select all and Select none at the top of Allocation select or clear all bills at once. With Batch (several contacts), you cannot type Amount. It is always the total of the selected bills.
documents.s: Pay the bills of many contacts at once

documents.t: Akaun saves a Payment record and opens its page. The rail of the payment shows Allocated to: each bill that the payment pays, and the amount for each bill. Each bill changes its status: Paid if the payment covers the full amount. Partially paid if the payment covers only part of it. The bill page shows the amount that is still outstanding. The page of each bill shows Payments applied in its rail. The bill is now locked. See Locked records.

Pay all payables shows only when the business owes money to more than one contact. The Outstanding payables panel shows only the payables. It does not show the receivables (the money that customers owe to the business). To pay a bill, you need the Add permission on Records. If you have only one cash or bank account, Payment account does not show. Akaun uses that account. To remove a payment from a bill, see Change, delete or undo a record. To record money that a customer pays you, see Getting paid.
Outstanding, partially paid and paid Contacts and their balances Review and confirm Locked records
Use this page to correct a record, to delete it, or to remove a payment from it. You change a record on its own page.
documents.s: Change, delete or undo a record

documents.t: On the Records screen, click the record. Change the fields that are wrong. A save bar shows at the bottom of the page. It shows Unsaved changes, Discard and Save changes. Click Save changes. To remove your changes, click Discard. The fields then show the saved values again. If the save bar shows a message in place of Unsaved changes, the record cannot be saved yet. Read the message and correct the form.

Akaun saves the changes. The History section in the rail shows a new line. It tells who made the change, when, and which fields changed. Akaun finds the kind again from the accounts. For example, if you change the Debit line of an expense from a category to Cash, the record becomes a Transfer.

If you click a link or Records before you save, Akaun shows Leave without saving?. Click Discard and leave to leave the page. Akaun does not save your changes. Click Cancel to stay on the page. caution If you reload the page or close the browser tab, Akaun does not warn you. Your changes are lost. Save first.
documents.s: If you leave the page before you save

documents.t: Some fields are read only in these cases: If the record is locked, the amount, the date, the currency and the cash or bank account are read only. A payment settles the record, or a bank statement line matches it. A note above the form gives the reason. See Locked records. If the record is a payment, you can change only the description, the reference and the remark. To correct a payment, click Reverse allocation on each allocation. Then delete the payment and record a new one. If the record came from an invoice, change the invoice, not the record. The note above the form says "This record was created by issuing an invoice. Change it on the invoice instead." See Invoices. If you do not have the Change permission on Records, all fields are read only. On a locked expense or income, you can still change the description, the contact, the reference, the remark, the attachments and the categories.

You can delete a record only when it is not locked. If Delete is not available, put the pointer on it to see the reason. caution You cannot undo a delete. Akaun removes the record and all of its lines. Each balance that the record touched changes. Open the record. At the top right of the page, click Delete. In Delete this record?, click Delete. Akaun deletes the record and shows the Records screen.

caution You cannot undo a delete. Check the selected records before you confirm. On the Records screen, select the check box of each record. A bar at the bottom shows the number of records and their total. On the bar, click Delete. In Delete these records?, click Delete. For one record, the dialog is Delete this record?. Akaun does not delete a locked record. If the selection has locked records, the dialog tells you how many. Akaun deletes the other records. Akaun also does not delete an Invoice record. Akaun deletes the other records and shows the reason. To remove an Invoice record, cancel its invoice. See Cancel an invoice. To select all records in the list, click the check box at the top of the list.

Use this when a payment is on the wrong bill. Reverse allocation removes the allocation only. The payment record stays, and its money still moved out of the cash or bank account. caution Akaun removes the allocation when you click the button. It does not ask you to confirm. Open the bill or the payment. In the rail, find Payments applied (on a bill) or Allocated to (on a payment). On the row of the allocation, click the undo arrow. Its tooltip is Reverse allocation. The bill is Outstanding or Partially paid again. If nothing else locks the bill, you can change it again. A payment with no contact, which pays several people at once, must always be spent in full. When you reverse one of its allocations, Akaun reverses all of them, and all of its bills are outstanding again. To use the money of the payment for a different bill, record a new payment. See Bills you pay later.
documents.s: Remove a payment from a record

documents.t: Open the record. In the rail, find History. Each line shows the user, the change and the time. The list shows changes to the fields and to the attachments.
documents.s: See the history of a record

documents.t: To change a record, you need the Change permission on Records. To delete a record or to click Reverse allocation, you need the Delete permission on Records. Without it, Delete and Reverse allocation do not show. To delete a payment that pays a bill, first click Reverse allocation on each allocation. If a bank statement line matches the record, remove the match first. See Bank reconciliation.
Locked records Outstanding, partially paid and paid Find records Attach receipts and documents
The Records screen shows the records of all kinds in one list. See Records for the kinds. This page tells how to find one record, or a group of records, in the list.

Under the title, the screen shows the number of records. Below it, four cards show totals: Card What it shows Income The total and the number of records with an income category. Expenses The total and the number of records with an expense category or equipment. Outstanding The amount that is still outstanding, and the number of records that are not fully settled. All records The number of records. When a tab, a filter or a search is active, the card shows Records shown. The cards always count the records that the list shows. When you use a filter, the cards change. The list has these columns: Item, Kind, Accounts, Status, Date and Amount. Item shows the description and the record number. A lock icon shows beside a locked record. Put the pointer on the icon to see the reason. See Locked records. Kind shows the kind and the contact. Accounts shows the credit account (the money came out of it) and the debit account (the money went into it). A record with more than two lines shows the number of lines, for example 3 lines. Status shows Outstanding, Partially paid or Paid. Unreconciled shows when bank statement lines do not yet match the full amount of the record. Amount shows an income with a plus sign (+). A foreign amount also shows in its own currency.
Above the list, click a tab to show the records with one status: All Outstanding Partially paid Paid Each tab shows the number of records that it contains. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.

Click the search box. It shows Search description, contact, ref…. Type a word or a number. The search finds text in the description, the contact, the reference, the remark, the record number and the account names. It also finds text in attached files when Akaun can read them. On a phone, click the search icon first.

The filters are above the list. You can use more than one filter at the same time. Filter What it does Unreconciled Shows only the records that show Unreconciled. Click it again to remove the filter. Kind Shows one or more kinds, for example Expense and Transfer. Contact Shows the records of one contact. Account Shows the records that use one account. See See the statement of one account. Category Shows the records that use one or more categories. A split record shows under each of its categories. Date Shows the records from one date (From) to a different date (To). Amount Shows the records between a smallest amount (Min) and a largest amount (Max). To remove one filter, open it and click Clear. To remove all filters, the search and the tab, click Clear beside the filters. This button shows only when a filter or a search is active. Below the filters, the screen shows Showing with the number of records, and the Filtered total. On a phone, click Filters, choose the filters, and then click Show results. The phone panel has the Category, Date range and Amount range filters only.
Click a column title to sort the list by that column: Item, Kind, Status, Date or Amount. Click the title again to change the order. By default, the list shows the newest records first.

When you filter by one account, the screen shows the statement of that account. The statement shows each transaction in date order, with a running balance. On the Records screen, click Account. Choose the account, for example Bank. Optional: click Date and choose a date range. The statement shows: Opening balance: the balance before the first row. A table with Date, Description, Amount and Balance. Balance is the running balance after each row. Closing balance: the balance after the last row. You can also open the statement from the page of an account. In the Account ledger card, click View account ledger. The statement shows only with the Account filter and an optional date range.
