If you add a different filter, a search or a tab, the screen shows the normal list. If you sort by a column that is not Date, the running balance does not show. The screen then tells you to sort by date and clear the other filters. The running balance disappears for a reason. A balance of only some records looks like the real balance of the account, but it is not.
documents.s: See the statement of one account

documents.t: Show the statement of one account. See See the statement of one account. Optional: choose a date range with Date. Click Export CSV. Your browser downloads a CSV file of the statement. info Export CSV is available only on the statement of one account. You cannot export the full list of records.

Each record has its own address. To share a record, open it and copy the address from your browser. A different user can open the address if they have the View permission on Records. The address of the Records screen also keeps the filters, the search and the tab. Copy it to share a filtered list. tip To open a record in a new browser tab, hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) and click its description.
documents.s: Share a record or a list

documents.t: The screen loads the newest 1,000 records. If there are more, the bottom of the list says so, for example "Showing the 1000 most recent of 1250". Use the search to find an older record. Paid and reconciled are different. A record can show Paid and Unreconciled at the same time. See Bank reconciliation.
Records Outstanding, partially paid and paid Change, delete or undo a record

Use a transfer when money moves between two of your own cash or bank accounts. For example, you take 100.00 out of the bank as cash. A transfer is not an expense or an income. It does not change the profit of the business. You use the same New record form as for an expense. Akaun saves the record as a Transfer when both lines are cash or bank accounts. You do not need the Adjustments permission.

This example moves 100.00 from Bank to Cash. On the Records screen, click New record. In Description, type a description, for example "Cash withdrawal". In Amount, type 100.00. In Date, choose the date of the transfer. On the Credit line, choose Bank. On the Debit line, choose Cash. Click Save record.

Akaun saves the record and opens its page. The top of the page shows Transfer. The balance of Bank goes down by 100.00. The balance of Cash goes up by 100.00. A transfer has no status on its page. Nobody owes money for a transfer. On the Records screen, the Kind column shows Transfer. The Accounts column shows Bank, an arrow, and Cash. A transfer does not count in the Income card or the Expenses card.
You move money from a marketplace account into the bank: credit Marketplace Clearing, debit Bank. You put cash into the bank: credit Cash, debit Bank.

The two lines must use two different accounts. A transfer is always in the main currency. The + Foreign currency button does not show on a transfer. A transfer has two lines only. Without the Adjustments permission, + Add a line does not show. With it, a record with a third line saves as a Journal entry, not a transfer. Accounts Payable, Loans and an account with the sub-type Credit card are not cash or bank accounts. Without the Adjustments permission, the form does not offer these accounts. Equipment is an asset, but it is not a cash or bank account. Money out of Bank into equipment is an Expense, not a transfer. See Accounts and categories. To match a transfer to a bank statement, see Bank reconciliation.
Record an expense or income How a record moves money Records

Use this page to record money that the business spends or earns. You use the same form for both. You do not choose the kind of record. Akaun finds the kind from the two accounts that you choose. To learn how a record moves money, read How a record moves money. info To make a record, you need the Add permission on Records. Without it, the Records screen does not show New record. See Permissions explained.

The New record page has three sections: Section What you type in it Transaction details Description, Amount and Date. The Amount label also shows the symbol of your main currency. Journal entry Two lines. The Credit line is the account that the money came out of. The Debit line is the account that the money went into. Details Contact, Reference and Remark. These fields are optional. The Attachments section is on the right side of the page. On a narrow screen, it is below the form. When the page opens, Akaun puts an account on each line. The Credit line gets your default payment account. The Debit line gets the first different account in its list. This account is often a cash or bank account, not a category. Always check both lines before you save.

This example records 50.00 that you pay from Bank for software. On the Records screen, click New record. In Description, type what you bought, for example "Accounting software, March". In Amount, type 50.00. In Date, choose the date of the payment. On the Credit line, choose Bank. On the Debit line, choose the expense category Software. Optional: in Contact, choose the supplier. Optional: in Reference, type the number of the receipt or the bill. Optional: in Remark, type a note. Optional: add the receipt. See Attach receipts and documents. Click Save record.

This example records 200.00 that a customer pays you in cash. On the Records screen, click New record. In Description, type what you sold, for example "Order 1042". In Amount, type 200.00. In Date, choose the date when you got the money. On the Credit line, choose the income category Product Sales. On the Debit line, choose Cash. Optional: in Contact, choose the customer. Click Save record. For an income, the income category is the credit. The income category is the place that the money came from.

Akaun saves the record and opens its page. The top of the page shows the kind, the date, the amount and the status. A record that moves money directly from a cash or bank account shows Paid. The record is also on the Records screen. The Kind column shows Expense or Income.

The Contact field searches your contacts while you type. It shows only contacts with the role that fits the record: For an expense, it shows contacts with the role Supplier. For an income, it shows contacts with the role Customer. If the contact is not in the list, click Create "…". The button shows the name that you typed, for example Create "Kedai Ali". Akaun makes the new contact when you save the record. The new contact gets the role that the list uses. If a contact does not have that role, it is not in the list. Add the role on the contact page first. If you click Create "…" for that name, Akaun makes a second contact. To make a new contact here, you need the Add permission on Contacts. If you have no contacts yet, the Contact field does not show. See Contacts.

The + Foreign currency button shows on an expense or an income. Click + Foreign currency. In Currency, choose the currency. In the second Amount field, type the amount in that currency. Check the Rate field. Akaun finds the rate for the date of the record. If Akaun finds no rate, type the rate. The first Amount field then shows the amount in your main currency. See Foreign currency.

The default payment account is the account that the Credit line gets on a new record. You choose it in Settings, on the Ledger tab, in Default transaction account. The General tab also shows Default payment account, but at this time a change there is not kept. See Settings reference.

If the save bar shows a message in place of Unsaved changes, the record cannot be saved yet. Read the message and correct the form. If Akaun cannot save the record, a red message shows at the top of the page. It tells you what to change. The two lines must use two different accounts. Without the Adjustments permission, each line offers cash or bank accounts and categories only. You cannot choose Accounts Payable, a loan account or a Credit card account on a new record. To pay a bill later, see Bills you pay later. To put one amount on more than one category, see Split a record across categories. To move money between two of your own accounts, see Move money between your accounts.
Records How a record moves money Accounts and categories Change, delete or undo a record

Use a split when one amount is for more than one category. For example, one supplier bill of 80.00 is for packaging and for shipping. You make one record with one line for each category. Read How a record moves money first if lines are new to you.

Without the Adjustments permission, you can save these splits: An expense: one cash or bank account, and two or more expense categories. An income: one income category or more, and one cash or bank account. Akaun keeps such a record as an Expense or an Income. You need the Adjustments permission for all other splits. Examples: The lines include two cash or bank accounts. The lines include an expense category and an income category. Akaun saves such a record as a Journal entry. See Permissions explained. info Without the Adjustments permission, the form offers only the lines that you can save. A new line on an expense offers expense categories. A new line on an income offers income categories. The list does not show a category that the record already uses.

This example records a bill of 80.00 from Bank: 50.00 for Packaging and 30.00 for Shipping. On the Records screen, click New record. In Description, type a description of the bill. In Amount, type the full amount, 80.00. In Date, choose the date of the bill. On the Credit line, choose Bank. On the Debit line, choose Packaging. In Journal entry, click + Add a line. On the Debit line for Packaging, change the amount from 80.00 to 50.00. On the new line, click Choose an account. Choose Shipping. In the amount box of the new line, type 30.00. Make sure that the top of Journal entry shows Balanced. Click Save record. tip If part of the amount is not on a line yet, a small arrow button shows in the amount box of the last line. Its tooltip gives the amount, for example Use the remaining 30.00. Click it to put that amount on the line.

The top of Journal entry shows the state of the lines: Balanced shows that the debits are equal to the credits. A figure with apart, for example 5.00 apart, shows the difference. The bottom of Journal entry also shows the difference as a number. While the debits and the credits are not equal, the save bar tells you why the record cannot be saved. For example: "Debits and credits do not balance. Difference: 5.00."
documents.s: How the form shows the difference

documents.t: When a record has more than two lines, each category line has a box below it: Label (optional) — defaults to the description. Type a label to describe that part of the bill, for example "Boxes". If you leave it empty, the line uses the description of the record.
documents.s: Give a line its own label

documents.t: Click the X at the end of the line. When you remove the last extra line, the record has two lines again. The category line then gets the full amount of the record again.

Akaun saves one record. The Kind column on the Records screen shows Expense or Income. The Accounts column shows the number of lines, for example 3 sides. The Category filter finds the record under each of its categories.

Without the Adjustments permission, + Add a line shows only when one line is an expense category or an income category. With the Adjustments permission, it shows on all records. Each line must have an account and an amount that is not zero. If not, the save bar shows "Pick an account for every side." or "A side of a record cannot be worth nothing." The money line always has the full amount of the record. You do not type its amount. On a locked expense or income, you can still change the categories and the split. See Locked records.
Record an expense or income How a record moves money Change, delete or undo a record
This page tells you about the parts of the Akaun screen. Read it after your first sign-in. It applies to all screens in Akaun.
After you sign in, Akaun opens the Records screen. If you cannot see records, Akaun opens the Dashboard. If you cannot see the Dashboard either, Akaun opens Settings.

On a computer, the sidebar is on the left side of the screen. From the top to the bottom, it has these parts. Workspace shows the main screens: Dashboard Records Quotations Invoices Contacts Auto Import Accounts Reports You see only the screens that you have the View permission for. A superuser sees all of them. You can change the order on your profile. See Choose your navigation. The number next to Records is the number of expense records that are not fully paid. Bank reconciliation has no item in the sidebar. To reconcile an account, open the account and click Reconcile. See Bank reconciliation. Administration shows Users & Groups. Only a superuser sees this part. See Users and groups. Below these parts are three more items: Settings opens the settings of the book. It shows only if you have the View permission on Settings. See Settings reference. Light or Dark shows the current theme. Click it to change to the other theme. Collapse makes the sidebar narrow, with icons only. To make it wide again, click the arrow at the same position. On a small screen, such as a tablet, the sidebar is narrow at the start. At the bottom, the sidebar shows your name and email. Click the user menu button (three dots) next to your name to open the user menu: Profile opens your profile. See Your profile. Sign out ends your sign-in on this browser. Under your name, the sidebar shows the version of Akaun, for example v0.1.7. Give this version when you report a problem.

On a screen narrower than 768 pixels, Akaun does not show the sidebar. It shows these items instead: The bottom bar. It shows up to five main screens. At the start, it shows Dashboard, Records and Auto Import, if you can see them. The menu button (☰) at the top left. It opens a menu with the other main screens under More. The menu also has Settings, the theme item (Light mode or Dark mode), Users & Groups for a superuser, Profile and Sign out.

You can choose the order of the main screens, and the screens on the bottom bar. Open the user menu and click Profile. Click the Navigation tab. To change the order, drag an item by its handle. For each screen that you want on the bottom bar, select Show on mobile. You can select five screens or fewer. Click Save changes. Akaun shows Navigation order saved. The sidebar and the bottom bar use the new order.

You can open Akaun from an icon on the home screen of your phone, as an app. Open the address of Akaun in the browser of the phone. Sign in. In the menu of the browser, choose the item that adds the page to the home screen. Its name is different in each browser, for example "Add to Home Screen" or "Install app". The Akaun icon shows on the home screen. Akaun opens in its own window, on the Dashboard. If you cannot see the Dashboard, Akaun opens Settings. Akaun does not work offline. The phone must connect to your Akaun server. Some browsers show the install item only for an HTTPS address.
documents.s: Add Akaun to the home screen of a phone

documents.t: Akaun shows the changes of other users without a reload. This also applies to your changes in a different browser tab. These screens update live: Records, Contacts, Accounts, Quotations, Invoices, Dashboard and Auto Import. If the connection to the server stops, the browser connects again by itself. If a list does not look correct, reload the page.

Each main screen starts with a list, for example the list of records. On the Records screen, the filters are part of the address in the browser. You can copy the address to give the same list to a different user. The first cell of each row is a link. Click the row to open the item. To open the item in a new browser tab, hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) and click the link. You can also click the link with the middle mouse button.

Each record, account, contact, quotation and invoice has its own page and its own address. You can copy the address and send it to a different user. That user also needs the permission to see the item. On a wide screen, the page has two columns. The left column shows the item. The right column shows the related items, for example the attachments, the payments and the History. On a narrow screen, the two columns show one above the other.

You change an item directly on its page. There is no separate edit screen. Open the item. Change the fields. In the save bar at the bottom of the page, click Save changes. On some pages, the button is Save. The save bar shows only after you change a field. It shows Unsaved changes. To remove your changes, click Discard. If the fields do not let you type, you do not have the Change permission, or the record is locked. See Locked records.
documents.s: Change an item on its page

documents.t: If you go to a different page in Akaun before you save, Akaun shows Leave without saving?. Click Cancel to stay on the page and keep your changes. Click Discard and leave to lose your changes and go to the other page. The Settings page asks the same question with different labels: Keep editing and Discard changes. Akaun does not ask when you reload the page or close the browser tab. Your changes are then lost. Save before you do this.
documents.s: Leave a page with unsaved changes

documents.t: A new record, payment, quotation or invoice opens on a full page. After you save it, Akaun opens the page of the new item. A payment that you start from an invoice is different: after you save it, Akaun opens the invoice again. A new account, contact or opening balance opens in a panel at the side of the screen. After you save it, you stay on the same screen. A new account or contact shows in the list.

At the top left of each detail page is a back link, for example Records. Click it to go back to the previous page. Akaun keeps the filters and the position in the list. If you opened the page from a different page, the link shows Back. If you opened the page from a shared address, the link opens the list.
Read Records to learn how Akaun keeps your books.
Use this page after you install Akaun. Akaun has no first-run wizard. You sign in with a default user and then change its password.
documents.s: Sign in for the first time

documents.t: When the server starts for the first time, Akaun makes these items: A user with the username admin and the password akaun-admin. The server also writes this password to its log. Four groups: Administrators, Bookkeeper, Data Entry and Reviewer. The admin user is in Administrators, which is a superuser group. A starter set of accounts, for example Cash, Bank and Accounts Payable. See Prepare your book.
documents.s: What Akaun makes on the first start

documents.t: Open the address of your Akaun server in a web browser. In Username, type admin. In Password, type akaun-admin. Click Sign in. The Records screen opens. The sidebar shows your name and the screens that you can use. caution Change the default password immediately. All Akaun installations start with the same password. Until you change it, any person who can open the address can sign in as a superuser.

At the bottom of the sidebar, click the user menu button (three dots) next to your name. Click Profile. Click the Security tab. In Current password, type akaun-admin. In New password, type a new password. Use 8 characters or more. In Confirm new password, type the new password again. Click Change password. Akaun shows Password changed. Akaun also disconnects all the connected apps of this user. caution Do not change the username admin. If no user has the username admin, Akaun makes a new admin user with the password akaun-admin at the next start of the server. You can change the name and email of the admin user. On the Profile tab, change Display name or Email, and then click Save changes. The default email is admin@localhost.

Invalid username or password: the username or the password is wrong. The username is case-sensitive. Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minute(s).: Akaun allows 5 failed attempts for one username from one computer. The 15 minutes start at the first failed attempt. Wait for the time that the message gives, and then try again. The number of minutes in the message can be smaller. Forbidden (CSRF origin check failed): the address in the browser is not the same as the ORIGIN setting of the server. See Install Akaun. A correct sign-in sets the count of failed attempts to zero. A restart of the server also sets it to zero.

The Forgot? button and the Ask your admin for access button on the sign-in page do not work at this time. Ask a superuser to give you a new password: The superuser clicks Users & Groups in the sidebar. On the Users tab, the superuser clicks your row. In Reset password, the superuser types a new password. The superuser clicks Save changes. Then sign in with the new password, and change it on your Profile page. caution Only a superuser can give a user a new password. If the only superuser forgets the password, nobody can reset it in Akaun. Add a second trusted user to the Administrators group. See Users and groups.
A sign-in stays valid for 30 days in that browser. To end it earlier, open the user menu and click Sign out. The Keep me signed in box on the sign-in page does not change the 30 days at this time.
Prepare your book.
Use this page to install Akaun on your own server. You do this one time, before the first user signs in. After the installation, each user opens Akaun in a web browser.

You need: A computer or server that stays on. All users connect to it. The address that the users will type in the browser, for example http://192.168.1.20:6969 or https://books.example.com. For a Docker installation: Docker with Docker Compose. For an installation from the source code: Bun version 1.2 or later, and Git. You can install Akaun in two ways. Docker is the easier way, and we recommend it.

Make a new folder for Akaun on the server. In this folder, make a file with the name docker-compose.yml. Copy this text into the file: services: akaun: image: ghcr.io/getakaun/akaun:latest restart: unless-stopped ports: - 6969:6969 volumes: - ./data:/app/data environment: - ORIGIN=http://localhost:6969 - TZ=Etc/UTC - PUID=1000 - PGID=1000 - BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=21M Change ORIGIN to the address that users will type and TZ to your business timezone, for example Asia/Kuala_Lumpur. On Linux, type id -u and id -g to find your user ID and group ID. Change the values of PUID and PGID to these two numbers. In the same folder, type this command: docker compose up -d Open the address in a web browser. The sign-in page opens and shows Welcome back. Docker makes a data folder next to docker-compose.yml. This folder holds all the data of your book. To add more settings, add more lines under environment:. The environment variables table gives each setting.

Get the code: git clone https://github.com/getakaun/akaun.git Go into the folder of the code: cd akaun Install the packages: bun install If bun install stops with an error about argon2, install Python 3, make and a C++ compiler. Then do step 3 again. Build the application: bun run build Copy the file .env.example to a new file with the name .env. Open .env and add a line for ORIGIN, for example ORIGIN=http://192.168.1.20:3000. Change the other values in .env if necessary. The environment variables table gives each setting. In the same folder, start the server: bun server.js Open the address in a web browser. The server shows Listening on http://0.0.0.0:3000. The sign-in page opens and shows Welcome back. Always start bun server.js from the folder of the code. Akaun finds its database changes in this folder. With the default settings, Akaun also keeps the data in the data folder here. The command stops when you close the terminal. Use the service manager of your server, for example systemd, to start Akaun again after each restart of the server.

Bun reads the .env file in the folder of the code. For Docker, put each setting under environment: in docker-compose.yml. Variable Default What it does ORIGIN (none) The full address that the users type, for example https://books.example.com. Akaun refuses sign-in and saves from a different address. TZ Etc/UTC in Docker and .env.example; otherwise the host timezone Business timezone for server-side document dates and overdue/expiry checks. Use an IANA name such as Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and restart after changing it. Browser date defaults use each device's timezone. PORT 3000 (Docker: 6969) The network port that Akaun listens on. HOST 0.0.0.0 The network address that Akaun listens on. 0.0.0.0 accepts connections on all network addresses. DATABASE_PATH ./data/akaun.db (Docker: /app/data/akaun.db) The location of the database file. A relative path starts at the folder where you start the server. STORAGE_PATH ./data/storage (Docker: /app/data/storage) The folder for the files that users upload, for example receipts and attachments. BODY_SIZE_LIMIT 21M in .env.example and in Docker The largest request that the server accepts. Akaun accepts files up to 15 MB. An AI assistant sends a file in a larger, encoded form, so a 15 MB file needs about 21 MB. Do not set a value smaller than 15M; below 21M, assistants cannot attach the largest files. If you remove this setting, the limit is 512 KB and most uploads fail. LOG_LEVEL info in .env.example and in Docker How much the server writes to its log: trace, debug, info, warn or error. A trace log can contain your financial data. Use it only for a short time. SSL_ENABLED false Set to true to serve Akaun over HTTPS without a reverse proxy. SSL_KEY_PATH (none) The path to the private key file. Necessary when SSL_ENABLED is true. SSL_CERT_PATH (none) The path to the certificate file. Necessary when SSL_ENABLED is true. OAUTH_ENABLED false Set to true to let AI assistants connect with OAuth. See Connect AI assistants. PUBLIC_BASE_URL the value of ORIGIN The public address for OAuth. If you set it, it must be the same as ORIGIN. AUTH_ISSUER the public address For OAuth only. If you set it, it must be the public address. MCP_RESOURCE the public address with /mcp For OAuth only. If you set it, it must be the public address with /mcp at the end. PUID, PGID 1000 Docker only. The user ID and group ID that own the data folder. caution Make sure that ORIGIN is the exact address in the browser, with http or https and the port. If the two are different, sign-in fails with Forbidden (CSRF origin check failed). The Docker image sets NODE_ENV=production. Then the browser keeps the sign-in only on an HTTPS address or on localhost. If the users connect over plain HTTP to a different address, use HTTPS.

Akaun keeps all the data of your book in two places: The database: the file at DATABASE_PATH, for example akaun.db. Two more files are next to it: akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm. The three files are one database. The -wal file can contain changes that are not in akaun.db yet. The storage folder: the folder at STORAGE_PATH. It holds the receipts, attachments, uploaded documents and the company logo. With the default settings, both are in one data folder. caution The data folder is the books of your business. Do not delete it, move it or edit it while Akaun runs. Always copy the three database files and the storage folder together. A copy of only akaun.db can lose recent records. Make a backup copy before you install a new version. See Backups and upgrades.

When a new version starts for the first time, Akaun updates the database by itself. You do not type a command. The server answers GET /health with a short status message. A monitor or a reverse proxy can use it. If you use a reverse proxy, for example nginx, disable buffering for the paths that end in /stream, and give them a long read timeout. Akaun sends live updates on these paths. If the proxy buffers them, other users' changes do not show until a reload. This guide does not cover the desktop app.
Sign in for the first time.

Use this checklist after the first sign-in, before anybody records money. Do the steps in this order. Two settings lock when the first record exists, so do them first. info Sign in as a superuser, for example admin, to do all the steps on this page.

1. Choose the main currency 2. Add the company details 3. Choose the document numbers 4. Check the accounts 5. Enter the opening balances 6. Check the default accounts 7. Add the users 8. Connect an AI provider

The main currency is the currency of your book. All amounts show in it. The default is USD. caution The Currency field locks when the first record, quotation or invoice exists. A starting balance is also a record. After the lock, you cannot change the main currency. In the sidebar, click Settings. Click the General tab. In Currency, choose the currency of your business. Click Save. If the field shows a lock icon, the currency is already locked. See Foreign currency.

Akaun shows these details on printed quotations and invoices. In Settings, click the Company tab. Under Logo, click Upload and choose a JPEG or PNG image of 5 MB or smaller. Optional: under Letterhead, click Upload and choose a JPEG or PNG image of your letterhead. In Company Name, type the name of the business. In Address, type the address. In Registration No., type the registration number of the business. Click Save. The Templates tab controls printed documents. To print the letterhead in place of the company name, set Header to Letterhead there. See Settings reference.

Akaun gives a number to each expense, income, payment, quotation and invoice. One format applies to all of them. The default format is {PREFIX}{YYYY}{MM}{DD}-{SEQ:3}, for example EX20261009-001. The format uses these tokens: Token Meaning {PREFIX} A fixed code for each type: EX for an expense, IN for an income, CL for a payment, QT for a quotation, IV for an invoice. You cannot change these codes. {YYYY} The year with four digits. {YY} The year with two digits. {MM} The month. {DD} The day. {SEQ} The sequence number. {SEQ:3} gives three digits, for example 001. The format must have one {SEQ} token. The sequence starts again at 1 when the date part of the number changes. With {DD}, it starts again each day. With only {YYYY}, it starts again each year. Without a date token, it never starts again. caution The format locks when the first record, quotation or invoice exists. After the lock, you cannot change it. In Settings, click the General tab. Under Numbering, click a token to add it to the format. You can also drag a token. Type other characters, for example a dash, directly in the format. Look at the Preview line under the format. Click Save under Numbering.

Akaun starts with these accounts: Type Accounts Asset 1000 Cash, 1100 Bank, 1200 Accounts Receivable, 1300 Inventory, 1400 Marketplace Clearing Liability 2000 Accounts Payable, 2100 Loans Equity 3000 Owner's Equity, 3100 Retained Earnings Revenue 4000 Product Sales, 4100 Other Revenue Expense 5000 Cost of Goods Sold, 5100 Advertising, 5200 Packaging, 5300 Shipping, 5400 Software, 5500 Utilities, 5900 Other Expenses An Expense or Revenue account is a category. Add the categories that your business needs. Add one account for each bank account, card and cash box of the business. In the sidebar, click Accounts. Click a tab to see one type, or click All. Click Add account. In Name, type the name, for example the name of your bank. In Account type, choose the type. You cannot change the type after the account has records. Leave Code empty. Akaun gives the lowest free number for the type. If Sub-type shows, choose the line of the report, for example Bank. Click Create account. The new account shows in the list. To change the name of a starter account, click the account, change Name, and click Save changes. On their account pages, Marketplace Clearing and Loans show Unclassified until you choose a sub-type. See Accounts and categories.

The opening balance is the money in an account on the day that you start to use Akaun. Enter it for each account that holds money, for example Cash and each bank account. In the sidebar, click Accounts. Click the account. On the right side of the account page, under Opening balance, click the card. In As at date, choose the first day of your books in Akaun. In Amount, type the balance on that day, in the main currency. If the account was overdrawn, type a negative amount. Click Save opening balance. The card shows the amount and the date. Akaun saves an Opening balance record. The other side of the record goes to the Opening balances default account, which is Owner's Equity at the start. Each account has one opening balance only. If you save a new one, it replaces the old one. If you save zero, Akaun removes the opening balance. You cannot change an opening balance after a payment settles it or a bank line matches it.

Akaun uses default accounts for the automatic side of some records. The starter values work for most businesses. Default What Akaun uses it for Starter account Accounts receivable An invoice that you send, and a payment from a customer. Accounts Receivable Accounts payable An expense that a different person pays for the business. Accounts Payable Opening balances The other side of each opening balance. Owner's Equity Sales revenue An invoice that does not choose a different revenue account. Product Sales Uncategorised expense An imported expense with no matching expense account. Other Expenses Default transaction account The account that new expenses and income use first. Bank Uncategorised income An imported income with no matching revenue account. Other Revenue In Settings, click the Ledger tab. Under Default accounts, choose an account for each default. Click Save defaults. info The Ledger tab shows only for a user with the View permission on Reports. To change a default account, the user needs the Change permission on Accounts and the Manage permission on Settings.
Add a user for each person who works in the book. Put each user in a group. Do not use the admin user for everyday work. See Users and groups and Permissions explained.
Auto Import uses AI to read receipts, bills and statements. It does not work until you add an AI provider. You can skip this step if you enter all records by hand. See Connect an AI provider.
Your book has the correct currency, company details, accounts and opening balances. You can start to record money. See Record an expense or income.
This page gives short answers to questions that bookkeepers and administrators often ask. Each answer has a link to the full page.

Your books stay on your own server. Akaun sends the text of each document that you give to Auto Import or to bank reconciliation to the AI provider that you choose. With the text, it sends the names of your categories. Akaun also gets exchange rates and text-recognition files from the internet, but these requests contain no data from your books. If you connect an AI assistant, the assistant can read the areas that you allow. See Connect an AI provider and Connect AI assistants.

Yes. Each user signs in from a web browser, with their own username. Most screens show the changes of other users immediately, without a reload. Each user sees and changes only what their groups allow. See Find your way around and Users and groups.
documents.s: Can several people work in Akaun at the same time?

documents.t: One Akaun installation keeps one book. For a second business, install a second copy of Akaun. Give it its own data folder, its own port and its own ORIGIN. See Install Akaun.
documents.s: Can I keep the books of two businesses?

documents.t: Yes. Your book has one main currency, and all reports use it. You can record an expense, an income, a quotation or an invoice in a foreign currency. Akaun changes the amount into the main currency with the exchange rate of the date. See Foreign currency.
documents.s: Can I use more than one currency?

documents.t: No. The Currency setting locks when the first record, quotation or invoice exists. A starting balance is also a record. Choose the main currency before you add any data. See Prepare your book.
documents.s: Can I change the main currency later?

documents.t: You do not mark a bill as paid. You record a payment, and Akaun calculates the status from the payments. On the Records screen, find the Outstanding payables panel. Click Pay all payables, or click View details and then Record a payment for one contact. See Bills you pay later and Outstanding, partially paid and paid.
documents.s: How do I mark a bill as paid?

documents.t: Open the invoice and click Record payment. Akaun opens a receipt with the invoice already ticked. Do not save a new income for this money, because the invoice already counts the sale. See Getting paid.
documents.s: How do I record a payment from a customer?

documents.t: No. Mark as sent on an invoice records that the customer owes the amount. It does not send an email. Click Print to get a PDF, and give the PDF to the customer yourself. See Invoices.
documents.s: Does Akaun send invoices by email?

documents.t: No. Akaun removes a deleted record permanently, and no screen can restore it. The only way to recover it is to restore a backup, and a restore also removes all later changes. See Change, delete or undo a record and Backups and upgrades.
Akaun has no backup button. Stop Akaun, then copy the database files and the storage folder to a different computer. With Docker, copy the full data folder. See Backups and upgrades.
documents.s: How do I make a backup of my books?

documents.t: No. Invoices and quotations have no tax field, and Akaun makes no tax report. The account sub-types Tax receivable and Tax payable put tax balances on the correct lines of the Balance Sheet. See Accounts and categories.
documents.s: Does Akaun calculate tax, for example GST, SST or VAT?

documents.t: Not directly. Each report has Export, which downloads a CSV file. Open the file in a spreadsheet program to print it. Quotations and invoices have Print, which makes a PDF. See Profit & Loss.

Not directly. Akaun cannot read a backup file or an export of the chart of accounts of a different program. Auto Import can read records from an Excel workbook (.xlsx) or a CSV file. Add the accounts and the opening balances by hand. See Import spreadsheets and Prepare your book.
documents.s: Can I import my data from a different accounting program?

documents.t: Akaun is a web application. It works in the browser of a phone, with a bottom bar in place of the sidebar. You can add Akaun to the home screen of the phone, and it then opens in its own window. Akaun does not work offline. See Find your way around and Scan with your phone.

Each record moves money out of one account and into a different account. The category is the account on one line of the record. For example, an expense of software paid from the bank has Software on the Debit line and Bank on the Credit line. Thus a category is an account of the type Expense or Revenue. See Accounts and categories and How a record moves money.
documents.s: Why is a category an account?

documents.t: Troubleshooting Glossary

This page gives the meaning of each term in Akaun and in this guide. It is also the approved term list: the guide uses each word here with one meaning only. Terms in bold are labels that you see on the screen.

An account is a place where money is kept, owed or counted. Each record moves money out of one account and into a different account. You find all accounts on the Accounts screen. See Accounts and categories.

The account code is the number of an account, for example 1000 for Cash. The field is Code. Each type has its own range, for example 1000–1999 for an asset. If you leave the field empty when you add an account, Akaun gives the lowest free number in the range. See Accounts and categories.

The account statement is the Records list filtered to one account. It shows the Opening balance before the first row, a running balance on each row and the Closing balance after the last row. On the account page, the Account ledger card opens it. It shows the running balance only when the list is in date order. A date range is permitted, but no other filter. See Find records.

Each account has one of five types: Asset, Liability, Equity, Revenue or Expense. The type tells the reports where the account goes. The Accounts screen has an All tab and one tab for each type. Asset: a thing that the business owns, for example cash, a bank balance or receivables. Liability: money that the business owes to a different person or business. Equity: the value that the owners or partners have in the business. Revenue: money that the business earns. A Revenue account is an income category. Expense: money that the business spends. An Expense account is an expense category. See Accounts and categories.

Accounts Payable is the account for the payables: the money that the business owes. Akaun uses it for a bill that is not paid yet, or for an expense that a different person paid for the business. Each amount on it belongs to one contact. See Bills you pay later.

Accounts Receivable is the account for the receivables: the money that customers owe to the business. Akaun uses it when you send an invoice. Each amount on it belongs to one contact. This account is an Asset. See Getting paid.

Adjustments is an ability in the Records permission area. It lets a user save a record between any two accounts. It also lets a user add more than two lines to a record that is not an everyday split. Of the groups that Akaun creates, only Administrators has it, because that group is a superuser group. When you select the whole Records area, Akaun does not select Adjustments. Give it only to a person that you trust with the books. See Permissions explained.
An AI assistant is a chat program, for example Claude or ChatGPT, that can connect to Akaun. It can read your books. If you give it the access, it can also change them. See Connect AI assistants.

An AI provider is a service that reads your documents for Auto Import. You add a provider in Settings, on the Intelligence tab, under Providers. Auto Import cannot read a receipt or a PDF until you add one provider. See Connect an AI provider.
Allocated to is a section on the page of a payment. It shows each record that the payment pays, and the amount for each record. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.

An allocation is the part of a payment that goes against one record. On the payment form, the Allocation section shows each outstanding record and the amount that the payment puts against it. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.
An API token was the secret key of older versions of Akaun. The upgrade revoked all API tokens, and they do not work any more. Use a personal access token. See Troubleshooting.
An attachment is a file that you add to a record, for example a receipt or a bill. The Attachments section is on the record page. See Attach receipts.

Auto Import is the screen where Akaun reads receipts, invoices, statements and spreadsheets. Akaun reads each file, usually with AI, and prepares one or more records. You check each record before Akaun saves it. See Import receipts.
Auto-detect is the default choice under Read as. Akaun uses an enabled import profile that fits the document. If no profile fits, Akaun reads the document as one record. See Import profiles.

The balance of an account is the total of all money into it and out of it. The balance of a contact is the amount that they owe you (a receivable), or that you owe them (a payable). Akaun calculates each balance from the records. You cannot type a balance. See Contacts and their balances.
Balance Sheet is a report. It shows the assets, liabilities and equity of the business on one date. See Balance Sheet.
Bank reconciliation is a check of an account against the statement from the bank. You match each statement line to a record in Akaun. Open an account, then click Reconcile. See Bank reconciliation.

The book is the full set of accounts, records and contacts for one business. One Akaun installation keeps one book. The Ledger tab in Settings has the Ledger integrity check, which makes sure that each record is in balance. See Prepare your book.

Cash and cash equivalents is the money that the business can use now. In Akaun, these are the Asset accounts with the sub-type Cash, Bank, Wallet or Prepaid/debit card. The guide also calls such an account a cash or bank account. Equipment, inventory and prepayments are assets, but they are not cash. On a record, the cash or bank account is the line that money came out of or went into. Earlier versions of this guide used the term "money account". See Accounts and categories and Cash Flow Statement.
Cash Flow Statement is a report. It shows where cash came from and what it went on, for a period. See Cash Flow Statement.

A category tells what the money was for or where it came from. In Akaun, a category is an account of the type Expense or Revenue. The Records screen has a Category filter. There is no separate screen for categories. See Accounts and categories.
The old name of Reconciled. See Reconciled.

A connected app is a program, for example an AI assistant, that you let read or change your Akaun data. You find the list on your profile, on the Connected apps tab. Click Revoke access to disconnect an app immediately. See Connect AI assistants.
A contact is a person or a business that you work with. A record can name one contact. Akaun uses the contact to show who owes money and to whom. See Contacts.
A role tells how you work with a contact. The roles are Customer, Supplier, Employee and Partner. A contact can have more than one role, or no role. See Contacts.

The control total is the total that a document gives, for example the total on a statement. Akaun compares it with the total of the items that it read. If the two totals are different, you can still confirm the items. See Documents with many records.

The Dashboard is a summary screen. It shows how the business performs in a period that you choose. It shows the revenue, the net profit, the cash balance and the receivables, each with its change against a comparison period. It also shows the trends of the last 12 months, the balance sheet, the payables, the sales pipeline, the action items and the recent transactions. See Dashboard.

Each record has a Debit line and a Credit line. A debit is the account that value goes into. A credit is the account that value goes out of. The debits of a record are always equal to its credits. See How a record moves money.

The Default transaction account is the account that new income and expenses use first. You choose it in Settings, on the Ledger tab, under Default accounts. On the Accounts screen, this account shows Default account. The General tab also has a Default payment account row, but at this time a change there is not kept. See Settings reference.
The entity type tells if a contact is an Individual or a Business. See Contacts.

The exchange rate changes an amount in a foreign currency into the main currency. The field shows the two currencies, for example Rate (1 USD = ? MYR). Akaun tries to find the rate for the date of the record. If it finds no rate, you type the rate. See Foreign currency.
Expense is a record of money that the business spends. Expense is also an account type. An Expense account is an expense category. See Record an expense or income.
Filtered total is the sum of the amounts on the list after your filters. It shows above the table on the Records, Quotations and Invoices lists. See Find records.

A foreign currency is any currency that is not the main currency. Click + Foreign currency on the record form to record an amount in a different currency. Invoices and quotations can also use a foreign currency. See Foreign currency.

A group is a set of users with the same permissions. Akaun creates four groups: Administrators, Bookkeeper, Data Entry and Reviewer. A user gets all the permissions of all their groups. At each start of the server, Akaun puts a user with no group into Administrators. See Users and groups.
History is the section on a record, account or contact page that shows the audit trail. The audit trail is a list of each change: who made it and when. See Edit, delete or undo a record.

An import profile is a saved way to read one kind of document, for example a marketplace statement. You make profiles in Settings, on the Intelligence tab. An enabled profile shows under Read as. See Import profiles.

An inactive account is an account that you do not use now. Click Deactivate on the account page to make it inactive, and Reactivate to use it again. Akaun keeps its history. You cannot deactivate an account that Settings names as a default account. The Accounts screen hides inactive accounts. To see them, click Show inactive (2). This button shows only when an inactive account exists. See Accounts and categories.
Income is a record of money that the business earns. The account for the income is a Revenue account. See Record an expense or income.

An inflow is money that comes into an account. An outflow is money that goes out of it. In an import profile, the direction column tells which rows are inflows and which rows are outflows. See Import profiles.

An invoice is a document that asks a customer to pay. When you click Mark as sent, the customer owes the amount and Akaun adds an Invoice record to the books. A sent invoice cannot be deleted, but you can cancel it. See Invoices.

An invoice shows one of these statuses: Draft: you can change or delete the invoice. The customer owes nothing yet. Sent: the customer owes the amount. Partially paid: payments cover some of the amount, but not all of it. Paid: payments cover the full amount. Akaun calculates this from the payments. Cancelled: the invoice does not count. It keeps its number, and its amount is not in the books. Overdue: the invoice is sent, the due date is in the past, and the invoice is not fully paid. See Invoices.
An item is one record that Auto Import read from a document. A receipt gives one item. A statement or a spreadsheet can give many items. You confirm or skip each item. See Review and confirm.

Journal entry is a record that is not an expense, income, transfer, payment, opening balance or invoice. Usually it is a correction. To save a journal entry, you need the Adjustments permission. See How a record moves money.

A line is one part of a record. Each record has two lines: the Debit line and the Credit line. On an expense or an income, click + Add a line to add more lines, for example to split a bill across categories. A user with Adjustments can add lines to any record. The debits of a record are always equal to its credits. See Split across categories.

A record is locked when a payment settles part or all of it, or a bank line matches it. The payment that settles it is locked too. Its amount, date, currency and cash or bank accounts cannot change, and you cannot delete it. The Records list shows a lock icon beside it. You can still change the description, contact, reference, remark and attachments. On an expense or an income, you can also change the category lines. See Locked records.

The main currency is the currency of your book. All amounts show in it. You choose it in Settings, on the General tab, in the Currency field. After the book has a record, an invoice or a quotation, you cannot change it. See Foreign currency.

A match connects a bank statement line to a record in Akaun. One line can match more than one record. Use Suggested Match accepts the match that Akaun found. Click Save or Save & Next to keep it. Save 3 exact matches saves many matches at one time. See Bank reconciliation.
The old name of a cash or bank account. See Cash and cash equivalents.
The old name of Unreconciled. See Unreconciled.

Opening balance is a record of the money in an account on the day that you start to use Akaun. On the account page, the card is Opening balance. The other side of the record goes to the account that Settings › Ledger names for Opening balances. By default, this is Owner's Equity. See Prepare your book.

Outstanding shows that nobody paid any of the amount of a record yet. One line of the record is on Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable. The record names the contact who owes the money, or who is owed it. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.
Outstanding payables is a panel on the Records screen. It shows each contact that the business owes money to, and the amount. From it, you can pay one contact or all of them. See Bills you pay later.

Paid shows that the full amount of a record is paid. A record that moves money directly from an account is paid when you save it. An outstanding record becomes paid when payments cover it. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.
Partially paid shows that payments cover some of the amount of a record, but not all of it. Earlier versions showed Part paid. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.

Partners' Equity is a report. It shows the contributions, share of profit and drawings of each partner. At this time, no control links a partner to an Equity account. So in a new book, contributions and drawings show 0.00. See Partners' Equity.
Payables are the money that the business owes to suppliers and other contacts. They are on Accounts Payable. See Accounts payable.

Payment is a record that pays an amount that the business owes. One payment can pay one record or many records. On the Records screen, open the Outstanding payables panel. Click Record a payment to pay one contact, or Pay all payables to pay all of them. On the payment form, Payee is the contact that you pay. Payer is the contact that pays you. See Bills you pay later.

Payments applied is a section on the page of an expense or an income. It shows each payment that paid part or all of the record. Reverse allocation removes one payment from it. See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.

A permission lets a user do one thing in one area of Akaun. Each area, for example Records, Contacts or Invoices, has a list of abilities. Most areas have View, Add, Change and Delete. Some areas have more, for example Send and Void on Invoices. Reports are view only. On the screens, you choose a level for each area: None, View, Edit, Full or Custom. See Permissions explained.

A personal access token is a secret key that lets a program, for example an AI assistant, use Akaun as you. You make it on your profile, on the Access tokens tab. Only you can make a token for yourself. Each token has a name, an expiry date or no expiry, and its own permissions. A token never does more than what you may hand on to tokens and apps. Akaun shows the full token one time only. It starts with akp_. Keep the token secret. See Your profile and Connect AI assistants.

Possible duplicate shows that an imported item looks like a record that is already in Akaun. On a receipt card, the tag shows Duplicate with a percentage and the reasons. Check the item before you click Import anyway. See Review and confirm.
Profit & Loss is a report. It shows the revenue and the expenses for a period, and the difference between them. See Profit & Loss.

A quotation is a document that offers a price to a customer before the work. A quotation does not change the books. Click Convert on a sent or accepted quotation to make a draft invoice from it. See Quotations.

A quotation shows one of these statuses: Draft, Sent, Accepted, Declined, Converted or Expired. You change the status with the buttons on the quotation page. Converted shows that you made an invoice from the quotation. Expired shows that the expiry date of a draft or sent quotation is in the past. See Quotations.
Read as is the choice on Auto Import that tells Akaun how to read the next file. The choices are Auto-detect, Single record, Multiple records and each enabled import profile. See Import receipts.

Receivables are the money that customers and other contacts owe to the business. They are on Accounts Receivable. The money that the business owes is the payables. See Accounts receivable and Accounts payable.

A record is reconciled when bank statement lines match its full amount. The Records list shows Unreconciled beside each record that is not reconciled yet. It shows no label for a reconciled record. Click Unreconciled above the list to show only the records that are not reconciled. Reconciled and paid are two different things. A record can be paid and unreconciled. See Bank reconciliation.
A record is one event with money, for example an expense, an income or a transfer. It tells where the money came from and where it went. All records show on the one Records screen. See Records.

The kind tells what a record is. The kinds are Expense, Income, Transfer, Payment, Opening balance, Invoice and Journal entry. You do not choose the kind. Akaun finds it from the accounts on the record. See Records.

Reverse allocation is the tooltip of the undo icon that removes a settlement. The record is then Outstanding or Partially paid again. If the record is locked only because of this settlement, it becomes unlocked. See Edit, delete or undo a record.

A running balance is the balance after each line of a statement. The account statement on the Records screen shows one on each row. Some spreadsheets also have a balance column. Akaun then checks that each row's balance follows from the row before it. A break shows that a row is missing or changed. See Find records and Documents with many records.
A section is one part of an import profile, for example the inflows and the outflows of a wallet report. Each section tells Akaun what kind of record its lines become. See Import profiles.
To settle a record is to pay what is owed on it. A payment settles one or more records. To remove a settlement, click its undo icon (Reverse allocation). See Outstanding, partially paid and paid.

Source account is a field on an imported item. On an expense, it is the account that the money came out of. On an income, it is the income category. The other field is Target account. For a single receipt, the Source account of an expense is Accounts Payable by default. The Target account of an income is Accounts Receivable by default. The record is then Outstanding until a payment settles it. See Review and confirm.
See Opening balance.
A statement is the list of lines that your bank sends for one account. You upload it with Upload Statement on the reconciliation screen of the account. See Bank reconciliation.

The sub-type puts an account into a line of a report, for example Bank, Credit card or Operating expense. Each account type except Equity has sub-types. An account with no sub-type shows Unclassified. An Asset or Liability account must have a sub-type. A Revenue or Expense account can have no sub-type. The reports then count it as operating. See Accounts and categories.

A superuser can do all actions in all areas. The permissions of the groups do not limit a superuser. Only a superuser can open Users & Groups. The Administrators group is a superuser group. See Users and groups.
The old name of Reverse allocation. See Reverse allocation.
Transfer is a record that moves money between two of your own accounts, for example from the bank to cash. A transfer is not an expense or an income. See Move money between accounts.

Unclassified shows that an account has no sub-type. The reports cannot put an unclassified Asset or Liability account into a group. The Balance Sheet shows it in an Unclassified group. The Cash Flow Statement shows its amount on the line Unclassified movements. Give the account a sub-type on its account page. See Accounts and categories.
Unreconciled shows that bank statement lines do not yet match the full amount of a record. See Reconciled.

Use the word in the right column. The left column shows words that other software uses, and words that do not match a feature of Akaun. Do not write Write entry (for a normal record) record journal (for a normal record) record vendor, party, client contact (or the role: customer, supplier). On the payment form, Payee or Payer. ledger account, GL account account chart of accounts screen Accounts screen categories screen, Categories tab (no such screen; see Category) into, out of (for a line) Debit, Credit (see Debit and credit) post (a new record) save a record leg, split line line unpaid, owed (as a status) Outstanding part paid, partly paid Partially paid cleared, not cleared (for one record) Reconciled, Unreconciled owed to you, you owe receivable, payable money account cash or bank account starting balance opening balance needs review, not yet classified Unclassified base currency, home currency main currency claim, reimbursement claim (not a feature) set up prepare, configure fill in, fill out complete look up find log in, log on sign in role (for a group of users) group admin rights superuser key (for API access), API token personal access token void cancel

Use this page when Akaun does not do what you expect. Each heading is a message or a problem that you see. Below each heading, the page tells you the cause and what to do. The links go to the full procedures.
The username or the password is wrong. The username is case-sensitive. For example, Admin is not the same as admin.
Type the username again. Check the capital letters. Type the password again. If you forgot the password, see You forgot your password. See Sign in for the first time.
Akaun allows 5 attempts for one username from one computer in 15 minutes. The 15 minutes start at the first attempt. While this message shows, Akaun refuses the correct password too.
Wait for the number of minutes in the message. Sign in again with the correct password. A correct sign-in sets the count to zero. A restart of the server also sets it to zero.
The Forgot? button on the sign-in page does not work at this time. Akaun cannot send a password by email.

Ask a superuser to give you a new password. The superuser opens Users & Groups. On the Users tab, the superuser clicks your row. The superuser types a new password in Reset password. The superuser clicks Save changes. Sign in with the new password. Change the password on the Security tab of your profile. See Users and groups and Your profile.
No screen in Akaun can give a new password to the last superuser. Only a superuser can open Users & Groups.

If a different user is in Administrators, that user can reset the password. See You forgot your password. If no other superuser exists, Akaun has no tested way to recover access at this time. The source code has a script, scripts/create-admin.ts, that adds a new user. Nobody has tested it outside the application, and it may not run. If you try it, make a backup first. See Backups and upgrades. caution Keep two or more trusted users in Administrators. Then one superuser can always reset the password of the other.

The address in the browser is not the same as the ORIGIN setting of the server. Akaun refuses a sign-in or a save from a different address. The scheme (http or https), the name and the port must all agree.

The administrator of the server does these steps. Find the exact address that the users type, for example https://books.example.com. Set ORIGIN to this address. Start Akaun again. If users open Akaun with two different addresses, only the address in ORIGIN works. See Install Akaun.
You type the correct username and password, but the sign-in page shows again. No message shows.
documents.s: The sign-in page opens again after you click Sign in

documents.t: The server runs with NODE_ENV=production, and the Docker image sets this value. Then the browser keeps the sign-in only on an HTTPS address or on localhost. Over plain HTTP to a different address, the browser does not keep the sign-in.
Serve Akaun over HTTPS. Use a reverse proxy, or set SSL_ENABLED, SSL_KEY_PATH and SSL_CERT_PATH. Set ORIGIN to the HTTPS address. Start Akaun again. See Install Akaun.

The user has no View permission on Records. After the sign-in, Akaun tries Records, then the Dashboard, and then opens Settings. For example, a user in the Data Entry group only sees this. This group can add records, but it has no View permission on Records. If the user also has no View permission on Settings, Akaun opens their Profile instead. These users see this: A user in no group, and with no extra permissions. A user in a group with no permissions, for example a group that stops access. A user who opens Akaun from the home screen of a phone can also see Settings. The home-screen icon opens the Dashboard, and only Administrators have View on Dashboard. Click Records in the menu to continue.

A superuser puts the user in a group with the correct permissions. See Users and groups. caution Do not leave a user in no group. At the next start of the server, Akaun puts each user with no group into Administrators. That user then becomes a superuser. To stop the access of a user, see Stop the access of a user.

Usually the user does not have a permission. Some items also show only in some conditions. What is missing Why A screen in the sidebar You have no View permission on that area. New record You have no Add permission on Records. Delete or Reverse allocation You have no Delete permission on Records. No group except Administrators gives it. Users & Groups Only a superuser sees it. Settings in the sidebar You have no View permission on Settings. The fields and the Save buttons in Settings You have no Manage permission on Settings. A note at the top of the page tells this. The groups that Akaun makes do not give it. Reconcile on an account page You have no View permission on Reconciliation, or the account is inactive. The Ledger tab in Settings You have no View permission on Reports. Quotations and Invoices You have no View permission on these areas. A group that you make has none until you choose a level for them in the group. Convert on a quotation The status is not Sent or Accepted. Or you do not have Convert on Quotations and Add on Invoices. Cancel invoice The invoice is a draft, or a payment is recorded against it. Or you do not have Void on Invoices and Change on Records. Record payment on an invoice The invoice is a draft, is cancelled or is fully paid. Or you have no Add permission on Records. The Partners' Equity tab No contact has the Partner role. Pay all payables The business owes money to one contact only, or to none. Or you have no Add permission on Records. Payment account on a payment The book has only one cash or bank account. Akaun uses that account. Contact on a new record You have no contacts yet. Scan on Auto Import The screen is wide. Scan shows only on a narrow screen, such as a phone.

Ask a superuser for the permission. See Permissions explained. Confirm & import and Skip show for all users, but Akaun refuses them without the Confirm permission on Auto Import. Read again shows only with the Upload and Change permissions on Auto Import. The Bookkeeper group does not give Change or Confirm on Auto Import. See Users and groups.
The full message is "API tokens were replaced by personal access tokens. Create one under Profile → Access tokens." A program or an AI assistant gets this message, and it cannot connect.
documents.s: API tokens were replaced by personal access tokens

documents.t: The program uses an API token of an older version of Akaun. The upgrade revoked all these tokens. They do not work any more.

Open your profile, and click the Access tokens tab. Make a new token with only the permissions that the program needs. See Make a token. In the program, replace the old token with the new token. The new token starts with akp_. If Permissions offers nothing, ask your administrator to let your group hand on permissions to tokens and apps. See What members may hand on.
A note above the form gives the reason. For example: "This record is settled by a payment. Reverse the settlement before you change its amount, date or account."
documents.s: The amount, the date or the account of a record is read only

documents.t: The record is locked. A payment settles it, a bank statement line matches it, or both. A locked record keeps its amount, date, currency and cash or bank account. You also cannot delete it.

Remove each thing that locks the record. If a payment settles the record, open the record. In Payments applied, click the undo arrow on the payment. Its tooltip is Reverse allocation. If a bank statement line matches the record, open the account page and click Reconcile. Click the row of the statement. Click the record in the list. Remove the tick from each statement line. Click Save & Next or Save. Change the record. Reverse allocation needs the Delete permission on Records. Save & Next and Save need the Match permission on Reconciliation. You can still change the description, contact, reference, remark and attachments of a locked record. On a locked expense or income, you can also change the categories. On a payment record, Akaun saves only the description, the reference and the remark. The other fields can look editable, but Akaun does not save them. See Locked records and Change, delete or undo a record.

The record is an Invoice record. Akaun made it when you clicked Mark as sent on an invoice. The record belongs to the invoice, so its record page is read only. If you try to delete it, Akaun shows "This record was created by issuing an invoice. Cancel the invoice instead."

In the rail of the record page, click the Invoice card. The invoice opens. To change the due date, the reference, the notes or the terms, click Edit. If the customer, the date, the currency or a line is wrong, click Cancel invoice. Then make a new invoice. See Change a sent invoice and Cancel an invoice.
The full message is "A payment has been recorded against this invoice. Remove that payment first, then cancel the invoice."
documents.s: A payment has been recorded against this invoice

documents.t: A payment settles the invoice, in full or in part. While a payment settles an invoice, Cancel invoice does not show. The message shows when someone recorded the payment after you opened the invoice page.

On the invoice page, in the Payments card, click the payment. Beside the allocation to the invoice, click Reverse allocation. Open the invoice again, and click Cancel invoice. Reverse allocation needs the Delete permission on Records. See Cancel an invoice.

Without the Adjustments permission, each line of the record form offers cash or bank accounts and categories only. Accounts Payable, a loan account and a Credit card account are not in the list. The same cause can make a line of an imported bill show Select account.

To record a bill that you pay later, import it with Auto Import. See Bills you pay later. For a different record on these accounts, ask a user with the Adjustments permission. No group that Akaun makes gives Adjustments. See Permissions explained.
The full message is: "These two accounts need the Adjustments ability. Ask an administrator for it, or choose an everyday account on each line."
documents.s: These two accounts need the Adjustments ability

documents.t: The accounts on the record do not make an everyday record, such as an expense, an income or a transfer. Akaun saves such a record as a Journal entry, and a journal entry needs Adjustments.

Check the account on the Debit line and on the Credit line. Choose a cash or bank account on one line and a category on the other line. If the record must use these accounts, ask a user with Adjustments to save it. See How a record moves money.
The full message is, for example: "Debits and credits do not balance. Difference: 5.00." This message shows on the save bar. The top of Journal entry shows a figure with apart.
documents.s: Debits and credits do not balance

documents.t: The record has more than two lines. The total of the category lines is not the same as the amount of the record.

Find the difference at the top of Journal entry. Correct the amount on one category line. Make sure that the top of Journal entry shows Balanced. Click Save record on a new record, or Save changes on a saved record. tip On the last line, click the arrow button in the amount box. Its tooltip shows the difference, for example Use the remaining 5.00. The button puts the difference on that line. See Split a record across categories.

Akaun does not save the record until you correct each problem. When the record has more than two lines, these messages show on the save bar: Message What to do "Select an account for each line." Choose an account on each line. "A line amount cannot be zero." Type an amount that is not zero on each line, or remove the line. "Select the contact for this receivable or payable." Choose a Contact. A record on Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable must name a contact. After you click save, these messages can show above the form: Message What to do "Select the contact for this receivable or payable." Choose a Contact. "Money cannot move from an account to itself. Choose two different accounts." Choose a different account on one line. See Record an expense or income.
documents.s: The record does not save, and a message shows

documents.t: Auto Import has no enabled AI provider. Each file that needs AI then fails with this message.

Add a provider, or enable a provider. See Connect an AI provider. On Auto Import, click Read again on each failed row. In the dialog, click Read again. Read again needs the Upload and Change permissions on Auto Import. A spreadsheet that a Table rows import profile reads does not need a provider. See Import profiles.

Akaun reads a limited number of files at the same time. Other files wait as Queued. A long document takes more time, because Akaun reads it in parts. Rate limit in Settings also makes Akaun wait between two calls to the provider.

Wait. The row shows the progress, for example Reading part 3 of 25…. To read more files at the same time, increase Parallel tasks. See Connect an AI provider. If the server stops during a reading, the reading starts again from the start at the next start of the server.
Akaun or the AI provider could not read the file. The row shows the reason. Usually the photo is not clear, the provider is not available, or no provider is enabled.

Read the reason on the row. Correct the cause. For example, enable a provider, or choose a different model. Click Read again. In the dialog, choose how Akaun reads the file. Click Read again. If the photo is not clear, upload a clearer photo. Then click Discard on the failed row. Retry uploads the same file again. It shows only in the browser tab where you uploaded the file, before a reload. Read again needs the Add and Change permissions on Auto Import. See Import receipts and documents.

A message shows below the drop area on Auto Import. It starts with the name of the file. Message What to do "This is an old Excel file (.xls), which cannot be read." Open the file in Excel. Save it as .xlsx or .csv. Upload it again. "This workbook is protected with a password, so it cannot be read." Remove the password in Excel. Save the file. Upload it again. "File too large. Maximum size is 15 MB." Make the file smaller, or divide it into two files. "Upload failed" The server refused the file before Akaun could read it. See the next paragraph. If a file of less than 15 MB shows "Upload failed", the server can have a lower upload limit. The BODY_SIZE_LIMIT setting controls this limit. The Docker image sets it to 21M. Without it, the server refuses files larger than about 0.5 MB. The administrator sets BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=21M and starts Akaun again. See Install Akaun. For more messages about spreadsheets, see Import spreadsheets.
documents.s: Akaun refuses a file when you upload it

documents.t: Akaun compares each item with the records in the book. It looks for the same file, the same reference, a similar amount, a near date, a similar contact, a similar file name and similar text. A new bill can look like an old bill. For example, a monthly bill from one supplier often has the same amount and the same layout.

Read the reasons on the tag, for example "Duplicate · 85% · reference · amount". Find the existing record on the Records screen, and compare it with the item. If the item is new, click Import anyway. If the item is a second copy, click Skip. See Review and confirm.
On Auto Import, the message is "Enter the rate manually to convert to MYR." The last word is your main currency.
documents.s: No rate found for that date — enter it yourself.

documents.t: Akaun gets exchange rates from a free public rate service on the internet. It finds no rate in these cases: The server cannot connect to the internet. The rate service does not have the currency. It has about 30 main currencies only. The rate service is not available at this time.
Find the rate on your bank statement or on the bill. Type the rate in the Rate (1 USD = ? MYR) field. The field shows your currencies. Save the record, or confirm the item. See Foreign currency.
The statement shows the status Failed. The statement drawer shows the reason after "Statement extraction failed:".
Akaun could not read the lines of the statement. The usual reasons are these: The file has too little text that Akaun can read. No AI provider is enabled. The AI provider found no lines in the text.

Correct the cause. For example, enable an AI provider. Open the statement drawer. Click Retry Extraction. If the retry fails again, click Delete in the drawer to delete the statement. Upload a clearer file, for example the PDF from the website of the bank. Retry Extraction needs the Add permission on Reconciliation. Delete needs the Delete permission on Reconciliation. One message tells you to add the lines by hand. At this time, no screen can add a statement line. See Bank reconciliation.

The match screen lists the records that have a line on an account with a statement. These are the usual reasons that a record does not show: The record uses a different account. For example, you recorded the expense on Cash and not on Bank. The record does not exist yet in Akaun. The search box or the date filter on the match screen hides it.

Clear the search box and the date filter. Open the record. Check the cash or bank account of the record. If the account is wrong, change it to the account of the statement. If the record does not exist, add it on the Records screen. If you cannot change the account, the record is locked. See The amount, the date or the account of a record is read only. The list can also show records from other accounts that have a statement. These records can never match this statement. If a statement line does not show under Compatible Statement Lines, check its Direction. See Bank reconciliation.
This message shows on the Balance sheet card of the Dashboard, with the difference. The Action items list also shows Balance sheet does not balance.
documents.s: The balance sheet does not balance

documents.t: The data of one or more records is damaged. The total of the lines of each record must be zero. The screens do not normally cause this.

Click Settings. Click the Ledger tab. Under Ledger integrity check, click Check now. Make a note of each record number and difference in the result. Report the problem. See Report a problem. The Ledger tab shows only with the View permission on Reports. The check only reads the book. It changes nothing. Do not send reports to anybody until the check shows The ledger is in balance. All records and the trial balance agree. See Dashboard.
