No control in Akaun connects an Equity account to a partner. The Partner role does not make these accounts. Thus Contributions and Drawings are 0.00 in a new book. Only Share of profit has a value.
At this time, the report cannot show contributions and drawings for a new book. Use the Records screen, filtered by the Equity account, to see this money. See Find records and Partners' Equity.

On the page of a saved record, Akaun does not show a message when an upload fails. These are the usual causes: The file is not a PDF, JPEG or PNG file. The file is larger than 15 MB. The server has a lower upload limit, because BODY_SIZE_LIMIT is not set. You have no Change permission on Records. Add shows, but the upload fails.

Check the type and the size of the file. Check that you have the Change permission on Records. If a small PDF also fails, ask the administrator to set BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=21M. Add the file again. See Attach receipts and documents and Install Akaun.

If this page does not solve the problem, report it to the people who make Akaun. Open an issue on the Akaun project on GitHub. Give this information: The version of Akaun. It shows under your name at the bottom of the sidebar, for example v0.1.7. The steps that you did, and the message that you saw. Copy the message exactly. The lines of the server log at the time of the problem. With Docker, type docker compose logs akaun. caution The server log can contain names, amounts and other data from your books. Remove this data before you send the log.

The Balance Sheet shows the assets, the liabilities and the equity of the business on one date. Assets: what the business owns. Liabilities: what the business owes. Equity: what the owners have in the business. info You need the View permission on Reports. Reports are view only. See Permissions explained.
Click Reports. Click the Balance Sheet tab. In As at, choose the date. At the start, As at is today. The report includes all records up to and including this date.

The top of the report shows Total assets, as at the date. Below it, Akaun compares this figure with the liabilities plus the equity. If the two are equal, Akaun tells you that the balance sheet is in balance. The report has three sections: Assets: the Asset accounts. Liabilities: the Liability accounts. Equity: the Equity accounts and Current earnings. Each section ends with Total. The report shows only the accounts with a balance on the date. If a section has no accounts, it shows "Nothing at this date." Current earnings is the revenue minus the expenses, from the first record up to the date. It is not an account. You cannot click it.

Assets and Liabilities each have up to three groups. Each group ends with Subtotal. Current: money and things that the business uses or pays within about one year. Non-current: things that the business keeps for longer, and loans for longer. Unclassified: accounts without a sub-type. The sub-type of the account selects the group. For example, Fixed asset goes into Non-current, and Credit card goes into Current. Give each account in Unclassified a sub-type. See Accounts and categories.
documents.s: How the sub-type groups the lines

documents.t: Assets, liabilities and equity all show as positive numbers. A negative number shows an unusual balance. For example, a bank account with an overdraft shows a negative asset.

On 31 March, the business has 8,000.00 in Bank and 2,000.00 in Accounts Receivable. It owes 3,000.00 on Accounts Payable. The owner gave 5,000.00 to the business at the start. Since then, the business made a profit of 2,000.00. Section Group Line Amount Assets Current Bank 8,000.00 Assets Current Accounts Receivable 2,000.00 Assets Current Subtotal 10,000.00 Assets Total 10,000.00 Liabilities Current Accounts Payable 3,000.00 Liabilities Current Subtotal 3,000.00 Liabilities Total 3,000.00 Equity Owner's Equity 5,000.00 Equity Current earnings 2,000.00 Equity Total 7,000.00 The assets are 10,000.00. The liabilities plus the equity are 3,000.00 + 7,000.00 = 10,000.00.

The assets must always be equal to the liabilities plus the equity. If they are not equal, the balance sheet is out of balance. The Total assets figure shows in red. The text below it gives the difference. A warning also shows below the report. This tells you that the data of a record is damaged. Click Settings. Click the Ledger tab. In Ledger integrity check, click Check now. Give the result to your administrator. Do not send this report to anybody until the check is good.
documents.s: If the balance sheet is out of balance

documents.t: To open a line, you also need the View permission on Accounts and on Records. Click the name of a line, for example Bank. On the account page, click View account ledger. The Records screen shows all records of the account, with a running balance. It shows all dates, not only the dates up to As at. See Find records.
documents.s: See the records behind a line

documents.t: Click Export. Akaun downloads a CSV file, for example balance-sheet-2026-03-31.csv. The file has the columns "Section", "Account" and "Amount". The sections are "Assets", "Liabilities" and "Equity", each with a "Total" row. Below the table, the file gives the date and the notes of the report. The Current, Non-current and Unclassified groups are not in the file.

You cannot print a report at this time. Use Export and print the CSV file. The address of the report includes the date. Copy the address to send the same report to a different user. On the Accounts screen and the account page, Liability and Equity balances show with a minus sign. The report shows them as positive numbers. If Akaun converted your book from an earlier version, a note shows below the report. Invoices from before the conversion are not in the figures.
Dashboard Profit & Loss Accounts and categories How a record moves money

The Cash Flow Statement tells you where your cash came from and what the business spent it on in a period. A business can make a profit and still have less cash. This report shows why. info You need the View permission on Reports. Reports are view only. See Permissions explained.

Click Reports. Click the Cash Flow Statement tab. In From, choose the first day of the period. In To, choose the last day of the period. At the start, the period is from 1 January of this year to today.

Cash means cash and cash equivalents: the money in Asset accounts with the sub-type Cash, Bank, Wallet or Prepaid/debit card. A transfer between two of these accounts does not change the cash. Thus it is not on this report. See Accounts and categories.

The top of the report shows Net change in cash for the period. Below it, Akaun shows the cash at the start of the period plus the change. The result must be equal to the cash at the end. If From is after To, Akaun uses the To date for both. The report has three sections. Each section ends with Total. Operating activities: the cash from the daily work of the business. Investing activities: the cash for things that the business keeps. Financing activities: the cash from loans and from the owners.

Each line is the total of a group of accounts. The account type and the sub-type select the line: Section Line Accounts Operating activities Revenue Revenue accounts Operating activities Change in receivables Accounts receivable Operating activities Change in inventory Inventory Operating activities Change in other current assets Other current Asset sub-types, for example Prepayments and deposits Operating activities Trade payables and other liabilities Current Liability sub-types, for example Accounts payable and Credit card Operating activities Cost of goods sold Cost of goods sold Operating activities Operating expenses Operating expense, or no sub-type Operating activities Other operating expenses Other expense Investing activities Capital expenditure Fixed asset, Intangible asset, Other non-current asset Financing activities Long-term debt Long-term loan, Other non-current liability Financing activities Owner's equity Equity accounts The report shows only the lines with an amount in the period. If a section is empty, it shows "Nothing this period."
documents.s: How the sub-type selects the line

documents.t: An Asset or Liability account without a sub-type does not go into a section. Its amount shows in a separate Unclassified box, on the line Unclassified movements. A note below the report also tells you about it. To give an account a sub-type, you need the Change permission on Accounts. Click Accounts. Click the account. Make sure that the top of the account page shows Unclassified. In Sub-type, choose the correct sub-type. Click Save changes. The report then puts the amount on the correct line. In a new book, Marketplace Clearing and Loans have no sub-type.
A positive number is cash that the business received. A negative number is cash that the business paid. For example, the expenses that you paid show as a negative number.

In April, the business had 5,000.00 in Bank at the start. Customers paid 9,000.00 for sales. The business paid 3,000.00 for expenses and 2,000.00 for a laptop. The owner gave 1,000.00 more to the business. Section Line Amount Operating activities Revenue 9,000.00 Operating activities Operating expenses -3,000.00 Operating activities Total 6,000.00 Investing activities Capital expenditure -2,000.00 Investing activities Total -2,000.00 Financing activities Owner's equity 1,000.00 Financing activities Total 1,000.00 The Net change in cash is 6,000.00 - 2,000.00 + 1,000.00 = 5,000.00. The cash at the end is 5,000.00 + 5,000.00 = 10,000.00.

If the change does not explain the cash at the end, the Net change in cash figure shows in red. The text below it gives the difference. A warning also shows below the report. This tells you that the data of a record is damaged. Click Settings. Click the Ledger tab. In Ledger integrity check, click Check now. Give the result to your administrator.
documents.s: If the figures do not agree

documents.t: You cannot click a line on this report, because each line can include many accounts. To see the records, use the Records screen. Filter it by one cash account and by the dates of the report. See Find records.
documents.s: See the records behind a line

documents.t: Click Export. Akaun downloads a CSV file, for example cash-flow-2026-01-01-to-2026-03-31.csv. The file has the columns "Section", "Account" and "Amount". It has the lines and the "Total" of each section. If an amount is unclassified, the file has an "Unclassified movements" row. At the end, it has three "Cash" rows: "Opening cash and cash equivalents", "Net change in cash" and "Closing cash and cash equivalents". Below the table, the file gives the period and the notes of the report.

You cannot print a report at this time. Use Export and print the CSV file. The address of the report includes the dates. Copy the address to send the same report to a different user. If Akaun converted your book from an earlier version, a note can show below the report. It shows when the period starts before the conversion. Invoices from before that day are not in the figures.
Dashboard Profit & Loss Accounts and categories Move money between accounts

The Dashboard shows how the business performs. It shows the headline figures, the trends of the last 12 months, the receivables and payables, the sales pipeline and the tasks to do. Use it for a fast check. For the full figures, open the reports. Each figure comes from the same calculation as its report. When you open the report from a figure, the report shows the same number. info You need the View permission on Dashboard. Without it, the Dashboard item does not show in the sidebar, and Akaun opens Settings instead. Of the groups that Akaun creates, only Administrators has this permission. See Permissions explained. Each section also needs the permission of its source screen. See Who sees which section.

Click Dashboard. The top of the screen shows Welcome back and your username. If the book has no records, the Dashboard shows No records yet and no figures. Click Add a record or Import a document to start.

The period bar is at the top of the screen. It has four periods: Period Dates This month From the first day of this month to today. This quarter From the first day of this quarter to today. Year to date From 1 January to today. Last 12 months From the first day of the month 11 months ago to today. Every period ends today. At the start, the Dashboard shows This month.

Each headline figure shows its change against a comparison period. Next to compared with, choose one of these: Previous period: the same number of days at the start of the previous month or quarter. For example, 1–16 October compares with 1–16 September. Same period last year: the same dates one year earlier. Year to date and Last 12 months always compare with the same period last year. For these periods, the two choices give the same dates. The dates of the comparison period show in brackets after the selector. The period and the comparison are in the address of the page. If you send the link to a colleague, the colleague sees the same period.

Each figure shows these items: A change chip: the change against the comparison period, as a percentage. Green shows good news. Red shows bad news. The chip shows new when the comparison period has no value. A small chart (a sparkline) of the last 12 months. Click a figure to open its report with the same dates.
Revenue is the total income for the period. It opens Profit & Loss.

Net profit is the revenue minus the expenses for the period. If the expenses are more than the revenue, the label changes to Net loss and the figure shows in red. Below the figure, Akaun shows the Net margin: the net profit as a percentage of the revenue. The margin of the comparison period shows after it, for example (was 12%). If the period has no revenue, the line shows No revenue in this period. It opens Profit & Loss.

Cash balance is the total of the cash and cash equivalents today. These are the accounts with the sub-type Cash, Bank, Wallet or Prepaid/debit card. The change chip compares the balance today with the balance at the end of the comparison period. When the cash falls, the figure also shows the Runway. The runway is the number of months that the cash lasts at the recent rate: Runway = cash balance today ÷ average fall in cash for each month Akaun calculates the average fall over the last three complete months. The runway shows only when the cash balance is more than zero and the cash fell over these three months. If the runway is less than six months, it shows in amber. It opens Cash Flow Statement.

Receivables is the total that customers owe you today. Below the figure, Akaun shows the overdue part in red. The bar shows the ageing of the total: Not yet due, 1–30 days, 31–60 days, 61–90 days and Over 90 days overdue. This figure has no change chip and no sparkline. Akaun keeps no dated history of the ageing. It opens the Contacts screen. If you do not have the View permission on Contacts, it opens the Records screen with the unpaid records. See Contacts.

This chart shows the revenue and the expenses for each of the last 12 months, as bars. A line shows the net profit of each month. The months before the selected period show lighter. Click a month to open the Profit & Loss for that month.
This chart shows the cash and cash equivalents at the end of each of the last 12 months. The last point is today. Click Cash flow to open the Cash Flow Statement for the period.

This card shows the Assets, the Liabilities and the Equity today. The assets are always equal to the liabilities plus the equity. Click Open report to open the Balance Sheet for today. The Balance sheet card does not change with the period. It always shows today.

Sometimes the card shows The balance sheet does not balance and the difference. This tells you that a record in the book is not correct. The lines of each record must add to zero. This message shows only when the data is damaged. Do not use the figures until you correct the problem. Click Settings. Click the Ledger tab. In Ledger integrity check, click Check now. Read the result. The Ledger tab shows only if you have the View permission on Reports. The check only reads the book. It changes nothing. If a record is wrong, the result gives its record number and the difference. Give this result to your administrator.
documents.s: If the balance sheet does not balance

documents.t: Profit and cash are not the same. This panel shows, step by step, how the net profit of the period becomes the change in cash. Each figure comes from the Cash Flow Statement and Profit & Loss of the period. Step What it shows Net profit Revenue minus expenses. Working capital changes Changes in receivables, payables and inventory. For example, a sale that the customer has not paid increases the profit, but not the cash. Operating cash flow Cash from operating activities. This is the net profit plus the working capital changes. Capital expenditure Purchases of equipment and other fixed assets. Free cash flow Operating cash flow minus capital expenditure. Financing activities Loans, owner contributions and drawings. Unclassified accounts Cash movements on accounts that have no sub-type. This step shows only when there are such movements. Net change in cash Closing cash minus opening cash.

You buy a machine for 10,000.00 and pay from the bank: The bank balance falls by 10,000.00. Capital expenditure shows −10,000.00, and the Net change in cash falls by the same amount. The machine is an asset, not an expense. The Net profit does not change. Akaun does not calculate depreciation. To put the cost of the machine into the profit over its life, record the depreciation with a journal entry. A journal entry needs the Adjustments permission. See How a record moves money. If the panel shows The cash flow statement does not reconcile, open the Cash Flow Statement to find the cause.

These two lists show the largest expense accounts and revenue accounts for the period. Each list shows the six largest accounts. The other accounts are added together in one Other line. Thus the list adds up to the total of the Profit & Loss. Each line shows these items: The amount. The percentage of the total. A change chip against the comparison period. For an expense, a fall shows green. Click a line to open the Records screen. It shows the records of that account for the same dates. The Other line does not open. Click Open report to open the Profit & Loss.

These two panels show the amounts that are outstanding today: Receivables: the amounts that customers owe you. Payables: the amounts that you owe to suppliers. Each panel shows these items: The outstanding balance. The overdue amount and the number of overdue items. The ageing bar: Not yet due, 1–30 days, 31–60 days, 61–90 days and Over 90 days. The three contacts with the largest balances. Click a contact to open its page. Click Contacts to open the Contacts screen. These links show only if you have the View permission on Contacts. The figures are the same as on the Contacts screen. See Contacts and balances.

This panel shows the sales that are not complete: Figure What it shows Open quotations The value and number of open quotations. The note shows how many expire this week. Accepted quotations Accepted quotations that you did not convert to an invoice yet. Invoiced sales The value and number of invoices sent in the period. Outstanding invoices Invoices that customers did not pay completely. The note shows how many are overdue, and their value. Click a figure to open the Quotations or Invoices screen. See Quotations and Invoices.

This list shows the tasks that keep the books correct. Click an item to open the screen where you do the task. Item Opens Balance sheet does not balance The Balance Sheet for today. Imported documents to review Auto Import. See Review and confirm. Overdue invoices Invoices. Unpaid bills Records, with the unpaid expenses. See Bills you pay later. Unreconciled bank lines The reconciliation screen of the account. If more than one account has such lines, it opens Accounts. See Bank reconciliation. Accounts without a sub-type Accounts. Give each account a sub-type, so that the reports classify it. See Accounts and categories. An item shows only when it has something to do. If no item shows, the list shows No open items. The books are up to date.

This list shows the eight newest records of all types: expenses, income, payments, transfers, opening balances, invoices and journal entries. Each row shows the description, the record type, the contact and the date. A plus sign shows that cash came in. A minus sign shows that cash went out. No sign shows that the cash did not change, for example a transfer between two of your own accounts. Click a row to open the record. Click View all to open the Records screen.

You need the View permission on Dashboard to open the page. Each section also needs the View permission of the screen that its figures come from: Section Permission Revenue, Net profit and Cash balance figures, Revenue and expenses, Cash balance chart, Balance sheet, Net profit to cash flow, Top expenses, Top revenue View on Reports Receivables figure, Receivables and Payables panels, Recent transactions View on Records Open quotations and Accepted quotations View on Quotations Invoiced sales and Outstanding invoices View on Invoices Each action item View on the screen that the item opens If you do not have a permission, Akaun does not show the section. It does not show the section empty.

The Dashboard updates by itself when somebody changes a record, a payment, an account, an invoice, a quotation or an import. "Today" is the date on the server. The Dashboard has no export. Use the reports to export the figures.
Profit & Loss Balance Sheet Cash Flow Statement Contacts Settings reference

Partners' Equity tells you what each partner has in the business for a period. It shows what each partner contributed, their share of the profit and what they withdrew. info You need the View permission on Reports. Reports are view only. See Permissions explained.
The Partners' Equity tab shows only when at least one contact has the Partner role. To give a contact this role, open the contact, select Partner under Roles and save the contact. See Contacts.

Click Reports. Click the Partners' Equity tab. In From, choose the first day of the period. In To, choose the last day of the period. At the start, the period is from 1 January of this year to today. If From is after To, Akaun uses the To date for both.

The report has one row for each partner, in the order of their names. It has these columns: Partner: the name of the contact. Contributions: the money that the partner put into the business in the period. Share of profit: the part of the Net profit of the period for this partner. Drawings: the money that the partner withdrew from the business in the period. Closing balance: Contributions plus Share of profit minus Drawings. If there are two or more partners, the last row is All partners. It gives the total of each column. A partner with no records in the period still has a row. On a phone, each partner shows as a small block with the same figures.

Akaun takes the Net profit of the same period from Profit & Loss. It divides it equally between all partners. Akaun cannot record a different share for each partner. A note below the report tells you this. If the business made a loss, each partner gets an equal part of the loss. The Share of profit is then a negative number.
documents.s: How Akaun calculates the share of profit

documents.t: Contributions and Drawings come from Equity accounts that belong to one partner. Money that a partner gives to the business is a contribution. Money that a partner takes from it is a drawing. At this time, Akaun has no control that connects an Equity account to a partner. The Partner role does not make these accounts. Thus, in a new book, Contributions and Drawings show 0.00. A book from an earlier version of Akaun can still have such accounts.
Contributions and a profit show as positive numbers. Drawings is also a positive number, and Akaun subtracts it.

Two partners, Aina and Ben, share a business. In the year, the business made a net profit of 10,000.00. Partner Contributions Share of profit Drawings Closing balance Aina 0.00 5,000.00 0.00 5,000.00 Ben 0.00 5,000.00 0.00 5,000.00 All partners 0.00 10,000.00 0.00 10,000.00 Each partner gets half of the profit, because Akaun divides it equally.

Click Export. Akaun downloads a CSV file, for example partners-equity-2026-01-01-to-2026-12-31.csv. The file has the columns "Partner", "Contributions", "Share of profit", "Drawings" and "Closing balance". It has one row for each partner. It has no "All partners" row. Below the table, the file gives the period and the notes of the report.

You cannot print a report at this time. Use Export and print the CSV file. Closing balance covers only the period of the report. It does not include earlier periods. You cannot click a row on this report. If you remove the Partner role from all contacts, the tab does not show.
Profit & Loss Balance Sheet Contacts Accounts and categories

Profit & Loss tells you if the business made a profit or a loss in a period. It shows the revenue, the expenses and the difference between them. info You need the View permission on Reports. Reports are view only. See Permissions explained.

Click Reports. Click the Profit & Loss tab. In From, choose the first day of the period. In To, choose the last day of the period. Profit & Loss is the first tab. At the start, the period is from 1 January of this year to today. If From is after To, Akaun uses the To date for both.

The top of the report shows Net profit or Net loss. This is the total revenue minus the total expenses for the period. Below it, the report has these sections: Revenue: one line for each Revenue account, and Total revenue. Expenses: one line for each Expense account, and Total expenses. Summary: Gross profit and Operating income. The report shows only the accounts with an amount in the period. If a section is empty, it shows "Nothing in this period." A transfer between two of your own accounts is not on this report. A purchase of equipment is also not on this report, because equipment stays on the Balance Sheet. See Accounts and categories.

The sub-type of each account puts its amount into the Summary: Gross profit is the Operating revenue minus the Cost of goods sold. Operating income is the Gross profit minus the Operating expense accounts. Other revenue and Other expense accounts are not in these two subtotals. They are in the Net profit. A Revenue or Expense account without a sub-type counts as operating. See Accounts and categories.
documents.s: How the summary uses the sub-type

documents.t: Revenue and expenses both show as positive numbers. A negative number on a line is unusual. For example, a refund that is more than the sales of the period gives a negative revenue line.

In March, the business sold goods for 10,000.00. The goods cost 4,000.00. Advertising cost 1,000.00. The bank paid interest of 100.00 into the Other Revenue account. Line Amount Product Sales 10,000.00 Other Revenue 100.00 Total revenue 10,100.00 Cost of Goods Sold 4,000.00 Advertising 1,000.00 Total expenses 5,000.00 Gross profit 6,000.00 Operating income 5,000.00 Net profit 5,100.00 The interest is in Net profit, but not in Operating income.

To open a line, you also need the View permission on Accounts and on Records. Click the name of a line, for example Advertising. On the account page, click View account ledger. The Records screen shows all records of the account, with a running balance. It shows all dates, not only the period of the report. Choose the dates again in the Date filter. See Find records.
documents.s: See the records behind a line

documents.t: Click Export. Akaun downloads a CSV file, for example profit-and-loss-2026-01-01-to-2026-03-31.csv. The file has the columns "Section", "Account" and "Amount". It has the revenue lines, the expense lines, the totals and the "Net profit (loss)" row. Below the table, the file gives the period and the notes of the report. The Summary subtotals are not in the file.

You cannot print a report at this time. Use Export and print the CSV file. The address of the report includes the dates. Copy the address to send the same report to a different user. If Akaun converted your book from an earlier version, a note can show below the report. It shows when the period starts before the conversion. Invoices from before that day are not in the figures. On the account page, the balance of a Revenue account shows with a minus sign. The report shows it as a positive number.
Dashboard Balance Sheet Accounts and categories Record an expense or income

When you mark an invoice as sent, the customer owes the amount. This amount is a receivable. This page tells how to record the payment from the customer, what Paid means for an invoice, and where you see your receivables. Read Outstanding, partially paid and paid first. It tells what Outstanding, Partially paid and Paid mean. info To record a payment, you need the Add permission on records and the View permission on invoices.

Record the payment from the invoice that it pays. Record payment shows on a sent invoice that is not fully paid. Open the invoice. Click Record payment. The Record a receipt page opens. Payer shows the customer of the invoice. In Allocation, the invoice is ticked, with its outstanding amount. Amount shows the same amount. If the customer paid only part of the invoice, type the amount that they paid in the box beside the invoice. In Description, type a description, for example "Payment for IV20261009-001". In Date, choose the date of the payment. In Receipt account, choose the account that got the money, for example the bank account. If you have only one cash or bank account, Receipt account does not show. Akaun uses that account. Optional: in Reference, type a reference, for example the number of the bank transfer. In the bar at the bottom of the page, click Save. Akaun saves a Payment record and opens the invoice again. The Payments card shows the payment. The Settled card shows the new Amount received and Outstanding amounts. The status of the invoice changes to Partially paid or Paid. The amount of a payment is always in the main currency. For an invoice in a foreign currency, see An invoice in a foreign currency. If the customer paid more than the invoice, the extra amount stays on the payment. It is not put against any record.
documents.s: Record a payment from an invoice

documents.t: A sent invoice puts its amount on Accounts Receivable, with the customer as the contact. A payment from the customer settles this amount, in full or in part. Akaun calculates the status from the payments. You cannot mark an invoice as paid. Status on the Invoices list What it shows Sent No payment covers the invoice yet. Partially paid Payments cover some of the amount, but not all of it. Paid Payments cover the full amount. Overdue The due date is in the past and payments do not cover the full amount.
documents.s: What Paid means for an invoice

documents.t: A receivable is an amount that a customer owes to the business. You can see your receivables in these places.
After you mark the invoice as sent, the Settled card in the rail shows Amount received and Outstanding. If a payment settles part or all of the invoice, the Payments card shows it.
The Sent tab shows the sent invoices that are not fully paid. The Outstanding card shows the amount that customers still owe on them. The Overdue card shows the amount that is overdue.

The Balance column shows Receivable beside each contact that owes money to the business. Under the title, Receivables shows the total. You see these amounts only if you have the View permission on records.
The amount at the top shows Receivable. This amount also needs the View permission on records.
The Outstanding tab and the Partially paid tab show each Invoice record that is not fully paid. See Contacts and their balances and Find records.
caution Do not save a new income for money that pays an invoice. The invoice already counts the sale. A second income counts the sale two times, and the invoice stays outstanding.
documents.s: Do not record the payment as an income

documents.t: The Records screen has no link to record a payment from a customer. Start from the invoice. The Outstanding payables panel on the Records screen shows only the payables of the business. It does not show receivables. To remove a payment from an invoice, open the payment from the Payments card. Then click Reverse allocation beside the allocation. See Edit, delete or undo a record. A paid invoice prints with Amount paid and the date of the last payment. See Invoices. If you change the Accounts receivable default account in Settings, a payment cannot settle an invoice that you sent before the change.
Invoices Outstanding, partially paid and paid Contacts and their balances Bills you pay later

An invoice asks a customer to pay. You write the invoice as a draft, and then you mark it as sent. When you mark it as sent, the customer owes the amount. Akaun posts the amount to Accounts receivable. info To make an invoice, you need the Add permission on invoices. To change an invoice, you need Change. To mark it as sent, you need Send on invoices and Add on records. To cancel it, you need Void on invoices and Change on records. To cancel and reissue it, you also need Add on invoices. To delete a draft, you need Delete. To record a payment from the invoice page, you need Add on records.

Open Invoices to see all invoices. Each row shows the customer, the invoice number, the status, the date, the due date and the amount. The tabs above the list filter it: All: all invoices. Draft: invoices that you did not mark as sent yet. Sent: sent invoices that are not fully paid. Paid: sent invoices that payments cover in full. Cancelled: invoices that do not count. Overdue: sent invoices with a due date in the past that are not fully paid. Each tab shows the number of invoices in it. The Status column shows Draft, Sent, Partially paid, Paid, Overdue or Cancelled. Akaun calculates Partially paid, Paid and Overdue from the payments and the due date. When you record a payment, the status on the list changes at once. Above the list, four cards show totals in the main currency: Outstanding: the unpaid amount on the sent invoices. Overdue: the amount that is still outstanding on overdue invoices. Paid: the amount paid on the paid invoices. All recorded: the total of all invoices, including drafts. Cancelled invoices are not in this total. To find an invoice, use these controls: Date: choose a From date and a To date. The list shows invoices with an issue date in that range. The search box (Search IV#, customer, ref…): type a word. Akaun finds it in the invoice number, the customer name, the reference, the notes, the terms and the line items. Clear: removes the filters and the search, and shows the All tab again. It shows only when a filter is on. Filtered total shows the total of the rows on the list.

On the Invoices screen, click New invoice. The New invoice page opens. Issue date shows today. Due date shows a date that comes from Settings. See Default terms. Optional: to change the due date, click a button below Due date: None, On receipt, 7d, 14d, 30d or 60d. Or choose a date in Due date. None removes the due date. On receipt sets the due date to the issue date. 30d sets the due date to 30 days after the issue date. In Customer, type a part of the name of the customer. Choose the customer from the list. The list shows only contacts with the role Customer. If the customer is not in the list, click Create "Acme Sdn Bhd" (with the name that you typed). When you save the invoice, Akaun adds a new contact. The new contact is a Business with the role Customer. If the invoice is in a foreign currency, choose the currency in Currency. A rate field shows, for example Rate (1 USD = ? MYR). Akaun tries to find the rate for the issue date. If it finds no rate, type the rate. Optional: in Reference, type a reference, for example the order number of the customer. In Line items, in Description, type what you sell. In Qty, type the quantity. In Unit Price, type the price of one unit. To add a line, click + Add line. Optional: in Notes, type a note for the customer. Optional: in Terms & conditions, type your terms. In the bar at the bottom of the page, click Create invoice. An invoice must have a customer and at least one line with a description. If one is missing, the bar at the bottom tells you what to add. A line with a price must have a description. The quantity must be more than zero, and the price cannot be less than zero. To remove a line, click the bin icon at the end of the line. An invoice always keeps one line. When you save, Akaun removes each empty line. If you click a button below Due date and then change the issue date, the due date moves with the issue date. Akaun saves the invoice as a draft and opens its page. A draft does not change the ledger. The customer owes nothing yet. You can also make an invoice from a quotation. See Make an invoice from a quotation.

Open the invoice. Click Edit. Change the fields. In the bar at the bottom of the page, click Save changes. Nothing is saved until you click Save changes. To leave without saving, click Cancel. A change of the issue date does not change the exchange rate. If necessary, type a new rate.

Mark as sent shows only on a draft invoice. Mark as sent does not send an email. It records that the customer owes the amount. Give the PDF to the customer yourself. See Print an invoice. caution After you click Mark as sent, the customer owes the amount and Akaun posts it to the ledger. You cannot delete a sent invoice, and you cannot change its customer, issue date, currency or lines. Check them before you mark the invoice as sent. Open the draft invoice. Click Mark as sent. A dialog opens, for example Mark invoice IV20261009-001 as sent?. It tells you that the amount becomes a receivable from the customer, from the issue date. After this you cannot change the customer, date, currency or line items. You can cancel the invoice, but you cannot delete it. Click Mark as sent. If Akaun cannot record the invoice, it records nothing, and the invoice stays a draft. The page shows the reason.

Akaun saves an Invoice record on the Records screen. The record has these values: The date is the issue date of the invoice. The description is "Invoice" and the invoice number. The reference is the invoice number. The amount goes into Accounts Receivable, with the customer as the contact. The other line is the revenue account that Settings › Ledger names for Sales revenue. The invoice page then shows the Settled card in its rail: Amount received: the total of the payments against the invoice. Outstanding: the amount that the customer still owes. The balance of the customer on the Contacts screen increases by the amount. See Contacts and their balances. Change the invoice, not its Invoice record. The page of the record is read only. Its rail has an Invoice card that opens the invoice. See Locked records.

After you mark an invoice as sent, you can still change some of its fields. Open the invoice. Click Edit. A note says that the customer, date, currency and line items are fixed. Change the Due date, the Reference, the Notes or the Terms & conditions. In the bar at the bottom of the page, click Save changes. If the customer, the date, the currency or a line is wrong, or the customer asks for a different item or price, cancel and reissue the invoice. See Cancel and reissue an invoice. Do not revise the quotation that the invoice came from: after the conversion, the invoice is the document that counts.
Record payment shows on a sent invoice that is not fully paid. It opens a receipt for this invoice. See Getting paid.
documents.s: Record a payment from the customer

documents.t: An invoice is overdue when it is sent, its due date is in the past, and it is not fully paid. On the invoice page, OVERDUE shows beside the Due date. On the list, the status of the invoice is Overdue. An invoice without a due date is never overdue. A draft, a paid invoice and a cancelled invoice are never overdue.

Cancel an invoice that you sent by mistake, or that the customer will not pay. Cancel invoice shows on a sent invoice when no payment is recorded against it. If a payment is recorded against the invoice, reverse the allocation first. See Reverse an allocation. caution You cannot undo a cancellation. Akaun removes the Invoice record from the ledger. The amount leaves Accounts receivable and revenue. This also changes the reports for the period of the issue date. Open the invoice. Click Cancel invoice. A dialog opens, for example Cancel invoice IV20261009-001?. Click Cancel invoice. To close the dialog and keep the invoice, click Keep it. The invoice keeps its number, and its status is Cancelled. The Invoice record is no longer on the Records screen. The balance of the customer decreases by the amount. A cancelled invoice cannot be changed or deleted. If the invoice was made from a quotation, the quotation goes back to Accepted. You can convert it again, or mark it declined.

Use Cancel & reissue to correct a sent invoice: a wrong line, a new price, or another item that the customer asks for. Akaun cancels the invoice in the same way as Cancel invoice, and makes a draft copy of it with a new number. Cancel & reissue shows where Cancel invoice shows, when you also have the Add permission on invoices. Open the invoice. Click Cancel & reissue. In the dialog, click Cancel & reissue. Akaun opens the new draft invoice. It has the same customer, currency, rate, line items, reference, notes and terms. Its issue date is today. Its due date is the same number of days after the issue date as on the old invoice. Change the draft, and then mark it as sent. Give the new PDF to the customer. The old invoice is Cancelled, and its PDF prints with VOID. On the old invoice, the Replaced by card opens the new one. On the new invoice, the Replaces card opens the old one. If the invoice was made from a quotation, the quotation stays Converted and now points at the new invoice. If a payment is recorded against the invoice, you cannot cancel or reissue it. Reverse the allocation first.

In an earlier version of Akaun, a cancelled invoice kept its amount in the ledger. Such an invoice shows Reverse posting in place of Cancel invoice. Click it, and then click Reverse posting in the dialog. Akaun removes the Invoice record in the same way.
documents.s: An invoice cancelled in an earlier version

documents.t: Open the invoice. Click Print. A PDF of the invoice opens in a new browser tab. Use the browser to print it or save it. The PDF shows these items: Your company name, address and registration number. These come from Settings, on the Company tab. If Header on the Templates tab is Letterhead, your letterhead prints at the top in place of the company name. The customer under Bill to, with the address, registration number and phone of the contact. The issue date, the due date and the reference. If the invoice is overdue, the due date shows "overdue". The amount that is due, or the date of payment if the invoice is paid. The line items, Subtotal, Total, and Amount due or Amount paid. The notes and the terms and conditions. All amounts on the PDF are in the currency of the invoice. The headings of the price and amount columns name the currency, for example Unit price (USD). Total, Amount due and Amount paid show the currency code after the amount, for example 1,000.00 USD. A draft prints with the word DRAFT across each page. A cancelled invoice prints with the word VOID across each page. A cancelled invoice shows no Amount due. The colour of the PDF comes from Accent color in Settings, on the Templates tab.

You can delete an invoice only while it is a draft. On a sent invoice or a cancelled invoice, Delete is disabled. A cancelled invoice keeps its number. caution You cannot undo a delete. Akaun removes the invoice permanently. Open the draft invoice. Click Delete. In the dialog, click Delete. If you made the invoice from a quotation, the quotation goes back to Accepted. You can then convert it again.

The rail on the right of the invoice page can show these cards: Settled: Amount received and Outstanding. It shows after you mark the invoice as sent. Payments: each payment against the invoice. Click a payment to open its page. Source: the quotation that the invoice was made from. It shows only when the invoice came from a quotation. History: who made each change, and when.

You can mark an invoice in a foreign currency as sent. Akaun records the amount in the main currency. It uses the exchange rate of the invoice. For example, an invoice is 1,000.00 USD and its rate is 4.50. The Invoice record is 4,500.00 MYR. The payment from the customer is in the main currency. If the rate on the day of the payment is different, the payment does not match the invoice exactly. A small amount then stays outstanding on the invoice. See Notes and limits.
documents.s: An invoice in a foreign currency

documents.t: A new invoice gets a due date from Invoice due in (days) in Settings, on the Templates tab. The default is 30 days. If the setting is empty, a new invoice has no due date. You can change the due date on each invoice. See Settings reference.

Akaun has no account for exchange gains and losses. On a foreign-currency invoice, a payment at a different rate can leave a few cents outstanding. Akaun cannot clear this difference. Because a payment is recorded, you also cannot cancel the invoice. Invoices have no tax. The PDF shows no tax line. If you change the Accounts receivable default account in Settings, a payment cannot settle an invoice that you sent before the change. The invoice still shows the correct status.

A quotation offers a price to a customer before you do the work. A quotation does not change the ledger. Use it when a customer asks for a price in writing. When the customer agrees, make an invoice from the quotation. info To make a quotation, you need the Add permission on quotations. To change one or its status, you need Change. To delete one, you need Delete. To revise one, you need Revise and Add on quotations. To make an invoice from a quotation, you need Convert on quotations and Add on invoices.

Open Quotations to see all quotations. Each row shows the customer, the quotation number, the status, the date, the expiry date and the amount. The tabs above the list filter it by status: All Draft Sent Accepted Declined Converted Superseded Expired Each tab shows the number of quotations in it. An expired quotation shows only on the Expired tab. It does not show on the Draft tab or the Sent tab. To find a quotation, use these controls: Date: choose a From date and a To date. The list shows quotations with an issue date in that range. The search box (Search QT#, customer, ref…): type a word. Akaun finds it in the quotation number, the customer name, the reference, the notes, the terms and the line items. Clear: removes the date filter and the search, and shows the All tab again. It shows only when a filter is on. Above the list, four cards show totals in the main currency: Sent, Accepted, This month and All recorded. Below the filters, Filtered total shows the total of the rows on the list.

On the Quotations screen, click New quotation. The New quotation page opens. Issue date shows today. Expiry date shows a date that comes from Settings. See Default terms. Optional: to change the expiry date, click a button below Expiry date: None, 15d, 30d or 60d. Or choose a date in Expiry date. None removes the expiry date. 30d sets the expiry date to 30 days after the issue date. In Customer, type a part of the name of the customer. Choose the customer from the list. The list shows only contacts with the role Customer. If the customer is not in the list, click Create "Acme Sdn Bhd" (with the name that you typed). When you save the quotation, Akaun adds a new contact. The new contact is a Business with the role Customer. If the price is in a foreign currency, choose the currency in Currency. A rate field shows, for example Rate (1 USD = ? MYR). Akaun tries to find the rate for the issue date. If it finds no rate, type the rate. Optional: in Reference, type a reference, for example the order number of the customer. In Line items, in Description, type what you sell. In Qty, type the quantity. In Unit Price, type the price of one unit. Total shows the amount of the line. Subtotal: shows the total of all lines. To add a line, click + Add line. Optional: in Notes, type a note for the customer. Optional: in Terms & conditions, type your terms. In the bar at the bottom of the page, click Create quotation. A quotation must have a customer and at least one line with a description. If one is missing, the bar at the bottom tells you what to add. A line with a price must have a description. The quantity must be more than zero, and the price cannot be less than zero. To remove a line, click the bin icon at the end of the line. A quotation always keeps one line. When you save, Akaun removes each empty line. If you click a button below Expiry date and then change the issue date, the expiry date moves with the issue date.

Akaun saves the quotation and opens its page. Akaun gives the quotation a number, and its status is Draft. The page shows the Line items and the Details. History in the rail shows who made each change, and when.

Open the quotation. Click Edit. Change the fields. In the bar at the bottom of the page, click Save changes. Nothing is saved until you click Save changes. To leave without saving, click Cancel. A change of the issue date does not change the exchange rate. If necessary, type a new rate. After a quotation leaves Draft, the customer has a copy. From then on, you can change only the expiry date, the reference, the notes and the terms and conditions. The customer, the issue date, the currency, the rate and the line items are fixed. To change them, revise the quotation. See Revise a quotation. You cannot change a converted or a superseded quotation. On these, Edit does not show.

The status tells where the quotation is with the customer. The buttons at the top of the quotation page change the status. Each status shows different buttons: Status Buttons Draft Mark as sent, Mark accepted Sent Mark accepted, Mark declined, Revise, Convert Accepted Undo acceptance, Revise, Convert Declined Reopen, Revise Converted none Superseded none Open the quotation. Click the button for the new status. Akaun saves the new status at once. History shows the change. Mark as sent does not send an email. It records that the customer has the quotation. Give the PDF to the customer yourself. See Print a quotation. Undo acceptance and Reopen put the quotation back to Sent. A quotation never goes back to Draft. To change a quotation that the customer has, revise it.
documents.s: Change the status of a quotation

documents.t: Revise a quotation when the customer asks for a different price, other items or other terms before you make the invoice. Akaun keeps the quotation that the customer has, and makes a new version of it. The customer can then see which version replaces which. Revise shows on a quotation with the status Sent, Accepted or Declined. Open the quotation. Click Revise. In the dialog, click Revise. Akaun makes a new draft quotation and opens its page. The new quotation has the same number with -R1 at the end, for example QT20261009-001-R1. A revision of that has -R2, and so on. The new quotation has the same customer, currency, rate, line items, reference, notes and terms. Its issue date is today, and its expiry date comes from Settings. The old quotation gets the status Superseded. It does not change in any other way. On the old quotation, the Replaced by card opens the new one. On the new quotation, the Revision of card opens the old one. Change the new quotation, and then mark it as sent. If you delete the draft revision, the old quotation goes back to Sent. If the customer had accepted or declined it, mark it again.

When the quotation is converted, it is closed. If the customer asks for a change after you make the invoice, do not revise the quotation. Change the invoice: while it is a draft, edit it. After you mark it as sent, cancel and reissue it. See Cancel and reissue an invoice.

Convert shows on a quotation with the status Sent or Accepted. It makes a draft invoice from the quotation. A sent quotation that has expired cannot be converted. Change its expiry date, or revise it, first. Open the quotation. Click Convert. Akaun makes a draft invoice and opens its page. The invoice gets these values from the quotation: The customer. The currency and the exchange rate. The line items. The reference, the notes and the terms and conditions. The issue date of the invoice is today. The due date comes from Invoice due in (days) in Settings. See Default terms. The status of the quotation is then Converted. On the quotation page, the Converted to card in the rail opens the invoice. On the invoice page, the Source card opens the quotation. A draft invoice does not change the ledger. Check it, and then mark it as sent. See Invoices.
documents.s: Make an invoice from a quotation

documents.t: You cannot change, delete or change the status of a converted quotation. To undo a conversion, delete the draft invoice. The quotation then goes back to Accepted, and you can convert it again. You cannot delete the invoice after you mark it as sent. See Delete a draft invoice.

Open the quotation. Click Print. A PDF of the quotation opens in a new browser tab. Use the browser to print it or save it. The PDF shows these items: Your company name, address and registration number. These come from Settings, on the Company tab. If Header on the Templates tab is Letterhead, your letterhead prints at the top in place of the company name. The customer under Bill to, with the address, registration number and phone of the contact. The issue date, Valid until (the expiry date) and the reference. The line items, Subtotal and Total. The notes and the terms and conditions. All amounts on the PDF are in the currency of the quotation. The headings of the price and amount columns name the currency, for example Unit price (USD). Total shows the currency code after the amount, for example 1,000.00 USD. The colour of the PDF comes from Accent color in Settings, on the Templates tab. A superseded quotation prints with the word SUPERSEDED across each page.

On a converted quotation and on a superseded quotation, Delete is disabled. Akaun keeps a superseded quotation, because it is what the customer has. caution You cannot undo a delete. Akaun removes the quotation permanently. Open the quotation. Click Delete. In the dialog, click Delete. Akaun removes the quotation from the list.

Expired shows that the expiry date is in the past. Only a quotation with the status Draft or Sent can expire. Akaun calculates this from today's date. You do not mark a quotation as expired. An expired quotation shows only on the Expired tab. Its page shows the buttons of its status. For example, you can still click Mark accepted or Convert on an expired quotation that was sent. A quotation without an expiry date never expires.

A new quotation gets an expiry date from Quotation valid for (days) in Settings, on the Templates tab. The default is 30 days. If the setting is empty, a new quotation has no expiry date. You can change the expiry date on each quotation. See Settings reference.
A quotation does not change any account or any contact balance.
